title: Helper startup must not block on TCC prompts (StartupStuck)
description: BevelHelper calls AXIsProcessTrustedWithOptions(prompt) + CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess at boot. That stalls Ping until the user dismisses System Settings dialogs; HelperProcessHost times out at 5s and kills/restarts the helper while the dialog is still open — grants attach to a dead process, prompts repeat, taskbar ends Hold StartupStuck after 3 restarts. Fix: never prompt on helper boot; preflight only; prompts stay on IPermissionBroker.RequestAsync / onboarding.
notes: Also: StackViewModel FileSystemWatcher on ~/Downloads blocked UI thread on Files-and-Folders TCC (FSEventStreamCreate→open). Deferred StartWatching to Task.Run.
close_reason: Helper boot no longer TCC-prompts; Downloads stack FileSystemWatcher deferred off UI thread. Verified core+taskbar Ready, no StartupStuck Hold.

title: Remove role=all entirely — split multi-process (launcher) is the ONLY mode
description: User directive (emphatic, repeated): kill role=all forever, remove it from the code; the shell must ONLY run as the split multi-process architecture (launcher supervises core + desktop + taskbar; Explorer per-window). role=all (single process, all shell windows in ONE NSApplication) is the source of the user's daily-usage problems (e.g. clicking a taskbar button raises ALL shell windows because they share one NSApp). Blast radius: 17 refs in src (RoleSelection.cs, CompositionRoot.cs, App.axaml.cs) + 5 in tests (RoleSelectorTests.cs). Remove ShellRole.All from the enum; no-args/unknown => Launcher; collapse every 'role is All or X' to X; fix default params (CompositionRoot role param, App.Role). Program.cs: default the split roles to include Desktop (Core+Desktop+Taskbar) so the desktop the user had in role=all is preserved (keep BEVEL_ENABLE_DESKTOP only as a disable override, or drop the temp gate). Update RoleSelectorTests. Update CLAUDE.md/CODEMAP (dev run 'dotnet run -- --pal=fake' now implies launcher). Full suite must stay green; real-PAL split boot validated on-device.
close_reason: role=all removed entirely; split (launcher -> core + taskbar; Explorer on-demand) is the only mode. Desktop off by default (Start-menu launch = bevel-gdie). Fixed a split-only core crash-loop (ShellCoreServer.StartAsync eager-enumerate raced the async helper connect -> unhandled 'Helper not connected' -> supervisor respawn loop; now retries ~10s + degrades to empty). Real-PAL boot validated: core+taskbar up, helper connects, 0 crash-loops. 819 green. Commit e9ec8ec.

title: Taskbar/Start-menu MVVM redesign: background shell-model service + observable collections + off-thread cached icons (never block UI thread)
description: User-directed architecture fix. Root problem: shell does model work on the UI thread and mutates the view imperatively. Target: (1) background ShellModel service owning ObservableCollection<TaskButton> (windows) + ObservableCollection<Program> (apps) + async icon cache, all updated off the UI thread; (2) TaskbarViewModel/StartMenuViewModel thin projections; (3) view = virtualized ItemsControl + DataTemplate, no hand-rolled UpsertButton/Items.Add; (4) icons render off-thread (Task.Run) cached by (path,size), lazy per visible item; (5) enumerate apps warm at startup off-thread. Decisions: Full MVVM (not incremental); model lives in a dedicated background service (not the view-model). Also fix settings load to not block UI thread. See bd memory never-block-ui-thread.
notes:
Added requirement: taskbar button changes ANIMATED like Windows XP — buttons fade/grow in when a window opens, fade/shrink out when it closes, and width changes (as the strip fills) transition smoothly. Implement via Avalonia Transitions on the button DataTemplate (Opacity+Width) for add + resize; exit animation coordinated by ShellModel delaying the collection Remove (set IsClosing → animate → remove after ~150ms, via a non-blocking DispatcherTimer/Task.Delay+Post, never blocking the UI thread).
STATUS 2026-07-12 (uncommitted): TASKBAR portion DONE (background ShellModel + observable collections + off-thread cached icons + data-bound ItemsControl replacing imperative buttons + XP width/opacity animations 250ms + 2s reconcile prune). PENDING USER VERIFY: animations actually animate live; disappear works. NOT DONE: START MENU rewire — bind Programs to ShellModel.Programs as a virtualized ItemsControl, instant open, lazy icons (ProgramItemViewModel.EnsureIcon already written but unused; StartMenu.axaml.cs still on the old eager 284-icon path that froze ~2s). Next concrete step = rewrite StartMenu to bind + virtualize.
close_reason: Verified done — closing during M2 sweep (d941581 and prior)

title: Startup deadlock: SettingsService.LoadAsync().GetResult() on UI thread hangs when settings.json exists
description: App.axaml.cs OnFrameworkInitializationCompleted blocks the Avalonia UI thread with settings.LoadAsync().GetAwaiter().GetResult(). LoadAsync awaits File.ReadAllTextAsync with default ConfigureAwait(true), so the continuation is posted back to the blocked UI SynchronizationContext -> deadlock. Only triggers when ~/.config/bevel/settings.json EXISTS (first run skips the await via File.Exists gate, so it went unnoticed in bevel-wym). Symptoms: process alive + foreground GUI app but zero windows on screen, and ignores SIGTERM (RequestExit posts Shutdown to the non-pumping dispatcher). Exposed by bevel-0ml taskbarRows persistence which guarantees the file exists. Fix: ConfigureAwait(false) on the file I/O awaits in SettingsService so it is safe to block on from the UI thread. Diagnosed via macOS 'sample': main-thread parked in Monitor_Wait/SyncBlock::Wait.
notes: FIXED + VERIFIED LIVE (uncommitted). Fix: ConfigureAwait(false) on SettingsService LoadAsync/SaveAsync/UpdateAsync file I/O + moved the startup LoadAsync().GetResult() from App.OnFrameworkInitializationCompleted to Program.Main BEFORE StartWithClassicDesktopLifetime (loads before the thread becomes the UI thread). App now shows windows + honours SIGTERM even with settings.json present. Ready to commit.
close_reason: Verified fix present in working tree: SettingsService Load/Save/UpdateAsync all use ConfigureAwait(false) on file I/O (SettingsService.cs:61,105,112,119); startup load moved to Program.Main:48 before StartWithClassicDesktopLifetime; App.axaml.cs no longer blocks the UI thread on LoadAsync. Verified live per bead notes.

title: FM regressions: view-switch breaks mouse, dup on first load, ctx-menu position, single-click activates
description: After recent FM work: (1) switching to Large Icons (any view switch) breaks mouse events; (2) first load lazy-loads duplicate files/folders; (3) right-click menu doesn't open at cursor; (4) single-click sometimes activates/navigates into folder.
close_reason: Drag guarded (button-held + 10px), NavigateTo dedup stops racing first-load, context menu opens at pointer. Switch-then-click proves view switch is fine. 110 FM tests green.

title: [bug] Windows: task-button click often fails to take the foreground (SwitchToThisWindow no-ops under the foreground lock); optimistic press then snaps back
description:
User report: clicking Zen on the taskbar leaves focus on WezTerm ("it immediately goes back to wezterm"). INTERMITTENT — the same user saw a later click work.

Confirmed by screenshot of the live bar: 250ms after a click, Zen's button is pressed + bold (the optimistic ClaimFocus in TaskItemViewModel.ToggleAsync); 2.75s later the press has snapped back to WezTerm, and the OS foreground never moved at all. So the user sees the button flick over and come back.

Root cause: the Win32 foreground lock. SPI_GETFOREGROUNDLOCKTIMEOUT on this box reads 2147483647 ms (~24.8 days; HKCU ForegroundLockTimeout is 200000), so a process that does not hold foreground rights can effectively NEVER set the foreground. WindowsWindowManager.ActivateCore calls SwitchToThisWindow, which in that state silently no-ops — no error, nothing to log. Its comment states the opposite assumption: "called from the taskbar process, which holds input at click time) sidesteps the background-foreground restriction. No AttachThreadInput tricks." That holds only while the taskbar actually owns the last-input privilege, and the bar is WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW | WS_EX_NOACTIVATE | WS_EX_TOPMOST, so clicking it never makes the process foreground.

Evidence:
- A FRESHLY started console process calling the same wm.ActivateAsync activates Zen instantly (fresh processes get a one-time foreground grant). The SAME process 45s later could no longer change the foreground at all.
- Three synthetic clicks (Zen, Task Manager, Settings) all left WezTerm foreground — but each test first reset the foreground from MY process, which arms the lock, so those runs are confounded and must NOT be read as "always broken". The user's real click did work. Intermittency is the signature of the privilege, not of the target app.

NOT the macOS bug (bevel-hx63): that was the menu-close key-focus handback replaying a captured pid. TaskbarWindow.SetKeyFocusAllowed returns early unless IsOSPlatform(OSX), so no handback exists on Windows. Same symptom, different cause — do not port that fix.

Two distinct defects here:
1. Activation does not reliably take the foreground on Windows. Fix options, in the order I would try them: (a) the standard AttachThreadInput ladder around SetForegroundWindow — note CODEMAP currently states "No AttachThreadInput tricks", a decision made on the assumption SwitchToThisWindow suffices, which this disproves; (b) let the bar take activation for the duration of a click (drop WS_EX_NOACTIVATE on press only) — closest to what Explorer's own taskbar does, and structurally the mirror of the macOS menu-scoped key-focus flip (bevel-vk4n); (c) AllowSetForegroundWindow plumbing. Do NOT globally write SPI_SETFOREGROUNDLOCKTIMEOUT=0 — that mutates a user-wide setting.
2. The optimistic press is never reconciled against the outcome. ClaimFocus presses the button immediately and nothing verifies the activation landed; the strip is only corrected ~2s later by the reconcile poll, which is the visible "flick and snap back". The optimistic claim should be confirmed or rolled back off the activation result, independent of fix 1.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking an unfocused task button brings that window to the foreground reliably on Windows, including when another process changed the foreground moments earlier; the pressed state reflects the real outcome rather than flicking and reverting ~2s later.
close_reason: Fixed in 32671f6 and verified live on Win11 Pro 26300: ForegroundCore() runs an AttachThreadInput ladder (BringWindowToTop + SetForegroundWindow between attach/detach) with a SwitchToThisWindow fallback. Root cause was SPI_GETFOREGROUNDLOCKTIMEOUT = 2147483647ms on this box, under which SwitchToThisWindow silently no-ops without foreground rights. Verified under the armed-lock condition (clicks -> zen, -> Settings), which is the condition the original intermittency came from.

title: [bug] P1: hard-killing the Windows launcher kills the terminal that started it (job-object blast radius)
description:
Hard-killing the Windows launcher took down the WezTerm terminal that had started it, killing the user's interactive session along with the shell.

Observed 2026-10-01 on Windows 11 Pro 26300:
- The user had launched the 0.1.0 release build from their terminal: "C:\Users\<user>\Downloads\Bevel-0.1.0-win-x64\Bevel.App.exe" (pid 23932, parent pid 9016 — a process in the terminal's tree).
- An agent ran Stop-Process -Id 23932 (TerminateProcess) on that launcher.
- bevel-health heartbeats for core (pid 21788) and taskbar (pid 5076) stop at 16:25:52. The replacement WezTerm starts at 16:26:06. Launcher, core, taskbar AND the terminal all died in the same instant.

Suspected mechanism (NOT yet confirmed — needs the repro below): WindowsJobObject uses JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, documented in WindowsProcessLifecycle.cs as the orphan backstop so "a wedged or missed child can never outlive the shell". If the launcher process is created inside a job that already contains the launching console/terminal (or nests into it), then closing the launcher's job handle reaps the terminal too. The blast radius of that backstop is then the whole terminal session, not the shell.

Why this matters beyond the incident: a crashing launcher closes its handle the same way a kill does. If the mechanism is what it looks like, ANY launcher crash kills the terminal it was started from — which is how most people run a dev build.

Repro (do this in a VM or on a spare session, NOT on a working desktop):
1. From a terminal, start the launcher: Bevel.App.exe --pal=windows
2. Confirm core + taskbar are up (bevel-health heartbeats).
3. From a DIFFERENT terminal, TerminateProcess the launcher pid.
4. Check whether terminal #1 survives. Then repeat with the launcher started by double-click (no console parent) to isolate job membership from console-group membership.
5. Instrument: IsProcessInJob on the launcher and on the parent terminal at startup, and log which job the launcher assigns itself to.

Fix direction if confirmed: create the job with CreateJobObject and assign ONLY spawned children to it (never the launcher process itself, and never nest into an inherited job); or set JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_BREAKAWAY_OK / use CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB when spawning so the launcher's job can't contain anything it did not create. Either way, add a test that asserts the launching console's process is not a member of the shell's job.
acceptance_criteria: Terminating or crashing the launcher tears down only Bevel's own processes; the terminal/console that started it survives, pinned by a test asserting the parent console process is not a member of the shell's job object.

title: [bug] Windows task buttons render label-only: BuildForeignWindow hardcoded IconPng: null
description:
Reported from a real Windows run: taskbar icons are missing. Root cause is WindowsWindowManager.BuildForeignWindow hardcoding `IconPng: null` — the task button icon comes from ForeignWindow.IconPng (TaskItemViewModel -> ShellModel.LoadWindowIcon decodes it off-thread), NOT from IIconProvider, so there was never anything to decode and every button rendered label-only.

bevel-ncfp.3 listed "window icon (WM_GETICON/GCLP_HICON)" in scope and was closed with the rest of the window manager (enumeration, WinEvent deltas, actions, capture) implemented, but the icon half never got wired.

Fix sits on the working tree (NOT committed, NOT built — this Windows dev box has no .NET SDK):
- NEW src/Bevel.Pal.Windows/WindowsIconBits.cs: HICON -> top-down BGRA, straight alpha. WindowsIconProvider already had this GDI dance (GetIconInfo/GetObject/GetDIBits); both now share it instead of carrying two copies. Also fixes legacy (no-alpha-channel) icons: alpha now comes from the AND mask rather than being forced opaque, which used to draw a solid square.
- WindowsWindowManager.WindowIconPng(hwnd, exePath): WM_GETICON (BIG -> SMALL2 -> SMALL) via SendMessageTimeout (50ms, SMTO_ABORTIFHUNG — delta events run this on the WinEvent pump thread and one hung app must not stall the stream), then the class icon (GCLP_HICON/HICONSM), then PrivateExtractIcons on the owning exe at 64px to match the macOS helper 64px source. PNGs cached by icon SOURCE (HICON value, or exe path) so N windows of one app cost one encode and the redundant 2s re-poll (bevel-tnii) is a dictionary hit.
- ResolveIdentity now also returns ExePath, kept separate from BundleId: for a packaged app BundleId is an AUMID, and the icon backstop needs the hosted app real exe, never ApplicationFrameHost.
- EncodePng gained preserveAlpha (default false, so window capture keeps forced-opaque); an icon encoded opaque is a solid block.
- Tests in WindowsWindowManagerTests: portable alpha round-trip (small PNG reader), plus a Windows-only fact that a real enumerated window carries a decodable non-transparent icon and that a second enumeration returns the identical array (the cache).
acceptance_criteria:
- Windows task buttons show the app icon at every taskbar icon tier (16/24/32), not label-only.
- Verified on a real Windows box: dotnet build, dotnet test tests/Bevel.Pal.Windows.Tests, then an actual --pal=windows shell run.
- No GDI handle leak across repeated polls: borrowed WM_GETICON/class icons are never destroyed; GetIconInfo bitmap copies and the PrivateExtractIcons handle are always released.
notes:
BUILT AND VERIFIED on the Windows box (SDK 10.0.401 now installed; NuGet had no package source configured, so restore needs -s https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json until that is fixed in %APPDATA%\NuGet\NuGet.Config).

Results:
- dotnet build Bevel.sln: 0 errors. The 15 warnings in Bevel.Pal.Windows are all pre-existing CA1416 call-site notes, none from this change and none in CI's warnings-as-errors set.
- dotnet test Bevel.sln: 1249 passed. The one failure, Bevel.Core.Tests.SymlinkCopyTest, is unrelated and environmental: Directory.CreateSymbolicLink needs the create-symlink privilege (Developer Mode / elevation) and fails in the test's own setup.
- tests/Bevel.Pal.Windows.Tests: 66 passed, including the new window-icon fact (confirmed actually exercising, not early-returning: 5s runtime = notepad launch + two enumerations).
- END-TO-END on the live desktop via a throwaway probe against the real WindowsWindowManager: 6/6 enumerated windows carried a decodable icon PNG. WezTerm 64px, Zen 32px (x2), Explorer 40px, Settings 64px, a third-party app 64px. Alpha survives where the source has it (Explorer 37% transparent, corner alpha 0).

Ordering corrected during verification: the exe's icon resource now ranks ABOVE the class icon (was below). Reason is resolution, not quality — PrivateExtractIcons takes the size we ask for, so the exe gives the 64px source this shell wants, while a class icon is whatever edge the app registered (WezTerm: no WM_GETICON icon, 32px class icon, 64px exe icon of the same artwork). The window's own WM_GETICON icon still outranks both as the only per-window identity.

False alarm worth recording: a window reporting itself as "Task Manager" came out fully opaque and looked like an alpha bug. It is not Windows' Task Manager — it is a third-party C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\Task Manager TMOG\Task Manager.exe whose icon genuinely has no transparency. A fully-opaque icon is NOT evidence of a broken alpha path; measured in CODEMAP as a not-this.

GDI handles: now covered by a test, not an assertion. WindowsIconBitsTests.Windows_repeated_reads_leak_no_gdi_objects does 500 conversions and asserts GetGuiResources(GR_GDIOBJECTS) growth stays under 10 (a two-bitmap-per-read leak would be +1000). Passes.

REMAINING for acceptance: the visual check in a live shell (dotnet run --project src/Bevel.App -- --pal=windows). Not done — that takes over the user's desktop surface, so it needs their go-ahead.

Files: src/Bevel.Pal.Windows/WindowsIconBits.cs (new), src/Bevel.Pal.Windows/WindowsWindowManager.cs, src/Bevel.Pal.Windows/WindowsFileStack.cs (WindowsIconProvider delegates to the shared helper), tests/Bevel.Pal.Windows.Tests/WindowsWindowManagerTests.cs, tests/Bevel.Pal.Windows.Tests/WindowsIconBitsTests.cs (new), CODEMAP.md (Notes bullet on the window-icon pipeline). Uncommitted on main.
Correction: the SiteShot 2x rendering gotcha described in the close reason is filed as bevel-xwex (the close reason names bevel-7wnq, which was a placeholder written before the id was assigned — no such issue).
close_reason:
Visual check done and passing — headlessly, without launching the shell onto the live desktop.

Method: a temporary harvest harness in Bevel.Taskbar.Tests rendered the real TaskbarView through Avalonia headless (SiteShot), fed with the icons the REAL WindowsWindowManager produced for the live desktop's windows. Harness deleted after the shot; it asserted nothing and depended on whatever windows were open.

Result at both tiers (Normal 16px and Big 32px, downscaled from the 64px source): WezTerm, the third-party Task Manager, Zen and Settings all render their correct app icons with alpha intact (rounded icon corners show the button face through), labels bold on the focused button, and the minimized Zen window's icon correctly dimmed via ContentOpacity. Measured per button in the PNG: buttons carry 350-1450 coloured pixels each where before the fix every button was label-only.

Gotcha worth knowing for any future taskbar screenshot (filed as bevel-7wnq): the first shots came out as one giant clipped glyph plus five EMPTY buttons, which looked like an icon bug and was not. SiteShot renders at 2x through RenderTargetBitmap, and its own doc comment warns that content forcing an intermediate composition layer renders wrong above 1x (content magnified and clipped, chrome at 1x). Task buttons animate Width/Opacity, which forces exactly that layer. scale: 1 renders correctly. Diagnosing this needed pixel counting per button region — the logical tree reported correct 32x32 Images with bound sources the whole time, so the visual tree and the captured frame disagreed.

Final gates: dotnet build Bevel.sln 0 errors; dotnet test Bevel.sln 1252 passed, 1 pre-existing environmental failure (Bevel.Core.Tests.SymlinkCopyTest needs the create-symlink privilege). tests/Bevel.Pal.Windows.Tests 66 passed including the GDI-leak guard.

title: Space switch: warp-and-restore so first taskbar click visibly flips other-display Spaces
description:
## Why
After removing permanent cursor warp (felt 'very off'), Jump Space switch works from the 2nd attempt on. Logs show first click does succeed Hide/Show/SetCurrent (currents update) but Mission Control applies the *visible* transition to the display under the pointer — so a primary-taskbar click only updates bookkeeping until a second click (or a click on that display).

## What
In SkyLight.switchToSpace: save cursor, focusDisplay (warp + mouseMoved onto owning display) BEFORE Hide/Show/SetCurrent, then warp cursor back. Do not leave the pointer on the other screen.

## Acceptance
- First taskbar click on a Jump session on the other display visibly switches that display's Space
- Cursor ends where the user clicked (taskbar), not teleported mid-screen
notes: ce-optimize: sibling_steal 0.538→0.0 via suppress+pin (exp2) + drop setFrontOnSpace (exp1). Live paint bench still 1.0. Helper redeployed to dist. Pending USER verify: first taskbar click on other-display Jump flips Space. Eval: python3 tools/eval/space_activate_eval.py; seed via tools/eval/HelperActivateJump.

title: ItemView static selection brushes resolved once at type-init, never invalidated
description:
Part of the stale-value audit (parent theme: value captured once in a provisional/prior state, nothing re-reads it when the real value arrives).

src/Bevel.FileManager/Components/ItemView.axaml.cs:267-273:
  static readonly IBrush SelectionFill/SelectionText/NormalText = ThemeBrush(...)

Unlike Glyphs' brush cache, these are plain C# static fields evaluated ONCE on first touch of the ItemView type (i.e. the first Explorer window constructed in the process), via a private ThemeBrush() helper. There is no cache-clear hook and nothing subscribes to a theme-change notification for them.

Captured: first Explorer window construction, whatever theme is active at that instant.
Should refresh: on the same theme-switch signal Glyphs uses (ThemeCacheInvalidated) or on settings.Changed re-theme.
Does it: no -- static fields, initialized once for the process lifetime.

Symptom: bevel-lej1's own repro shows the type can easily be first-touched during the startup window where settings have not arrived yet (Win2000 defaults painting before the real Luna settings land). If ItemView is first constructed in that window, the selection highlight and text colors freeze at Win2000 navy/white for the REST OF THE PROCESS, even after every other surface (icons via GlyphIcon, chrome, taskbar) correctly re-themes to Luna moments later. Result: a Win2000-navy selection bar permanently inside an otherwise-Luna Explorer window, for that run.

Fix shape: turn these into instance-level or theme-observable brushes (e.g. GetResourceObservable, matching the pattern already used correctly for the tray icon tint in TaskbarView.axaml.cs:419-423) instead of static readonly fields computed once. Needs a small design decision on the right binding mechanism for ItemView's rendering path -- left as a bead rather than fixed in this audit pass.

title: Glyphs.Icon() direct consumers never rebuild on live theme switch
description:
Part of the stale-value audit (parent theme: value captured once in a provisional/prior state, nothing re-reads it when the real value arrives).

Glyphs' static brush cache IS correctly invalidated on every theme/scheme/variant switch (InvalidateThemeCache(), wired from ThemeService.cs:140, ColorSchemeService.cs:81, Luna/LunaVariant.cs:197), and GlyphIcon (src/Bevel.UI/GlyphIcon.cs:52-69) is the one correct consumer: it subscribes to Glyphs.ThemeCacheInvalidated and rebuilds itself.

But several call sites bypass GlyphIcon and call Glyphs.Icon(...) directly, getting back a Path/Canvas that holds the ALREADY-RESOLVED brush objects from whenever it was built. Nothing tells these controls the cache was dropped:
  - src/Bevel.FileManager/Components/ItemView.axaml.cs:312,321,330,348,371
  - src/Bevel.Taskbar/StartMenu.axaml.cs:501
  - src/Bevel.FileManager/Components/PropertiesDialog.axaml.cs:169,214 (lower severity: transient dialog, short-lived)

Captured: whenever the icon is first realized (item listed, or StartMenu constructed).
Should refresh: on Glyphs.ThemeCacheInvalidated, same as GlyphIcon.
Does it: no.

Symptom: bevel-lej1/bevel-7s9n already proved that a live theme change happens on this shell (both via a genuine settings edit and via an async startup race). When that happens with an Explorer window open, every file/folder icon already on screen keeps the OLD theme's palette (wrong folder yellow, wrong paper colour) until the row is virtualized away and rebuilt -- which for a small/static listing may never happen without a full re-list. StartMenu's 8 fixed-item glyphs (Programs/Documents/Settings/Search/Help/Run/LogOff/ShutDown) are built once in its ctor and StartMenu itself is a lazily-cached singleton (TaskbarView.axaml.cs:401) that lives for the whole taskbar process, so once stale, stale for the rest of the session.

Fix shape: either route these call sites through GlyphIcon (preferred, matches the one correct pattern) or add the same Glyphs.ThemeCacheInvalidated subscription + rebuild wherever Glyphs.Icon() is still called directly. Needs a design decision on which, and StartMenu's lifecycle makes the fix non-trivial (not a one-line invalidation call) -- left as a bead rather than fixed in this audit pass.

title: [bug] No single-instance guard: a second launch hijacks the core socket instead of discovering the running shell
description:
## Why

Hit hard on 2026-09-29. Repeated build/relaunch cycles left FIVE Bevel processes alive from three separate launches (19:18, 19:23, 19:36 plus a 19:44 core+taskbar pair) — three orphaned launchers competing with one live pair. Symptoms the user saw: the taskbar reverted to 1 row, the theme reverted to Win2000, tray icons stopped rendering, and a fixed bug appeared to come back. All of it was several instances writing one settings.db and one socket.

The persisted settings were NEVER damaged (themeId=luna, taskbarRows=2 still on disk, PRAGMA integrity_check ok) — they were simply being overwritten in memory by whichever instance wrote last.

## What is missing

- No single-instance guard anywhere in Bevel.App or Bevel.Taskbar: no mutex, no lock file, no 'already running' check. Launching the binary a second time starts a whole second shell.
- UdsMessageServer.cs:83 does File.Delete(_socketPath) BEFORE binding, so a second core silently unlinks the first core's socket and takes it over. The first core keeps running, orphaned and unreachable, while still holding settings.db open.

That second point also undermines bevel-hprv's health probe: the probe asks whether core.sock is connectable, and after a hijack it is — just to the wrong core.

## What it should do

A second launch should DISCOVER the running shell and hand off to it (focus/raise, or exit quietly), not start a rival. Concretely:
- Take an exclusive lock (flock on a pidfile, or bind the socket WITHOUT unlinking and treat EADDRINUSE as 'someone else owns this').
- Only unlink a stale socket after proving nobody is listening on it — connect first, unlink only on refusal.
- The launcher should adopt or refuse, and say which.

## Acceptance

- Running the binary twice leaves exactly one launcher, one core, one taskbar
- A second launch reports that a shell is already running rather than starting one
- A genuinely stale socket (owner died) is still reclaimed, so a crash does not wedge the next start
- Covered by a test that starts two launchers against one socket dir
close_reason: Duplicate of bevel-wio0, which described this design (flock + probe-then-bind + owner-only unlink) on 2026-08-20 and predicted the exact failure. Today's field evidence folded into that bead and its priority raised to P1.

title: Start menu: type-to-search while open
description:
## Problem
With the Start menu open, typing does nothing — no filter, no jump-to-program. Live report: \"start menu still doesn't allow to search when typing.\" Expected: modern-shell type-to-search (or at least classic first-letter jump) while the menu is open.

## Context
- opportunity-map ranks this as \"Start menu type-to-search (mandatory)\": classic = type-to-select in Programs cascade; Luna = inline filter over FrequentPrograms + All Programs, Enter launches top hit.
- Spec R-KB-1: Start menu keyboard-operable including first-letter.
- Current \"Search\" UI is only a leaf (For Files or Folders… / On the Internet…) via _openSearch — not an in-menu filter.
- Program index / FrequentPrograms already exist (ProgramsVm); data side is ready.
- Related foundation: shared TypeToFind service (ItemView.TypeAhead extract) — optional dependency; Start menu can ship a focused filter first.

## Acceptance
- With Start open, printable keystrokes filter or jump within Programs (both classic cascade and Luna two-column)
- Enter launches the current/top match; Esc clears filter or closes menu (match existing Esc behavior)
- Focus/typing must not fight menu navigation (arrows still work)
- No UI-thread blocking over the program index
- Headless/unit coverage for filter + Enter launch path

## Non-goals
- Full Spotlight / file index in Start (spec: apps via our index; ⌘Space stays system)
- Replacing the Search submenu leaves
acceptance_criteria: Typing with Start open filters/jumps Programs; Enter launches top hit; arrows/Esc still work; tests cover filter path
notes:
## Fixed (2026-09-23), merged to main

Root cause: the Start menu had NO key or text-input handler at all — AND the obvious place to add one
would not have worked. The menu lives in a Popup, a separate visual tree with its own TopLevel, so a
handler on the StartMenu UserControl never sees a keystroke aimed at the focused menu row. Handlers must
be attached to the popup's OWN root panel and to the inner Menu (the ancestor Avalonia's menu interaction
handler uses to receive keys from nested submenu rows), de-duplicated per event instance.

Shipped: new Model/StartMenuFilter.cs (pure logic) — accumulating query ignoring control chars and a
leading space, ranked name-prefix > word-start > substring, ties in index order, a linear pass over the
already-in-memory program list (no I/O, nothing off the UI thread needed). Both layouts filter while
typing: classic turns the Programs cascade into the ranked result cascade and opens it, with a sunken
Win2000 search field (code-drawn vector magnifier, theme tokens) showing live query + match count; Luna
turns the pinned column into the result list with a rounded field under the header, restoring the curated
frequent list when cleared. Enter launches the top match and closes, but DEFERS when focus has been
arrowed onto a matched row so that row's own activation wins. Backspace widens, Escape clears the query
before closing (two-step), arrows/Home/End untouched, empty results show a disabled (No matches) row
rather than an empty cascade. Search submenu leaves unchanged.

Design decision worth review: ONE mechanism (a filter) for both layouts rather than classic-jump +
Luna-filter. The bead allows 'filter OR jump ... in BOTH'. Bevel.Core.Input.TypeToFind was deliberately
NOT reused — it is a jump matcher with a 700ms idle reset, and a search query must survive the pause while
you read results. Rationale documented in the new class. (So bevel-psro's shared-service extraction does
not subsume this.)

Files: Model/StartMenuFilter.cs (new), StartMenu.axaml, StartMenu.axaml.cs, TaskbarView.axaml.cs (3 lines
in the existing Escape branch), tests StartMenuSearchTests.cs (new) + RenderStartMenuSearchTest.cs (new).

Tests: 14 behaviour + a 2-case render test typing through the real event path.

### Integration fix (mine, not the agent's)
RenderStartMenuSearchTest(luna) passed in the worktree and FAILED on integrated main:
CaptureRenderedFrame() returned null under a full-solution run (test assemblies run in parallel, first
frame still pending) though the search strip already had real bounds. Same flake class as
RenderLunaStartMenuTest; fixed the same way — poll the FRAME on a time-based deadline instead of capturing
once. Assertion strength unchanged, no product behaviour involved. Commit 9532d4d.

Verified on main: full suite 1079 passed / 0 failed / 2 skipped.

### Remaining before close: on-device QA
1. NESTED-POPUP ROUTING — the important one. Headless Avalonia never realizes a submenu's containers or
   lays out popup content, so no test can raise a keystroke from a FOCUSED CASCADE ROW. Typing right after
   opening always lands on a main-popup row (focus never moves on its own), so that path IS covered — but
   verify on a real macOS run that typing keeps working after you arrow Down into the results. That is
   exactly why the handler is also attached to the inner Menu.
2. Bare-letter mnemonics (_Programs, _Help): Avalonia's AccessKeyHandler lives on the popup's TopLevel and
   tunnels ahead of anything registerable here, so if it activates bare letters while the menu is open it
   could race the filter. No sign of it headlessly (open-mode cascade rows aren't a Menu), needs a real check.
3. site/index.html not updated with a re-harvested search shot — deliberately left alone during the
   parallel run since it is a merge magnet. Harvest via BEVEL_RENDER_OUT=... --filter RenderStartMenuSearch.

title: Taskbar click fails to raise app / focus snaps back (Arc vs Terminal)
description:
## Why
User report on macOS: clicking a taskbar button often does not bring the target app forward, or focus immediately switches back. Reproduced when trying to activate Arc — Terminal kept coming back immediately.

## What
Investigate Activate/RestoreAndActivate vs menu-scoped key-focus handback (SetKeyFocusAllowed / CancelKeyFocusHandback / prior-app PID). Suspect prior-app re-activation stomps a just-activated window, or IsFocused is stale so Toggle minimizes/activates the wrong way.

## Acceptance
- Clicking an unfocused task button raises that window and it stays frontmost
- Prior app (e.g. Terminal) does not immediately steal focus back
- Menu handback still restores focus when the menu closes without an activation action
design: Preferred fix: call CancelKeyFocusHandback before any menu dismiss when ToggleAsync activates a foreign window; optionally strengthen helper NSRunningApplication.activate to IgnoringOtherApps. Do not remove handback for true menu Esc/dismiss without an activate.
notes:
## Fix applied (2026-09-23) — handback is now evidence-based

### Root cause (confirmed in code, not just suspected)
The menu-close handback replayed a pid captured at menu-OPEN time, unconditionally. Correctness
therefore depended on every call site that activates a foreign window remembering to call
CancelKeyFocusHandback() first — an opt-out contract. ActivateGroupWindowRow + TaskButtonMenu
onActivateForeign do remember; the plain task-button ActivateCommand (TaskbarView.axaml:147 ->
TaskItemViewModel.ToggleAsync) does NOT.

Repro path confirmed reachable: StartMenu.axaml has IsLightDismissEnabled=True, so with Start open,
clicking a task button dismisses the popup -> Closed -> ExitMenuScope -> SetKeyFocusAllowed(false) ->
ActivateAppByPid(priorApp). That re-raises the previously-frontmost app (Terminal) over the
just-activated one (Arc). It wins every time, not just on a race, because the handback uses
activateWithOptions: NSApplicationActivateIgnoringOtherApps while the helper's foreign activation uses
a bare NSRunningApplication.activate() (WindowServiceImpl.raiseAppThenWindow:1101) — unequal strength.

Ruled out along the way: the hover tooltip is a raw Popup, not a FlyoutBase, so WireFlyoutScope never
puts it in menu scope — it does not capture a prior pid. With NO menu open _priorAppPid is 0, so on a
plain click nothing in our code re-activates anyone; the notes' hypothesis #1 only bites while an owned
menu/popup is open, which is exactly the hole above.

### Fix (root cause, all call sites)
TaskbarWindow.ShouldHandBackKeyFocus(priorAppPid, frontmostPid, ownPid) now gates the handback on the
LIVE foreground instead of trusting the call site:
  prior <= 0            -> false (nothing captured / cancelled)
  frontmost <= 0        -> true  (unknown; keep classic restore)
  frontmost == prior    -> true  (no-op handback, harmless)
  frontmost == ownPid   -> true  (only we took front for the menu; restore the user's app)
  otherwise             -> false (a THIRD app is front => we activated it; never stomp it)
A third app holding the foreground IS the evidence that an activation we drove landed. This converts
the invariant from 'every call site promises' to 'observable evidence' and covers present + future
sites. Existing CancelKeyFocusHandback calls remain correct but are no longer load-bearing.

Tests: 5 new [Theory] cases in TaskbarAccessibilityTests (Key_focus_handback_only_runs_when_no_other_
app_took_the_foreground). Full solution suite green (968 passed / 0 failed).

### Deliberately NOT changed
Helper activation strength (raiseAppThenWindow bare activate()). Deployment target is macOS 15 where
activate(options:) is deprecated; the macOS 14+ replacement is activate(from:). I have no evidence that
path actually fails — the reported symptom is fully explained by the handback — so hardening it would be
a speculative fix. Revisit only if on-device QA shows a no-menu-open failure.

### Remaining before close: on-device QA
Acceptance is behavioural and needs the real PAL + AX grants + real Arc/Terminal:
 1. Start open -> click Arc's task button -> Arc comes forward and STAYS (was: Terminal snapped back)
 2. No menu open -> click an unfocused task button -> target raises and stays frontmost
 3. Open Start, press Escape (no activation) -> focus returns to the prior app (handback still works)
 4. Group flyout row + context-menu Activate still land frontmost
close_reason: Verified on device 2026-09-29 (macOS, signed dev build 3252897). Clicking an unfocused task button raises the target and it stays frontmost — the prior app no longer steals focus back. This is the case that could not be proven headless: the evidence-based handback (ShouldHandBackKeyFocus) only matters against real AX activation.

title: PublishSingleFile dist drops Avalonia XAML (TaskbarView XamlLoadException)
description:
## Why
A rebuilt dist/Bevel.app (PublishSingleFile + R2R) crash-looped the taskbar on XamlLoadException loading TaskbarView / missing AvaloniaResources. Framework-dependent DLL run succeeded. A 0-byte Luna DLL was a separate publish glitch (clean republish fixed LunaTheme). The new health framework (bevel-9h7n) will now Hold + alert instead of spinning silently, but the packaged app still cannot boot.

## What
Find why single-file publish omits or fails to load TaskbarView XAML (and any other !AvaloniaResources). Likely IncludeAvaloniaResources / PublishSingleFile interaction. Do not ship dist until a packaged .app can create the taskbar surface. Framework-dependent and Fake PAL paths are not the acceptance test.

## Acceptance
- dist/Bevel.app (build-app.sh && dev-sign.sh) launches launcher+core+taskbar without XamlLoadException
- Heartbeat for taskbar reaches ready; no Hold/CrashLoop
- Luna theme DLL in the bundle is non-empty
notes: Reopened: closed by mistake during CI merge; PublishSingleFile XAML issue remains.
close_reason: Verified against the live deploy: dist/publish-app/Bevel.App passes verify-bundle.py (8 Avalonia assemblies carry CompiledAvaloniaXaml + !AvaloniaResources, Luna.dll non-empty 98KB), and the CURRENTLY RUNNING dist/Bevel.app shell (built by build-app.sh + dev-sign.sh) has core + taskbar heartbeats at status=ready on the same build stamp — no XamlLoadException, no Hold. Root cause was a corrupted incremental Release build; build-app.sh is now clean-by-default and gates every bundle through verify-bundle.py.

comments.author: ikari
comments.text: Root cause + fix (commit 2007ab3 on worktree-agent-a7297ec5e4d4e8649): the crash was a CORRUPTED INCREMENTAL Release build, not a PublishSingleFile/R2R/avares defect. Evidence: clean single-file publishes of a639386 (the tree current when this was reopened) and of HEAD both bundle every UI assembly with CompiledAvaloniaXaml + !AvaloniaResources (manifest-parsed), and a --role=taskbar process from the artifact reaches heartbeat status=ready (written only after new TaskbarView() + Show()). Mechanism: Avalonia's CompileAvaloniaXamlTask rewrites obj/<cfg>/net10.0/<proj>.dll in place with no inputs/outputs, so an interrupted/concurrent build leaves plain IL that R2R+single-file bundle silently. Fix: build-app.sh cleans Release obj/bin (CLEAN=0 to skip) and gates the bundle via packaging/macos/verify-bundle.py (fails the build instead of shipping a XamlLoadException). NOT verified: the original crash itself could not be re-reproduced from a clean tree (it is not deterministic from source); acceptance item 'dist/Bevel.app via build-app.sh && dev-sign.sh launches launcher+core+taskbar' was exercised only against a scratch OUT with Fake PAL in isolated HOME/TMPDIR, not against the user's live dist/.

title: Shell process health: startup, IPC, version skew
description:
## Why
A packaged dist that crash-looped on XamlLoadException (TaskbarView) plus a 0-byte Luna DLL looked "not even up" — the launcher kept respawning silently. Startup failures, core IPC drops, and cross-role version mismatches must be first-class signals: visible, logged, and healed (restart with budget) or held with an alert so they cannot be invisible.

## What
- Per-role heartbeat files (starting/ready/failed) + BEVEL_BUILD_STAMP / protocol
- ShellHealthMonitor (tick-based): StartupFailed, StartupStuck, VersionSkew, Communication, CrashLoop
- Supervisor honors Hold (no more silent respawn) and Restart (skew / stuck / lost core)
- Native user alert on Hold; always log to RestartDiag + health status file
- Tests for monitor policy + supervisor hold/skew; wire ReportStarting/Ready/Failed in Program/App

## Acceptance
- A child that reports failed (e.g. XAML) is held after the first death and surfaces an alert — not crash-looped
- A live child whose stamp/protocol does not match the launcher is restarted onto the current binary (budget then hold)
- Taskbar ready but core=false for N ticks restarts the core
- Existing supervisor tests still pass with health monitor optional/off
close_reason: Health framework landed: heartbeats + ShellHealthMonitor (startup fail/stuck, version skew, lost IPC, crash-loop hold+alert), wired in Program/App/supervisor, 34 related tests passing. Does not fix the dist PublishSingleFile XAML load; that remains a packaging follow-up.

title: Quit leaves the Windows taskbar hidden (no restore / no crash-heal)
description:
## Why
Hiding Shell_TrayWnd is a process-local ShowWindow(SW_HIDE). Nothing restores it:
- TaskbarWindow.OnClosed unsubscribes Screens.Changed only — never SetAutoHideAsync(false).
- WindowsDockController is not IDisposable, has no ProcessExit handler, and writes no crash marker.
- MacOSDockController does all three (bevel-3kz). Windows does not.
A hard kill (Job Object, 3s grace then Kill) skips OnClosed entirely, so the machine is left with no taskbar at all. User-reported as much worse than the positioning bug.

## What
- OnClosed + host Dispose + ProcessExit all restore Shell_TrayWnd (and Shell_SecondaryTrayWnd).
- Persist a claim marker; heal on next launch like the macOS Dock controller.
- Restore even when SetAutoHideAsync(false) never ran.

## Acceptance
- Start ▸ Quit shows the Windows taskbar again.
- kill -9 / Job-Object teardown: next Bevel launch (or a heal path) restores it if the marker is present.
notes: Fix in tree: OnClosed SetAutoHideAsync(false); WindowsDockController is IDisposable + ProcessExit + win-taskbar-claimed.json crash-heal (mirrors MacOSDockController); also restores Shell_SecondaryTrayWnd. Pending Windows-box deploy.

title: Start ▸ Quit only restarts the taskbar (launcher treats it as a crash)
description:
## Why
Quit Bevel comes back. Two independent holes:
1. LauncherControl.Command.Quit only stop.Set()s — unlike SIGTERM/SIGINT/WindowsShutdownSignal it does NOT RequestStop(), so the monitor can respawn a child that exits during teardown (the bevel-ply race, quit path only).
2. RequestExit returns after a successful TrySend(Quit) without exiting the sender. If TrySend fails (stale launcher.sock), it ShutdownLocal()s only THIS process; the launcher sees a dead taskbar and respawns it. That is the 'wrong process comes back' irony.

## What
- Quit handler must RequestStop() before stop.Set(), matching the signal handlers.
- RequestExit writes a quit-request marker the monitor honors (no respawn) BEFORE sending or falling back to ShutdownLocal.
- Clear a stale marker at launcher boot.

## Acceptance
- Start ▸ Quit tears the whole shell down and nothing comes back.
- A failed launcher-control send still quits (does not look like Restart).
notes: Fix in tree: Quit handler RequestStop(); RequestExit writes quit-requested marker before send; monitor honors marker and will not respawn; RequestRestart no longer goes through RequestExit. Tests: QuitRequestTests, RoleProcessSupervisorTests.Does_not_respawn_when_quit_is_requested. Pending Windows-box deploy.
close_reason: Verified on device 2026-09-29 (macOS, signed dev build 3252897). Start > Turn Off exits the whole shell — the launcher no longer reads the quit as a crash and restarts the taskbar — and the macOS Dock is restored on the way out.

title: Core stays down: launcher watches process liveness, not the socket
description:
## Why
Peers show the disconnected-core indicator and stay that way. The launcher does not bring core back because RoleProcessSupervisor only respawns when Process.HasExited. A core whose socket was unlinked (or never bound) still looks healthy in ps, so the crash-monitor never fires. Manual "Restart shell core" exists (bevel-corepulse UI) but nothing auto-repairs.

## What
- Supervisor: when Core is alive, probe core.sock (missing/unconnectable for a few ticks) and restart it the same way as a crash.
- Taskbar: after a sustained disconnect, auto-send RestartCore (capped) instead of waiting for a click.
- Cover both with supervisor + auto-repair tests.

## Acceptance
- Killing or unlinking core.sock while the core process still lives causes a respawn without user action.
- A healthy core that is merely slow to accept the first connect is not kill-looped.
notes: Fix in tree: supervisor coreHealthyProbe (core.sock missing → Kill+Start after 3 ticks) + LostCoreAutoRepair (8s disconnect → RestartCore, cap 3). Tests: RoleProcessSupervisorTests.Restarts_a_live_core_whose_health_probe_fails, LostCoreAutoRepairTests. Pending Windows-box deploy.
close_reason:
Verified on device 2026-09-29 (macOS, signed dev build 3252897). Both acceptance criteria met.

AUTO-REPAIR: unlinked core.sock while the core PROCESS was left alive — the exact case the old supervisor missed, since Process.HasExited stays false and the core still looks healthy in ps. The launcher replaced it within 2.5s: core 14226 -> 17571, socket recreated, helper respawned alongside it (14228 -> 17575). No user action, no click on 'Restart shell core'.

NO KILL-LOOP: core pid stable at 14226 for 20s before the test and at 17571 for 30s after, so the health probe repairs once and then leaves a healthy core alone.

STILL SERVING AFTERWARDS: connected to the recreated socket directly (AF_UNIX) and it accepted, so the new core is bound and listening, not merely present. The launcher (14224) and taskbar (14227) kept their original pids — only core and its helper were replaced, which is the intended blast radius.

Windows-box deploy for the same path is still outstanding — see bevel-injy and bevel-h0sr.

title: Tray icons never captured: self-test probes the retired SCK path and latches liveMirroring=false
description: TrayServiceImpl.selfTestCapture() still fetches SCShareableContent(onScreenWindowsOnly: true) and captures via SCK — a pipeline enumerateWithCapture() no longer uses (it moved to LegacyWindowCapture precisely because SCK returns -3811 for a window that has left every display, the state Strategy A and third-party bar managers like Ice put status items in). With items hidden, the probe finds no status window, reports 'granted but broken', and LATCHES liveMirroringEnabled=false, so enumerateWithCapture bails at its guard and every item keeps its limited-mode app icon. Self-reinforcing: the better the off-screen hiding works, the more certainly the self-test fails. Observed: self-test build=25G229 discovered=true ax=true grant=true capture=false -> liveMirroring=false.
