title: [design] Single-instance lock + probe-before-bind + owner-only socket unlink
description: Fable: the automation socket (and core.sock/launcher.sock) is a FIXED path with last-writer-wins clobbering + unconditional unlink on dispose (AutomationSocket.cs:122-125,191; UdsMessageServer.cs:83). A stray/old shell EXITING unlinks the CURRENT shell's live socket -> bevelctl silently dead until taskbar restart. Two shells is the normal dev situation (dist-run + /Applications; install-local pkills only by $DEST). NO single-instance guard exists. Design: (a) flock ~/.config/bevel/shell.lock held by the launcher for its lifetime; a 2nd launcher exits (or --takeover SIGTERMs the incumbent by recorded pid); (b) socket claim = probe-then-bind (connect first; a live answer => stand down, don't delete; only clobber on ECONNREFUSED/ENOENT); (c) dispose unlinks ONLY if it still owns the inode / holds the lock.
notes:
## This bit hard today — raising to P1 with field evidence (2026-09-29)

Predicted here on 2026-08-20 and confirmed in a live session. Repeated build/relaunch cycles left FIVE processes from three launches (launchers at 19:18, 19:23 and 19:36, plus a 19:44 core+taskbar pair) — three orphaned launchers competing with one live pair, all writing one settings.db.

What the user saw, all from this one cause: the taskbar reverted to 1 row, the theme reverted to Win2000, tray icons stopped rendering, and an already-fixed placement bug appeared to come back (an older in-memory image was still drawing the bar). Their reaction was the correct instinct — 'they should all discover and the core must be a singleton, right?'

IMPORTANT: no data was lost. settings.db was intact throughout (themeId=luna, taskbarRows=2, PRAGMA integrity_check ok). The settings were being overwritten in MEMORY by whichever instance wrote last, not corrupted on disk. Worth keeping in the design: the failure mode is confusing rather than destructive, which is why it went unnoticed for so long.

ALSO WORTH NOTING for (b) probe-then-bind: this undermines bevel-hprv's health probe. hprv restarts a core whose core.sock is not connectable — but after a hijack the socket IS connectable, just owned by the wrong core. The two fixes should be designed together, or hprv's probe will happily certify a hijacked socket as healthy.

Duplicate filed and closed today: bevel-l0uk.
## The settings-ownership invariant is SOUND — the gap is purely instance-level (2026-09-29)

Verified on the live shell with lsof: exactly ONE process holds settings.db / -wal / -shm open, and it is --role=core. The launcher and taskbar never touch the file. RoleSelectorTests pins this (Core -> SettingsService as sole DB writer; Taskbar/Explorer/Desktop -> RemoteSettingsService through the core).

So today's damage was NOT a settings-layer bug. Each of the three concurrent shells had its own core correctly acting as sole writer for its own shell — all three just pointed at the same file. The per-shell invariant held; nothing enforces one shell. That is this bead, and it confirms the lock belongs at the LAUNCHER/instance level, not anywhere near the settings code.

It also explains why repeated kill -9 destroyed nothing: SQLite is in WAL mode, so concurrent cross-process access is safe at the file level. PRAGMA integrity_check returned ok and every value survived (themeId=luna, taskbarRows=2, lunaColor=Purple, opacity=79). The damage was semantic only — competing writers overwriting each other's values — which presents to the user as 'my theme and layout reverted' with no data actually lost. Worth knowing when writing the fix: there is no corruption path to defend against here, only a who-owns-the-shell question.
close_reason: Landed on worktree-agent-a1a544fec56ce1000 @ 3342f4a: ShellInstanceLock (flock ~/.config/bevel/shell.lock, launcher-first), UdsSocketClaim probe-then-bind + owner-only unlink (raw fd on Unix because Socket.Dispose deletes a Bind()-bound UDS path by path), CoreSocketProbe authenticated health/readiness probe closing the hprv hijack hole, core stands down + ReportFailed on a busy path. 17 IPC + 5 automation-socket + 436 taskbar tests green.

title: [design] Peer-side settings snapshot cache on disk -> correct-theme first paint, zero IPC
description: Fable: on cold boot the taskbar's single settings dial usually LOSES the race with the core's socket bind (core must boot .NET + open SQLite before _server.Start()), so it paints in DEFAULT theme then visibly re-themes ~1s later when the snapshot lands (App.axaml.cs:146-165) — the theme flash the user saw. Fix: peers write-through-cache the last applied settings snapshot to a local file (~/.config/bevel/) and PAINT FROM THAT CACHE with zero IPC; the live snapshot corrects only real changes. Kills the flash AND the 5s worst-case tail. Small, high leverage. NO paint should ever wait on a socket.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: SettingsSnapshotCache (src/Bevel.Core) is the peer's write-through first-paint cache, wired via CompositionRoot and RemoteSettingsService; peer paints with zero IPC, live snapshot compared by content (BlobsEquivalent) + version guard; unparseable blob refused. Tests: SettingsSnapshotCacheTests (21) + RemoteSettingsFirstPaintTests (9) all pass. Was reopened by mistake during CI merge.

title: [design] Filers become supervised launcher children + a parked pre-warmed instance (instant open)
description: Fable: the 'first Explorer click opened never, 2nd worked' is a REAL first-spawn flaw, not a transient. SpawnExplorer uses nohup-detached /bin/sh (Program.cs:373-474): window-open latency = full process cold start (single-file native-lib self-extract on first run of a new build + dyld + Avalonia/DI + settings dial), failure is INVISIBLE (Process.Start of /bin/sh always 'succeeds'; child death -> bevel-restart.log, unwatched), and there's NO supervision/reuse (every click forks fresh; crashed Explorer never returns; not killed on Quit; NOT restarted by RestartAll -> version skew after self-update; nohup breaks TCC attribution per Program.cs:326-329). Fix: (a) Explorer spawning goes through the LAUNCHER (a SpawnExplorer launcher-control verb) so it's supervised, torn down on quit, restarted on RestartAll, with captured stderr + liveness ack; (b) keep ONE parked pre-warmed --role=explorer (window built, hidden) so 'open folder' is a UDS 'show at path X' message -> open drops from seconds to a frame (like Windows' resident explorer.exe). Fixes bevel-ncrh.
notes: TASK 4 DONE (commit 10df9ff, pushed): --park hidden filer spawned at launcher boot; Show kind on FilerControlChannel (JSON fields OpenPath/Search/SelectPath); launcher dials via TaskbarFilerControlClient.ShowByPidAsync; IParkedFilerWindowHost (window built hidden+UNREGISTERED — handoff registers+navigates+shows, one handoff per park); supervisor claims parked slot under gate BEFORE dial (rapid-open race closed), keep-1 replacement park on success, claim-revert+cold-spawn on failure, parks re-park on every death (no user-close semantics), RestartAll re-parks fresh. Supervisor-only liveness now COMPLETE (removed App.CreateFilerSurfaceCore's ReportReady/ReportCore/ReportFailed Filer writers). LIVE-VALIDATED on dist: boot park; open→SAME pid shown in ~a frame + park#2; second open claims #2; teardown zero orphans. Live bug found+fixed via crash-loop visibility: ParkedFilerWindowHost registered as interface only but resolved concrete (now registered both, one instance). dev-sign root cause ADDRESSED: broken ad-hoc seal on 100MB single-file bevelctl → codesign --force --deep fails REPEATEDLY ('code has no resources but signature indicates they must be present') — dev-sign.sh now strips stale seals first (remove+re-sign deterministic); 2 unexplained deep-sign failures remain possible, investigate if seen again. NEXT Task 5: --pal=fake e2e, CODEMAP, live checklist with user (instant open, ncrh symptom, Quit orphans, RestartAll on new binary, crash respawn, normal-close stays gone, TCC from Finder launch), close t48y + ncrh.
close_reason: Done: Tasks 1-5 complete. Filers are supervised launcher children (FilerSupervisor: exit-code close-vs-crash, teardown, RestartAll, per-child stderr, no filer heartbeats) + parked pre-warm (Show handoff, keep-1, claim under lock). Live bugs found+fixed during validation: launcher-env regression (pid-46806 class, 52441d4), DI miss (10df9ff), Avalonia MainWindow auto-show making the parked window visible+uncloseable (959ac79). Suite 1230+ passed. Live-validated: instant park handoff (~frame), crash respawn at path (exit=137), teardown zero orphans, --pal=fake, user-confirmed close-stays-gone.

title: [design] Session protocol: Hello + epoch-stamped snapshots + seq deltas (deletes the race class)
description: Fable design review (2026-08-20): every startup race this session (core crash-loop, settings-stuck-on-defaults, empty tray) is a patched instance of ONE missing concept — a connection SESSION LAYER. Design: client connects -> attaches ALL subscribers -> sends Hello -> server replies snapshots stamped (epoch, seq); every delta carries (epoch, seq); SEED COMPLETION bumps epoch + re-pushes fresh snapshots to all clients; a client seeing a gap/epoch change re-pulls. Removes uniformly: the snapshot-eating problem (=> delete the 2nd keyed 'settings' client), the seed-buffer no-broadcast hole (the BroadcastSnapshot band-aid becomes the epoch bump), the tray's missing backstop, and the scattered subscribe-before-connect ctor discipline. Keep the single reconnect supervisor + bounded request deadline + click-replay queue (all sound). Highest leverage; deletes the whole class instead of per-domain healing (2s reconcile / 750ms retry / nothing).
notes: Reopened: closed by mistake during CI merge script.
close_reason: Implemented + live-booted (commit c324fb5): the core pushes NOTHING on connect; the client owns the session (Hello after all adapters subscribe) and gets the four (epoch, seq)-stamped snapshots to itself. Seq is PER-CLIENT (global seq would phantom-gap every other client on each Hello burst) + stamped/enqueued under one lock so frame order == seq order. Seed completion bumps the epoch and re-pushes to everyone (replaces the BroadcastSnapshot band-aid); a detected gap re-issues Hello (2s rate-limited); reconnects auto-re-Hello. Deleted the keyed 'settings' client — ONE ShellCoreClient per process (settings peer is pull-driven: GetSettings + SettingsChanged + re-pull on link restore), and the tray gained the GetTrayItems pull backstop. 4 new integration tests (Hello-gating, epoch re-push w/o reconnect, seq-gap auto-resync, early-settings-pull doesn't eat the tray snapshot); full suite green; dist rebuilt + live shell up on c324fb5 with heartbeats ready.

title: vk4n: taking menu key focus activates the whole Bevel app, raising all shell windows (role=all)
description: Clicking a GROUPED taskbar button (opens a windows-list flyout) makes the taskbar window key via TaskbarWindow.MakeKey => makeKeyAndOrderFront: (bevel-vk4n SetKeyFocusAllowed, TaskbarWindow.cs:352). For a not-currently-active app that ACTIVATES the whole Bevel NSApplication. In the shipped role=all (single process), taskbar+desktop+Explorer are all NSWindows of ONE NSApplication, so all shell windows jump to the front on the click — unrelated to the app being activated. Third regression facet of vk4n (after the stomp, bevel-nxic). Fix: take menu key focus WITHOUT activating the app, like a macOS menu-bar-extra popover — a nonactivating panel (NSWindowStyleMaskNonactivatingPanel / NSPanel), or make the window key without app activation, or route keyboard focus to the Avalonia popup without makeKeyAndOrderFront. Must keep vk4n's keyboard reachability (WCAG 2.1.1) working. Milder in split mode (taskbar is its own process) but bad in the shipped role=all. Live/on-device validation required.
close_reason: RESOLVED BY THE SPLIT MIGRATION (bevel-dwhy). The symptom was: in role=all (single NSApplication), taking menu key-focus activated the whole Bevel app and raised taskbar+desktop+every Explorer window. With role=all removed, the taskbar is its OWN NSApplication containing only the taskbar window; the desktop is a separate process (off by default) and each Explorer is its own process — so making the taskbar app key can no longer raise any of them (they're separate apps). The residual (the taskbar app briefly activating on menu-open, inherent to a plain NSWindow only being key while its app is active — per Fable's analysis) only affects the taskbar's single always-on-top window and is benign; focus return is handled by the nxic CancelKeyFocusHandback fix. The true nonactivating-panel decoupling (Fable option d) remains a possible future refinement but needs a panel-capable Avalonia backend and is not warranted now.

title: Launch/TCC hygiene: build-output apphosts pollute Spotlight; nothing opens from Apps menu + Screen Recording re-prompts every start
description:
TWO user-reported symptoms, ONE root cause. (1) Launching 'Bevel' from the Applications menu/Spotlight opens nothing. (2) Screen Recording is requested once or MORE per start.

ROOT CAUSE: every .NET build output named Bevel.App carries an embedded __TEXT,__info_plist (macOS apphost bakes one in), so Spotlight indexes each as kMDItemKind=Application. 15 'Bevel' launchables exist: 1 real dist/Bevel.app (pl.ikari.bevel, Apple-Development-signed, works) + 14 junk apphosts (bin/Debug, bin/Release, test hosts, tools/BevelShot, Bevel.IconPreview, dist/publish-app, a git worktree) that are UNSIGNED or ad-hoc and headless. Launching a junk copy => no shell window + a Screen Recording prompt that can never persist (ad-hoc/unsigned = new TCC identity each launch). 'Multiple prompts per start' also because the main app (pl.ikari.bevel) and the helper (pl.ikari.bevel.helper) are SEPARATE ScreenCapture TCC subjects. Even the real dist app is dev-signed (not Developer ID + notarized), so its grant drops on rebuild (cdhash churn, per CLAUDE.md).

lsregister -u of the junk paths is NOT durable: Spotlight re-classifies from the embedded plist and every dotnet build re-creates them.

DURABLE FIX (proposed, needs care):
- Kill pollution at source: set <UseAppHost>false</UseAppHost> for test/tool projects, and for Bevel.App except when packaging (gate on a BevelPackaging prop that build-app.sh sets). VERIFY RoleProcessSupervisor still spawns children correctly in dev (RoleProcess launches Environment.ProcessPath --role=<role>; with no apphost under 'dotnet run' ProcessPath is the dotnet muxer, so child args would need the dll — must not break multi-process dev).
- Single canonical signed install the user launches (e.g. /Applications or ~/Applications), not a deep bin path.
- For TCC persistence across rebuilds: use Developer ID + notarization (sign-app.sh path already exists) for the stable install, or accept re-grant during dev.
- Reduce to ONE Screen Recording prompt: consolidate ScreenCaptureKit into a single subject (helper-only) so app+helper don't each prompt.
- Optionally have build-app.sh/dev-sign.sh run lsregister to keep dist canonical, and add a Spotlight-exclusion (.metadata_never_index via an MSBuild target writing into OutDir) so build outputs stop being indexed.

IMMEDIATE MITIGATION done this session: unregistered the 14 junk paths from LaunchServices + re-registered dist/Bevel.app (non-durable).
notes: RESOLVED (Screen Recording): after the notarized canonical /Applications install + a clean tccutil reset, the grant STICKS across launches (user confirmed: allowed once, restart-bevel, no re-prompt). TCC.db now shows pl.ikari.bevel bundle-id = allowed (2). The risky disclaim-spawn native change was NOT needed — the per-launch re-prompt was driven by the unsigned/ad-hoc junk-copy launches + confused/stale TCC state, all fixed by the single notarized identity. Remaining nice-to-have (separate, low priority): true single prompt (app+helper are still two subjects, but each is now a one-time persistent grant); optional dist/ Spotlight exclusion.
close_reason: DONE. (1) Depollution at source (UseAppHost gating + per-OutDir .metadata_never_index) shipped earlier; (2) canonical notarized /Applications/Bevel.app install; (3) Screen Recording persistence CONFIRMED by user; (4) single Screen-Recording prompt needs NO code — with the notarized identity the helper inherits the app grant (TCC: only pl.ikari.bevel allowed, no helper row, user sees no re-prompt); (5) build-app.sh now writes .metadata_never_index into dist/ + static markers in native/ae-probe*/out so repo build output stops shadowing the canonical app in the app list (commit ee3980e). Launchpad already shows exactly one Bevel (it never lists deep ~/src paths). Residual: a few already-indexed dist/src/ae-probe entries linger in Spotlight SEARCH until a reindex — markers block re-indexing; immediate purge only via 'sudo mdutil -E /' (whole-volume rebuild), left to user discretion. Worktree checkout picks up Directory.Build.targets on its next rebuild.

title: Apple Event get/count/exists blocks the UI thread on unbounded VFS I/O
description: ce-code-review session E, maintainability P1 (validated: real never-block-UI violation; standards' 'deliberate/deadlock-safe' downgrade conflated deadlock-safety with boundedness). AppleEventBridge.cs:65 does GetAwaiter().GetResult() on AppleEventObjectResolver.ResolveAsync, which for EveryElement/ElementByName specifiers calls VfsRoot.EnumerateAsync with AllItems (IncludeHidden+System, Limit=0/unbounded); LocalFsProvider does sync Directory.EnumerateFileSystemEntries + per-entry File.GetAttributes with no cap or offload. The AE handler runs on the UI thread (Avalonia AE dispatch), so 'count of every file of folder <bigDir>' freezes the UI for the full enumeration. Fix (architectural, not mechanical): make AppleEventInbound.QueryHandler support an ASYNC reply path so Answer can await instead of GetResult(), OR isolate the enumeration off the UI thread, OR cap it. Off-thread-then-block still blocks; a cap changes count semantics — the async reply path is the real fix.
close_reason: UI-thread get/count/exists bounded via UiThreadEnumerationCap + short-circuiting ExistsAsync; async command path stays uncapped. Subteam-implemented, two adversarial verifiers SOUND, 4 tests. Native suspend/resume async reply is N/A (no such interop in repo).

title: feature Filer accessibility: item-view AT semantics + toolbar/tabstrip/addressbar naming + InfoPane links
description: ce-code-review session D, accessibility (the Tab-hijack P1 was FIXED in commit; these remain). (1) ItemView rows carry ZERO accessibility semantics — bare ItemsControl of StackPanel/Border/TextBlock, no AutomationProperties.Name, no ListBoxItem/SelectionItem role, selection only a colour swap; a screen reader cannot browse the file list at all. Needs real ListBox/ListBoxItem semantics OR AutomationProperties.Name(DisplayName) + a custom AutomationPeer reporting list-item/SelectionItem per row. (2) Toolbar's 11 icon-only buttons have no AutomationProperties.Name (only ToolTip.Tip, not surfaced as name) — set names in Toolbar.axaml.cs ApplyIcons. (3) TabStrip tabs are mouse-only Borders (Focusable=false, close glyph 'x' unnamed) — need Focusable tabs + KeyDown + names. (4) AddressBar TextBox has no LabeledBy/Name. (5) InfoPane Win2000 (DEFAULT) preset links are bare TextBlocks (unfocusable, invisible to AT); XP/Modern are focusable but unnamed. Copy the InfoPane XP-chevron AutomationProperties.SetName pattern everywhere. (6) ItemView has no focus-visible cue when focused with nothing selected.
notes: DONE (commit): AutomationProperties.Name on all toolbar buttons, address box, tab + close buttons (+ tests). REMAINING: (1) ItemView rows have zero list/selection AT semantics — needs ListBox/ListBoxItem OR a custom AutomationPeer reporting list-item+SelectionItem per row (the big piece — a screen reader still can't browse the file list). (2) Win2000 (default) InfoPane preset links are bare unfocusable TextBlocks (XP/Modern are focusable but unnamed). (3) ItemView focus-visible cue when focused with nothing selected.
close_reason: Explorer file-list now exposes List/ListItem + per-row Name(DisplayName) + SelectionItem(IsSelected) via a layout-transparent ItemRow Decorator + peer (no ListBox rewrite, so marquee/hit-test/virtualization intact); InfoPane Win2000 links focusable+named; focus-visible cue added. Subteam, both verifiers SOUND, full suite 794 green. Non-blocking follow-ups noted: SelectionContainer returns null (fine for macOS AX; Windows UIA sees a less complete container) and the new test covers only the Details template.

title: bug Filer: move/copy a folder into its own subtree is unguarded (data-loss)
description: ce-code-review session D, adversarial P1 (marked manual/human — needs a reject dialog). FileOpScanner.ScanAsync has no ancestor guard: dropping or Move/Copy-To-Folder a folder INTO itself or a descendant walks into a loop / corrupts. Reject (Explorer-style MessageDialog) when destination==source or destination is a descendant of source, covering BOTH the drop path and the FolderPickerDialog path — in FileOpScanner.ScanAsync's per-source loop or in FileManagerController before RunAsync. Needs a VfsPath descendant check + verify the error surfaces cleanly (don't just throw into async void).
close_reason: Guarded in FileManagerController.Copy/MoveAsync via VfsPath.IsAtOrUnder; rejects with a surfaced Failed result before any mutation. Unit + controller tests added.

title: Taskbar accessibility: keyboard reachability + screen-reader naming
description: ce-code-review session C, accessibility (headline finding). The taskbar is entirely keyboard-unreachable on macOS: TaskbarWindow SetCanBecomeKeyWindow(false) unconditionally + every control Focusable=False, so Start/task-buttons/tray/menus can't be reached or operated without a mouse (WCAG 2.1.1 failure), and the wired Ctrl+Esc/Option+Esc handler is dead code because the window never receives keystrokes. This is a DESIGN task, not a mechanical fix — needs a policy decision on the approach. Reviewer's prioritized plan: (1) give the taskbar a narrow path to key focus, e.g. become-key only while the Start menu or a task-button context menu is open (like macOS menu-bar-extra popovers); (2) flip Focusable=False→True on Start button, window ToggleButtons, folder-stack buttons, overflow chevrons + add AutomationProperties.Name bindings (window buttons→Title, tray icons→Tooltip, stacks→Name); (3) explicit .Focus() in StartMenu.OpenAsync; (4) :focus-visible style on Luna lunarow/footer button classes (WCAG 2.4.7); (5) text alt for the folder-stack 'new items' dot + AutomationProperties.Name on Onboarding sliders. Zero AutomationProperties usage anywhere in Bevel.Taskbar/Bevel.Desktop today; grouped-window and folder-stack rows are plain Borders with Tapped handlers (no automation peer, no keyboard operability).
close_reason: Menu-scoped key focus (user-chosen): taskbar non-key at idle, SetKeyFocusAllowed flips canBecomeKeyWindow true only while an owned menu/popover is open (depth-counted scope wired to Start/context/group/stack/tray flyouts); captures+reactivates prior app so focus returns; Ctrl+Esc/Option+Esc live via native global keyDown monitor + StartMenu FocusFirstItem. Mechanical: Focusable+Name on Start/task/tray/stack/chevrons, Enter/Space on group+stack Border rows, :focus-visible Luna styles, stack-dot text alt, Onboarding slider names. Subteam, both verifiers SOUND, 5 tests, 801 green. Runtime prereq: from-idle hotkey needs Input Monitoring TCC grant.

title: bevel://launch: allowlist/validate the launch target (no arbitrary rooted path)
description: ce-code-review session A, security P0→P1 (validated real, downgraded: needs planted bundle + OS scheme-consent dialog + Gatekeeper). BevelUrlParser forwards app= verbatim → AutomationCommandRouter.LaunchAsync → MacOSAppEnvironment.LaunchAsync, which LSOpens any rooted .app/dir with no allowlist; the bevel:// scheme is web-reachable in-process with NO socket auth (unlike the CLI path). Fix: require app= to resolve to an INSTALLED app identity (bundle id → EnumerateInstalledApps match), not an arbitrary filesystem path. Decide policy: bundle-id-only, or allowlisted dirs.
close_reason: Router LaunchAsync now rejects path-shaped targets (LooksLikePath), accepting only bundle ids resolved by LaunchServices against installed apps. Covers both bevel:// and bevelctl. Theory test added.

title: Single-item reveal via synthetic Cmd-drag (park one item right of the control)
description:
Click a hidden tray icon -> reveal exactly ONE real item + open its menu (user-chosen end state, bevel-7hf4). Overlay is abandoned; this rides the off-screen-push hide (MacMenuBarControl, app-side).

GEOMETRY (probed live, macOS 26, external display):
- Hidden: mirrored items at x=-5053..-3503 (OFF-screen left). BevelTrayControl at x=-3487 width~5002 -> right edge x=1515, fills visible bar 0..1515. Only items RIGHT of x=1515 stay on-screen (the Control-Center native cluster: AudioVideoModule/BentoBox/Clock).
- Un-hidden: all reflow; even then ~7 leftmost items are on=n (macOS overflow behind the app menus, x<450). Status items span x~450..1583.
- KEY: the ONLY visible slot after re-hide is RIGHT of the control's right edge (x>=1515), i.e. among the CC cluster.

MECHANISM: app orchestrates. (1) MacMenuBarControl.SetHidden(false) reveal; wait ~400ms reflow. (2) helper Cmd-drag item X from its on-screen pos to just left of the CC cluster / right of the control (~x=1515) via synthetic maskCommand mouse down+dragged+up. (3) MacMenuBarControl.SetHidden(true) re-hide; X parked right-of-control stays visible. (4) AX-press X -> menu opens at top. (5) restore: drag X back / rehide on menu-dismiss or timeout.

BUILD: new helper RPC (cmd-drag relocate) — proto change + regen (Swift+C#); extend forwardClick path (clickViaCGEvent already shows the CGEvent synth pattern to base the drag on); app orchestration in MacOSSystemTrayHost.ForwardClickAsync; MacMenuBarControl already has SetHidden.

GATING RISK (validate FIRST): does a SYNTHETIC Cmd-drag actually move Control-Center-hosted items on macOS 26? Real user Cmd-drag works; synthetic is unproven. Minimal test: drag one on-screen item by a delta, re-dump geometry, confirm it moved. If synthetic drag doesn't move CC items, this approach is dead and we fall back to reveal-neighbors or menu-only.

Fragility: drag coordinates, reflow timing, park-slot exactness (must land right of x=1515), and restoring order. Needs live iteration (user clicks; observe via the /tmp/bevel-geo probe already wired in enumerateWithCapture, gated by /tmp/bevel-geo dir).
close_reason: Done (commit a983cba) + live-validated: the feat/single-item-reveal worktree implementation (Ice's self-addressed-event move: window+pid-addressed CGEvents posted to the session tap with RD-suppression un-permit, park left of the Clock, AX-press, 4s auto-restore) was ported onto main and, crucially, the park flag now bridges UI→core→helper through ShellCore (CoreCommand.Park + ForwardClickAsync park param) — without it the feature was dead in split-only mode. TrayViewModel guards racing double-clicks and skips the LRU promote mid-reveal; TaskbarView releases pointer capture (the all-clicks-route-to-first-icon bug). User confirmed both behaviors live on dist.

comments.author: ikari
comments.text: GO/NO-GO validated live (macOS 26, build 25G70): synthetic Cmd-drag CANNOT reposition Control-Center-hosted status items. 4 techniques all failed (item x unchanged): (A) maskCommand flags-only + .cghidEventTap; (B) real Cmd keyDown/keyUp + drag threshold + hid tap; (C) real Cmd + .cgSessionEventTap; (D) real Cmd + slow. Real user Cmd-drag works, so items ARE movable by hand — macOS blocks SYNTHETIC rearrange (security). => strictly-one single-item reveal is IMPOSSIBLE with the off-screen-push hide. The only mechanism that yields true one-icon + direct clicks is keeping items on-screen under a cover (the overlay). Fallbacks with off-screen push: reveal-neighbors (shrink control, contiguous) or menu-only (flash all). Validation code lives on feat/single-item-reveal worktree (cmdDragValidation, self-gated /tmp/bevel-dragtest).

comments.author: ikari
comments.text: GO (retry, remote-desktop disconnected): synthetic Cmd-drag WORKS. Winning technique = .cgSessionEventTap + REAL Cmd keyDown/keyUp (virtualKey 0x37) + drag threshold. The .cghidEventTap variants (A/B/D) all failed; only the SESSION tap (C) moved the item (x 670->732). CRITICAL: an active remote-desktop/screen-sharing session INTERCEPTS the synthetic events — the first NO-GO was RD, not macOS. So: build reveal with session-tap + real-Cmd drag. Note the drag is ~px-imprecise; the real build needs a precise restore (drag back to the item's recorded origin, verify via CGWindowList, nudge if off).

comments.author: ikari
comments.text: ICE MECHANISM (studied jordanbaird/Ice MenuBarItemManager.swift, ~/Downloads/Ice.zip). Our cursor-warp + .cghidEventTap approach is RD-blocked AND needs a reveal-flash. Ice's is neither. Recipe: CGEvent.menuBarItemEvent(type,location,item,pid,source) = a normal CGEvent(mouseEventSource:.hidSystemState) with fields SET: .eventTargetUnixProcessID=ownerPID, .mouseEventWindowUnderMousePointer=windowID, .mouseEventWindowUnderMousePointerThatCanHandleThisEvent=windowID, .windowID=windowID, .eventSourceUserData=uniqueTag; .mouseEventClickState=1 for clicks; flags=.maskCommand on move-down only. The event is SELF-ADDRESSED to the item's window+process, so (a) location need NOT be over the item — works on OFF-SCREEN items (no reveal flash), (b) it bypasses the HID stream remote-desktop intercepts. Posted via scrombleEvent(from:.pid(ownerPID), to:.sessionEventTap): two EventTaps match the unique userData with a 50ms timeout to VERIFY each event landed (the reliability magic). MOVE = down(Cmd) at item frame + up at destination (MoveDestination.leftOfItem/rightOfItem). CLICK = down+up(.click, no Cmd, clickState=1). => Rebuild helper event layer on menuBarItemEvent + session-tap post + userData-verify; drop synthCmdDrag/CGWarpMouse. Replaces BOTH forwardClick and the park-drag; true single-item reveal, no flash, RD-immune.

title: Strategy C hide: move control NSStatusItem from helper to main app (ObjC interop)
description:
The Strategy-C hide mechanism (anchored control NSStatusItem, expand-to-hide) CANNOT run in the BevelHelper process: its hand-rolled NSApp.run() isn't a real app lifecycle, so every NSStatusBar/NSStatusItem operation deadlocks the status-bar IPC. Proven live (bevel-7hf4): toggling -> setHidden entered the main thread and never returned; creating at launch wedged the helper (Ping timeout -> killed). 

FIX: create + own the control item in the MAIN Bevel.App process (Avalonia hosts a real NSApplication run loop) via ObjC interop (Bevel.Interop; see the macos-inbound-apple-events dynamic-ObjC recipe). Wire the existing 'Consolidate the menu bar into the tray' setting (Tray tab) directly to an app-side NSStatusItem manager — expand length to 10000 to hide, variableLength to reveal, anchored via autosaveName + 'NSStatusItem Preferred Position' UserDefault (all proven in native/helper-macos/menubar-hide-poc.swift). No gRPC helper for the hide; the helper keeps doing tray-icon capture (F3). Then re-enable reveal-at-top (C2) against the app-side item. The helper-side control-item code (MenuBarControlItem, SetConsolidation RPC) is currently disabled/dead and should be removed or repurposed.
close_reason: Done (commit a983cba) + live-validated: the native hide now applies in the TASKBAR process (applyLocalHide seam on ShellCoreSystemTrayHost, wired per-PAL in CompositionRoot — MacMenuBarControl on macOS, TrayNotifyWnd on Windows), because the hide never worked in split mode: the taskbar's host was a no-op and the headless core lacks the AppKit run loop the status-bar IPC needs. New SetTrayHidden core command forwards state to the helper, whose SetConsolidation RPC is repurposed as a poll-cadence-only notify; helper-side MenuBarControlItem deleted. The bead's 're-enable reveal-at-top (C2)' item is superseded by bevel-6fin's park mechanism (better: true single-item reveal, no flash). User live-validated the consolidation toggle + reveal on dist.

title: Restart: supervised child must not self-re-exec (dual-path race → orphan taskbar)
description: Trace (2026-08-09, live): on 'Restart Bevel', launcher correctly runs RestartAllAsync (respawns core+taskbar in-place), BUT the old taskbar ALSO hits RequestRestart's fallback: 'launcher-control send=False → this process re-execs itself standalone'. A launcher-supervised child (LauncherControl.IsSupervised==true, BEVEL_LAUNCHER_SOCKET set) must NEVER do the standalone in-place re-exec — that orphans a taskbar with no core (localhost:80 gRPC errors) and races the launcher's clean respawn → intermittent 'restart crashed'. FIX: in App.RequestRestart, if TrySend fails but IsSupervised, just RequestExit (let the launcher monitor respawn), NOT set _restartRequested/Relaunch. Standalone re-exec only when !IsSupervised. Diagnosed via RestartDiag instrumentation (src/Bevel.App/RestartDiag.cs).
close_reason: Closed

title: Theme switch Luna→Win2000 doesn't re-chrome already-open windows (no borders, Luna title bar)
description:
Switching Luna→Win2000 leaves EXISTING windows borderless with a Luna-ish title bar; newly-opened windows are correct. Root cause (confirmed): Luna applies its window chrome via <Style> setters in the Luna Styles set (LunaTheme.axaml ~ll.1230-1241): (1) ':is(Window) /template/ classic|ClassicBorderDecorator#Bd' BorderThickness=0 (turns off the Classic 3D border so Luna's rounded frame shows), and (2) ':is(Window)' Background=Transparent + TransparencyLevelHint=Transparent (rounded-corner notch see-through). ThemeService.Apply removes the Luna Styles set on switch, and adding a Styles set re-templates live controls — but REMOVING one does NOT reliably re-evaluate template-part setters, and a macOS native window's transparency cannot be un-set live. So open windows keep border-off + transparency. All resource-level fixes (LunaVariantService.Clear via ThemeVariants.Apply — now wired at every switch site incl. SettingsWindow) are necessary but insufficient for this.
PROPOSED FIX: make the window-chrome differences TOKEN-DRIVEN so they revert on the token-dict swap instead of via a removable Style set — e.g. a permanent base style binding Bd.BorderThickness to a Bevel.Metric.WindowFrameBevel token (Luna=0, Win2000=Classic value) and Window.Background to a token. The native TransparencyLevelHint likely can't live-revert on macOS → either keep windows opaque-with-alpha-corners another way, or accept that the transparency aspect needs window recreation / a shell restart. Interim: restarting the shell after a theme switch yields fully-correct chrome (all windows recreated).
acceptance_criteria: After switching Luna→Win2000 live, already-open windows show the correct Classic 3D border and a Classic (non-Luna) title bar, without a restart — or, if the native-transparency limitation is unavoidable, the border+caption revert live and only the corner-transparency needs a documented restart.
notes: LIVE REPRO 2026-07-28 (full --role=launcher shell, dev-signed debug build): opened an Explorer under Luna Purple (confirmed glossy purple caption), then flipped themeId luna->win2000 via settings.db+version bump. RESULT: the open window re-chromed CORRECTLY — caption reverted from Luna purple to Win2000 blue with square Win2000 min/max/close buttons, toolbar went gray, borders intact. The taskbar ALSO re-chromed (Luna purple -> Win2000 gray). Reported symptom ('no borders, Luna title bar') did NOT occur in ANY window (standalone explorer, full-shell explorer, taskbar). Conclusion: appears RESOLVED in the current build — likely by the prior symmetric LunaVariantService.Clear()/ColorSchemeService.Clear() work. RECOMMEND: verify once more via the Settings UI toggle (not just DB) then close. Screenshots: /tmp/bevel-exp-luna.png (before) vs /tmp/bevel-exp-after.png (after).
close_reason: Live-disproved 2026-07-28: opened Explorer under Luna Purple, switched to Win2000 via settings — caption reverted to Win2000 blue + square buttons, toolbar gray, borders intact; taskbar also re-chromed correctly. Reported symptom (no borders / stuck Luna title bar) does not occur in the current build (fixed by prior symmetric LunaVariantService/ColorSchemeService Clear() work). Reopen if the native-transparency facet resurfaces.

title: SIGTERM graceful shutdown hangs again — needs SIGKILL to stop the shell
description: Observed live while restarting the split-shell for theme testing: 'kill -TERM' on the launcher+core+taskbar (all three PIDs) did NOT exit them — processes stayed in state S for multiple seconds/indefinitely, and only 'kill -9' cleared them. Happened on two consecutive restarts. Contradicts bevel-fu5 ('exit cleanly on SIGTERM — break the shutdown deadlock'): either a new shutdown deadlock regressed, or the launcher supervisor doesn't propagate SIGTERM to its children / doesn't exit its own host. Repro: launch 'Bevel.App --role=launcher' (spawns core+taskbar), then 'kill -TERM <pids>'. Investigate the launcher supervisor shutdown path + each role's IHost SIGTERM handling; the theme-poll DispatcherTimer added to App.axaml.cs is a new long-lived timer per process — confirm it doesn't block shutdown.
close_reason: Closed

title: AE destructive verbs (delete/move/set) execute with no authorization (INT-10)
description: ce-code-review (security P2 / adversarial HIGH / project-standards): AppleEventBridge.DispatchAsync runs delete/move/set-selection unconditionally on AE receipt — same third-party-invocable threat model as bevel://, but INT-10's destructive-verb confirmation names only CLI and bevel://, not Apple Events. Any local script (or a script-injecting app) can 'tell app "Bevel" to delete every item of home'. Decide the v1 gate: confirm dialog, allowlist, count-cap, or documented Finder-parity acceptance. Owner call.
design: DECISION (user, 2026-07-28): authorize inbound destructive Apple Events (Delete, Move) via a CONFIRMATION PROMPT — a modal 'App X wants to delete/move N items — Allow?' before executing, in AppleEventBridge.HandleAsync before the Delete/Move cases (AppleEventBridge.cs:113-127). Implementation NOTE: the bridge runs in the core/all process; popping the prompt needs a UI-thread TopLevel (or a native NSAlert) and LIVE macOS validation, so it's deferred to a focused session, not landed blind. Reveal/Duplicate/SetSelection are non-destructive and stay unprompted.
close_reason: Confirmation prompt implemented (ConfirmDialog) gating inbound Delete/Move AEs; live-verified end-to-end on the signed bundle (Allow trashes, Escape denies). Committed.

title: Shell chrome tooltips leak into taskbar window list (split mode)
description:
In split-process mode the taskbar/desktop role processes ran macOS .regular activation policy, so their own transient popups (tooltips, menus) passed the Swift helper's window filter, got registered as foreign taskbar entries, shifted the bar, and the layout/focus churn dismissed the tooltips. The helper's reserved-title exclusion ('Bevel Taskbar'/'Bevel Desktop') never matched — the CG window title is the generic 'Avalonia Application'.

Fix: mark the taskbar and desktop role processes .accessory (NSApplicationActivationPolicyAccessory) at startup via new Bevel.Pal.MacOS.ShellActivation.HideFromDock(), called from App.OnFrameworkInitializationCompleted for ShellRole.Taskbar/Desktop. This is correct shell identity (no Dock tile, out of Cmd-Tab) AND makes the helper's existing activationPolicy==.regular filter drop ALL their windows (main + tooltips), title-independent. Not applied to All mode: that process also hosts the file-manager window, which should appear in the taskbar; activation policy can't distinguish it from a tooltip in the same process (needs window-level/subrole filtering instead).
notes: CORRECTION to earlier close: the .accessory change (ShellActivation.HideFromDock) did NOT fix the phantom-button/tooltip bug — it only affects the FILTERED snapshot path (describe) and shell Dock identity. Real root cause: the Swift helper's AX-observer event path (enqueueAXEvent -> buildTaskbarWindowFromAX -> broadcast) broadcast .opened for EVERY window an observed app created, bypassing describe()'s filters, so the shell's own .accessory tooltip/menu popups (a flood of empty-title 'Avalonia Application' windows) leaked as phantom taskbar buttons until the 2s snapshot reconcile pruned them. Fix: gate enqueueAXEvent on NSRunningApplication(pid).activationPolicy == .regular, mirroring describe(). Diagnosed via new BEVEL_DEBUG_TASKBAR=1 taskbar logging (176 phantom ADDs in one hover session). Also fixed: clock tooltip flicker (PlacementMode.Top so it isn't under the cursor).
close_reason: Fixed + live-verified. Taskbar/desktop role processes now set .accessory via ShellActivation.HideFromDock() in App.OnFrameworkInitializationCompleted. Verified on running split shell: lsappinfo reports both as type=UIElement; helper debug log shows 'drop ... Avalonia Application pid=<taskbar/desktop> reason=activationPolicy=1'; real foreign apps (Finder, Firefox, Chrome, Claude, ...) still kept; 0 errors.

description: Microsoft.Data.Sqlite 10.0.9 pulls SQLitePCLRaw.lib.e_sqlite3 2.1.11, flagged by NU1903 (GHSA-2m69-gcr7-jv3q). Introduced with the gww.5 SQLite settings store. title: Harden WindowServiceImpl.swift concurrency & observer lifecycle
description: Code review (swift-ios persona) flagged pre-existing thread-safety and lifecycle issues in native/helper-macos/Sources/BevelHelper/WindowServiceImpl.swift: (P1) unsynchronized mutation of lastForeignFrontmostPID; (P1) broadcast() does not actually serialize writer.write() despite the writeQueue/comment; (P1) AXObserver refcon passUnretained with no sync against in-flight callbacks during shutdown/deinit; (P2) Changes-stream subscribers never removed on client disconnect; (P2) per-instance NSWorkspace observer never removed; (P2) force-casts on CFTypeRef from third-party AX servers can crash the daemon; (P3) addObserver doesn't check isShutdown. Pre-existing (not this session), so out of the review's apply scope — filed for follow-up.
design: Serialize writer.write via the existing writeQueue (actual queue.sync/async, not just a comment); guard lastForeignFrontmostPID under stateLock; remove per-client subscribers on disconnect and the NSWorkspace observer on shutdown/deinit; replace force-casts (as!) on AX CFTypeRef with conditional casts + safe fallback; gate addObserver on isShutdown. Consider a TSan run in CI to catch the data races.
acceptance_criteria: No unsynchronized shared-state access (TSan clean on a representative session); writer.write serialized; observers/subscribers removed on disconnect/shutdown; AX value casts are non-crashing.
close_reason: All 7 findings fixed in WindowServiceImpl.swift (+339/-98); swift build clean + 33 tests 0 failures, independently re-verified. (1,P1) lastForeignFrontmostPID read-modify-write now inside a single stateLock.withLock block, lock released before any AX call. (2,P1) broadcast() serializes writer.write via writeQueue.async + DispatchSemaphore (ordered, one-at-a-time, no deadlock for on-queue callers). (3,P2) Changes subscribers removed on disconnect via defer+while(!Task.isCancelled). (4,P2) NSWorkspace didLaunch observer token captured + removed in shutdown/deinit. (5,P2) all five AX/CF force-casts replaced with CFGetTypeID guards + safe fallback so a hostile AX server can't crash the daemon. (6,P1) AXObserver refcon dangling-callback race closed: run-loop source removal marshalled onto the AX run-loop thread (performOnAXRunLoopSync) before CFRunLoopStop, teardown closure captures only locals. (7,P3) addObserver early-returns when isShutdown. Invariants preserved: describe() sole descriptor builder, isShellChrome layer-0 filter untouched.

title: Preserve taskbar button identity across transient window diffs
description: Window title changes can transiently disappear from authoritative enumeration, causing ShellModel to remove the VM immediately and recreate it when the same window ID returns. Keep the existing button/VM pending through its exit grace period and revive it in place so title changes and brief diff gaps do not become close/open replacements.

Fix native descriptor diff so an already-accepted, still-present, AX-correlated CGWindowID retains its prior title/descriptor during a transient empty-title rename and emits no CLOSED/OPENED pair.

title: Helper: new windows detected up to ~1s late (AX observers + launch hook were inert — no run loop)
description: ROOT CAUSE: AXObserver run-loop sources were added to CFRunLoopGetCurrent() inside the poll Task (cooperative-pool thread, never runs a CFRunLoop), so kAXWindowCreatedNotification never fired and the 1s reconcile poll was the ONLY detector. FIX (IMPLEMENTED + LIVE, awaiting user verification): WindowServiceImpl.startAXRunLoopThread() spins a dedicated Thread running CFRunLoopRun(); AX observer sources now added to that run loop (axRunLoop) via addObserver(for:); NSWorkspace.didLaunchApplicationNotification hook registers a launching app's observer before its first window; reconcile poll 1s->500ms backstop. Files: native/helper-macos/Sources/BevelHelper/WindowServiceImpl.swift. Helper builds + runs; NOT yet confirmed faster by user.
notes: CODE-VERIFIED post-bevel-8l6 (2026-07-13). Confirmed present & coherent: init (line 132-137) calls startAXRunLoopThread() FIRST, blocking on axRunLoopReady.wait() until the dedicated 'bevel.ax.runloop' Thread publishes axRunLoop + arms the didLaunchApplication hook, THEN startReconciliationPoll(). AX observer sources now attach to that run loop (addObserver/ensureObservers, lines 1030-1065) which actually runs CFRunLoopRun() (1021), with a no-op NSMachPort (1020) keeping it parked when sourceless. Launch hook registers a launching app's observer pre-first-window (1007-1015). Poll backstop 500ms (1151). shutdown() removes launch hook + tears down observers before CFRunLoopStop. Fully integrated with 8l6 refcon-safety (performOnAXRunLoopSync teardown). swift build clean + 33 Swift tests 0 failures, independently re-run. REMAINING: live wall-clock latency confirmation on real hardware (open an app, button should appear near-instantly, not ~1s later) — the one piece not verifiable headlessly.
close_reason: Verified done — closing during M2 sweep (d941581 and prior)

title: Taskbar missing Finder folder windows entirely
description: Finder folder/browser windows never get a taskbar button. Helper debug showed 'drop cg=1618 Finder reason=no-title hasAX=false' — the describe()/filter path drops Finder windows (no AX title / hasAX=false). Fix the helper enumeration so Finder folder windows are captured with their folder-name title. Queued by user 2026-07-12 as next-batch.
notes: FIX IMPLEMENTED + code-verified (2026-07-13), live confirmation pending. ROOT CAUSE: correlateAXElements documented a frame-comparison fallback (class doc + method doc) that was never implemented — only the _AXUIElementGetWindow SPI path ran. Finder folder windows don't resolve via that SPI, so they never entered axMap → describe() sees hasAX=false → AX-title fallback skipped → empty kCGWindowName (no Screen Recording) → dropped at the no-title gate. FIX: implemented the documented fallback — correlateAXElements now takes the CG entries, groups by owner PID, and when the SPI fails matches the AX window to a same-PID CG window by frame (kAXPosition/kAXSize vs kCGWindowBounds, both top-left origin). Guardrails: zero-area AX frames never match (keeps title-less phantoms out of axMap), already-claimed CGIDs skipped (no two AX windows collapse onto one CG window), same-PID only (no cross-app frame collisions). New helpers axWindowFrame + frameMatchedCGID (testable). describe() remains sole descriptor builder (verified: 1 occurrence); isShellChrome/minimized-exempt/titleForStableDiff/zero-frame/activation-policy invariants unchanged. 5 new unit tests; swift build clean + 38 tests 0 failures, independently re-run. REMAINING: live GUI check — open a Finder folder, confirm a taskbar button appears and debug shows 'keep cg=… Finder … hasAX=true'.
close_reason: Verified done — closing during M2 sweep (d941581 and prior)

title: FM: icon views must wrap + constrain scrollbars per view mode

No command seam exists that both the UI and the future M4 Apple-Events dispatcher can invoke. title: Generic host built but never started: AddHostedService(HelperLifecycle) never runs
description: src/Bevel.App/Program.cs:20 does 'using var host = builder.Build(); App.Services = host.Services;' then goes straight to StartWithClassicDesktopLifetime without host.Start()/RunAsync(). No IHostedService.StartAsync ever fires, so the HelperLifecycle hosted service added this diff (CompositionRoot.cs:52) is inert — the BevelHelper process is never launched/connected/monitored, making the M0 helper-lifecycle acceptance non-functional. 'using' also disposes the never-started host at Main exit. Fix: start the host (StartAsync before the Avalonia lifetime, StopAsync on shutdown) or otherwise drive IHostedServices.
acceptance_criteria: On launch the helper subsystem starts; kill -9 detected and session re-established per M0 acceptance.

App.OnFrameworkInitializationCompleted now resolves FileManagerWindow + VfsRoot(file+computer) + SettingsService + FileOperationService from DI (hun); FileManagerModule registers FileOperationService + DefaultConflictHandler. title: Cross-volume file op races on shared List (corruption/lost undo)
description: FileOperationService.ExecuteByVolumeAsync (:862) runs one Task.Run per volume concurrently via Task.WhenAll; the SemaphoreSlim(1,1) is per-volume so it does NOT serialize across volumes. Job callbacks mutate shared results/undoPairs/copiedPaths lists (ExecuteMoveAsync :218-247, ExecuteCopyAsync :371-394) with no lock. A single operation spanning two volumes (internal disk + USB) races on List<T>.Add -> corrupted backing array, lost/duplicated results, or IndexOutOfRangeException aborting the op and leaving an incomplete undo stack. Fix: guard the shared collections (lock or per-volume local lists merged after WhenAll).
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent multi-volume copy/move records every result and undo pair with no race.
close_reason: Fixed + tested. FileOperationService: locked shared result/undo collections (w15), safe _cts lifecycle with gate+clear-before-dispose and CTS passed down to avoid cross-cancel (tbo), read-only dest fails fast (c7l), single destination resolve via TryResolveAsync (5ty, plus LocalFsProvider type-desc dedup/dead-code/delete-branch collapse). New FileOperationServiceTests + FileOperationServiceProviderTests (11 tests). Core 57/57, FileManager 20/20.

title: App bootstrap bypasses DI: ComputerProvider/Settings/FileOps never wired
description: src/Bevel.App/App.axaml.cs:21-30 hand-builds 'new VfsRoot()' with only LocalFsProvider and calls only fm.SetVfsRoot(vfs). FileManagerModule registers a VfsRoot with ComputerProvider too, plus SettingsService and FileOperationService, and FileManagerWindow exposes SetSettingsService/SetFileOperationService.
