title: NetMQ is not NativeAOT-compatible on Windows (AsyncIO delegate marshalling) and the publish is silent about it
description:
Measured 2026-10-03 on Win11 Pro 26300, NetMQ 4.0.4.3, net10.0, win-x64, as the Task 1 gate of bevel-aqr7.

A NativeAOT publish (-p:BevelPublishAot=true) SUCCEEDS WITH ZERO WARNINGS. The published binary then throws at the FIRST socket bind:

  System.NotSupportedException: 'AsyncIO.Windows.AcceptExDelegate' is missing delegate marshalling data.
    at RuntimeInteropData.GetForwardDelegateCreationStub(RuntimeTypeHandle)
    at PInvokeMarshal.GetDelegateForFunctionPointer(IntPtr, RuntimeTypeHandle)
    at AsyncIO.Windows.Socket.LoadDynamicMethod[T](Guid)
    at AsyncIO.Windows.Socket.Listener..ctor(Socket)
    at AsyncIO.Windows.Socket.Listen(Int32)
    at NetMQ.Core.Transports.Tcp.TcpListener.SetAddress(String)
    at NetMQ.Core.SocketBase.BindRandomPort(String)

ROOT CAUSE: AsyncIO (NetMQ's transitive dependency) resolves Winsock extension functions - AcceptEx, and by the same mechanism ConnectEx etc. - by GUID at runtime through WSAIoctl, then wraps the returned function pointer with GetDelegateForFunctionPointer. NativeAOT cannot generate forward-delegate marshalling stubs for a type it never saw statically, and emits no warning because nothing is statically wrong.

Confirmed AOT-specific: the identical code as a framework-dependent Release build on the same machine prints 'bus-selftest: ok'.

THE TRANSFERABLE LESSON, which is the reason this bead exists: a clean AOT publish is NOT evidence that a dependency works under AOT. Only RUNNING the published binary caught this. Any future AOT gate must execute the binary, not just build it.
acceptance_criteria: The component-bus transport decision is re-made with this constraint known, and whichever path is chosen, any AOT gate in the project RUNS the published binary rather than only building it.
notes:
OPTIONS, with costs, for whoever re-decides the component-bus transport (bevel-aqr7 Task 1 is BLOCKED on this):

1. Keep AOT, drop NetMQ -> use the existing Bevel.ShellCore.Ipc AF_UNIX transport (BCL-only, already works on Windows 10+ via AddressFamily.Unix under a user-only-ACL dir, and AOT-clean). Cost: hand-roll the pub/sub fan-out ZeroMQ gives for free. This was the original recommendation that NetMQ was chosen over.
2. Keep NetMQ, defer AOT. CHEAPER THAN IT LOOKS: BevelPublishAot appears in NO CI workflow, NO packaging script and NO release pipeline - it is an opt-in aspiration (bevel-gww.7), and bevel-gww.9 is still open ('convert 3 code-behind reflection Bindings'), so AOT is already not reachable today for unrelated reasons. NetMQ would add a second blocker to a target that has one. Cost: the single-binary/no-JIT goal recedes further.
3. Keep both - fork or patch AsyncIO to use delegate* unmanaged<> function pointers instead of GetDelegateForFunctionPointer. Surgical in principle (a handful of Winsock extension lookups) but it means owning a fork of a third-party package.
4. Native libzmq via direct DllImport instead of NetMQ/AsyncIO. DllImport interop is AOT-fine (the Bevel.App.csproj comment says so explicitly), but reintroduces a native dependency to ship, sign and notarize - the bevel-ka6c class of pain.

Also surfaced incidentally, both machine-config only and NOT persisted by the implementer: the global nuget.config has an empty package-source list (every restore needed --source https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json), and vswhere.exe was not on PATH, which the AOT native link step needs.

title: [epic] Windows shell replacement: Bevel replaces Explorer as the shell
description:
THE MISSING ROOT. Two epics (bevel-985s, bevel-7p9r) and seven children are written as 'gated behind shell replacement', but no bead represented shell replacement itself — the de-facto gate was bevel-2t7u, a P3 task still titled 'mirror third-party notification-area icons', whose title stopped describing what it had become. This epic is that root; bevel-2t7u becomes the tray-claim child of it.

PROVEN FEASIBLE, 2026-10-01 on Win11 Pro 26300. The spike (docs/spike/WindowsTrayMirror.cs.spike plus the shell-swap harness) established that the whole loop can be exercised WITHOUT a logout:
  • WM_USER+436 (0x5B4) to Explorer's tray window asks it to exit cleanly, leaving the desktop and the user session intact.
  • RegisterClassEx with class name 'Shell_TrayWnd' then a TaskbarCreated broadcast makes apps re-register.
  • Apps then deliver Shell_NotifyIcon traffic to us over WM_COPYDATA as SHELLTRAYDATA/NOTIFYICONDATA. Measured live: NIM_ADD=4, NIM_MODIFY=1, NIM_DELETE=3.
  • Recovery is 'stop all explorer.exe, start one' — not a reboot.

WHY IT IS AN EPIC AND NOT A TASK. Claiming Shell_TrayWnd is a CONTRACT, not just a privilege. The same WM_COPYDATA channel that delivers NIM_ADD delivers NIM_INFO, and nothing else draws balloons once Explorer is gone. And the spike measured that only 4 of ~9 visible tray items are Shell_NotifyIcon clients at all — the rest (network, volume, input, battery, action centre) are Explorer's OWN shell-drawn XAML with no API to mirror and nothing to forward a click to. So the day we claim the tray we inherit an obligation to DRAW all of it.

ERA NOTE, and the reason the old shell-replacement lore understates this: on Windows 2000/XP, volume, network and battery WERE real Shell_NotifyIcon clients (systray.exe, sndvol32), so a LiteStep-era shell got them free. In the Win10/11 era they became shell-drawn with no registration. The classic playbook does not transfer.

SCOPE OF THE ROOT ITSELF (the mechanics, not the indicators):
  • Clean Explorer handoff and restoration, including crash-heal: if Bevel dies while it is the shell, the user must not be left with no shell.
  • The Shell_TrayWnd claim and WM_COPYDATA ingest (bevel-2t7u).
  • Registering as the shell properly (Winlogon Shell value) vs the per-session claim, and which Bevel supports.
  • The desktop/wallpaper, Alt+Tab, and work-area obligations that move to us — note bevel-514269e already proved Explorer re-asserts the work area instantly, which is why the AppBar ABS_AUTOHIDE + reassert path exists.
  • A safety story: an escape hatch that restores Explorer without a working Bevel UI.
acceptance_criteria: Bevel can take over as the Windows shell and give the session back to Explorer cleanly, without a logout; while it is the shell it receives Shell_NotifyIcon traffic, draws the indicators Explorer used to own, and renders balloon tips; a crash or a forced exit always leaves the user with a working shell.
notes:
SEQUENCING — the opinion this epic exists to record.

DO NOT START bevel-985s.1-.4 YET. Two reasons, in order of force:
  1. They are only needed in shell mode, which does not exist yet.
  2. All four are structurally identical (glyph + state source + flyout), so building them as four more hardcoded blocks in TaskbarView.axaml is precisely the thing bevel-aqr7 exists to stop. bevel-aqr7's own notes make this argument; the dep edge now records it.

CHEAPEST HIGH-INFORMATION ITEM IN THE WHOLE ARC: bevel-7p9r.2, the modern-toast spike. ShellExperienceHost.exe is a SEPARATE process from explorer.exe, so toasts may survive a shell swap entirely untouched — and the answer decides whether a whole toast-rendering surface gets built or whether we merely coexist with one. It is runnable NOW with the harness already written, and it already blocks bevel-7p9r.3. Measure before designing.

HARD OBLIGATION, not a sibling: bevel-7p9r.1 (legacy balloon tips) must ship WITH the tray claim, not after it. An app calling Shell_NotifyIcon with NIF_INFO gets silence otherwise — a regression against both Explorer and every classic shell replacement. The dep edge makes the tray claim unshippable without it.

title: [epic] Taskbar as configurable, generalized components (zones, instances, per-component settings)
description:
The taskbar is currently a fixed XAML layout: Start button, window-button strip, stacks, tray, clock — each hardcoded into TaskbarView.axaml in a fixed order, each with bespoke settings. Every feature request so far has meant editing that one file. That does not scale to the surface Windows 11 actually has (search, task view, widgets, jump lists, pinned apps, toolbars, quick settings), and it does not survive shell-replacement mode, where Bevel must also supply volume, network, input, battery and notifications (bevel-985s, bevel-7p9r).

TARGET: the bar is a COMPOSITION of generalized components, not a layout with holes in it.

A component declares what it is and what it needs; the bar hosts it. Concretely:
- A registry of component types (start, window-strip, stack, tray, clock, search, task-view, pinned-apps, toolbar, indicator-*, …), each self-describing: display name, whether it can appear more than once, its own settings schema, its preferred sizing behaviour (fixed / content / greedy).
- ZONES rather than a fixed order: leading / centre / trailing, with components ordered within a zone. Win11 centres Start and the strip; Win2000 pins them leading. Centred alignment (bevel-9ue) becomes "which zone", not a special case.
- INSTANCES, not singletons: a user can have two folder toolbars, or no clock, or a clock on one display and not another. The existing stacks feature already proves the multi-instance need and currently hardcodes it.
- PER-INSTANCE SETTINGS persisted with the instance, not as a flat pile of Taskbar* keys in BevelSettings. The current settings object has ~20 taskbar keys and grows by several per feature; that is the symptom this fixes.
- VISIBILITY as a first-class per-instance property, so "hide the clock" or "hide the search box" is the same mechanism for every component rather than a bespoke bool each time.

WHY NOW, beyond tidiness: shell-replacement mode turns a handful of optional extras into a list of things Bevel MUST provide, and several of them (volume, network, battery, input) are structurally identical — a glyph, a state source, a flyout. Building them as four more hardcoded blocks would bake the problem in permanently. Building the component model first makes each of them a small, testable unit and gives the user a way to turn off the ones they do not want.

ALSO IN SCOPE: a settings surface for arranging components (add/remove/reorder/configure per zone), and persistence that survives a component type being removed in a later version (unknown component instances must be ignored gracefully, never crash the bar).

DELIBERATELY NOT IN SCOPE: imitating vendor-specific Win11 items with no Bevel meaning — Copilot, the Widgets board, Meet Now, search highlights. The component MODEL should make a third party able to add such things; Bevel itself should not ship them.

CROSS-PLATFORM: the model is platform-neutral; availability is per-platform (a Windows volume indicator has no macOS counterpart because the macOS menu bar owns it). Components declare the capability they need and are simply absent where the PAL reports it unavailable — the existing Capabilities feature-detect contract.
design:
DESIGN DECISIONS (brainstorming session 2026-10-03, user-approved in order).

1. BOUNDARY - public extension point in v1. Components are declared by a MANIFEST, not a C# type, so the contract is authorable by a stranger. Rejected: purely-internal registry (would key persistence on .NET type identity and force a second settings migration later).

2. CONTRACT SHAPE - manifest fields: id (stable reverse-DNS string type-id), contractVersion (bar refuses a future manifest loudly), displayName, multiInstance, sizing (fixed|content|greedy), requiresCapability (PAL feature-detect; component simply absent where unavailable), settingsSchema (self-describing typed fields + defaults + labels + ranges), view (primitive tree).
   - settingsSchema is what kills the three-edits-per-key tax at SettingsService.cs:542/664/932: the arrangement UI renders each editor FROM the schema, so a new component ships zero hand-written settings UI and zero hand-written serialization.
   - id is a stable string, never a type name: instances persist against it, so a component can be renamed/refactored and an unresolvable instance is skipped rather than crashing the bar.

3. RENDERING - hybrid A+B, resolved so that B is a PRIMITIVE and not a parallel mode. A component declares a view tree of Bevel primitives (glyph | label | badge | separator | flyout | surface); surface is a pixel region the component paints itself, backed by MmfBgraPool. Degradation is therefore LOCAL TO THE REGION, not whole-component.
   Mandatory, or the hybrid rots the way bevel-voqo/yduf/sd6n describe:
   a. a surface MUST declare accessible name + role (otherwise every surface is a hole in the UIA/AX tree that TaskbarAccessibilityTests cannot cover);
   b. theme tokens are PUSHED to the component process with a re-paint signal on theme/colourway switch (without this, surfaces go stale on every switch - that is bevel-voqo exactly);
   c. the bar owns layout - a surface declares intrinsic size and honours the scale it is handed, never positions itself.
   Decisive reason the bar must own rendering generally: a themable shell cannot let components ship their own pixels, or "rendered in the skin" stops being true the moment the user switches theme or re-hues a colourway.

4. EXECUTION TIERS - three, one contract. Built-in (start, window-strip, tray, stacks, clock, and all four 985s indicators) run IN the taskbar process, no IPC. Third-party-with-code gets its own supervised process on the component bus. Third-party declarative-only (view bound to state the bar already publishes) gets NO process at all.
   Built-ins go through the IDENTICAL manifest, primitive vocabulary and settings schema, binding a local implementation instead of an IPC one. That dogfooding is what keeps the public door honest: if the contract cannot express Bevel's own clock, it cannot express anyone else's component - and we learn that immediately rather than after shipping. It also means a clock does not cost a process.

5. LAYOUT - option B: ONE ORDERED LIST, spacer is itself a weighted component. No zone abstraction in v1. Centring EMERGES from two equal spacers (flexbox / NSToolbar model), so Win2000 [start, strip(greedy), tray] and Win11 [spacer, start, pins, strip, spacer, tray] are the same model.
   - Rejected A (three fixed zones): the centre zone IS the greedy cell, so its contents anchor to that cell's left edge rather than the bar's centre. True centring needs slack on BOTH sides, which three fixed zones cannot express - bevel-9ue would stay a special case forever.
   - Rejected C (zones for people, spacers for the engine) only for v1: user-facing helpers/wizards that offer leading/centre/trailing buckets are deferred to v2, so v1 carries ONE representation and no zone-to-list projection to keep in sync or test.
   - Consequence closed explicitly: with no zones, a newly added component needs a deterministic home. Rule: APPEND AT END OF LIST, user reorders. No cleverness guessing intent.
   - At most one greedy component per list, validated at load.
   - Instances are { instanceId, typeId, settings }; multiInstance:false enforced at add-time, not assumed.
   - Unknown typeId KEEPS ITS SLOT as an inert placeholder rather than vanishing, so uninstall+reinstall does not silently reshuffle the bar.
   - Dividers stop being chrome: today's StartDivider tracks the Start button's Bounds in code-behind; as a list entry that code goes away. The tray well likewise becomes a component.
   - bevel-9ue (edge position / vertical / centred) and bevel-tjr2 (per-display component sets = just another list) collapse into the model rather than needing their own mechanisms.

6. TRANSPORT - option C: FULL CONSOLIDATION ON NetMQ + protobuf. Two separate buses (internal shell bus, component bus) with separate sockets and separate nonces; gRPC-over-UDS and raw UDS both retire onto NetMQ.
   User chose this against my recommendation of reusing the existing AF_UNIX transport. The finding I raised and they decided against, recorded so it is not re-litigated but IS mitigated:
   - NetMQ has NO ipc:// on Windows (libzmq#3691; zmq_ipc(7)) - it must use tcp://127.0.0.1, which is reachable by every local process and every local user.
   - Bevel ALREADY has AF_UNIX on Windows today with filesystem-permission isolation: UdsMessageClient.cs:78 uses AddressFamily.Unix, and BevelRuntimeDir.cs:11 puts the socket under the user profile's user-only ACL, documented in-repo as "the 0700 equivalent". So C is a step DOWN in isolation on Windows, not sideways.
   REQUIRED MITIGATIONS, now load-bearing rather than defence-in-depth:
   - Handshake.ComputeHmac carries over unchanged (pure function of nonce + capability, transport-agnostic by design) - mandatory on connect, immediate rejection, and NO state disclosed to an unauthenticated peer.
   - Separate nonce per bus, so a component that discovers the internal port still cannot reach the internal bus.
   - Ephemeral random port; port+nonce written to a per-session file with a user-only ACL (the replacement for socket-directory permissions).
   - Connection-flood / rate limiting, since any local process can now attempt connects.
   - Consider ZMQ CURVE on the component bus specifically (the untrusted one).
   - NetMQ must be verified against PublishAot EARLY - BevelPublishAot=true targets a single Mach-O with no JIT, and NetMQ becomes load-bearing. De-risk in sub-project 1, do not discover late.
   SETTLED REGARDLESS: frames NEVER go through any queue - pixels land in MmfBgraPool and the bus carries only "frame N ready in slot K", so transport choice has zero effect on surface throughput. Protobuf toolchain already present (Grpc.Tools 2.70, Google.Protobuf 3.29.3, codegen off proto/).
   SEQUENCING: the Swift helper (native/helper-macos, gRPC-swift) migrates LAST - consolidating it means libzmq as a native Swift dependency to sign and notarize, which is the bevel-ka6c class of pain. It is macOS-only while the component model is Windows-driven, so it must not gate this work.

7. DECOMPOSITION - too large for one spec. (1) contract + registry + ordered-list host + per-instance persistence, with Bevel's own components through the public door from day one; (2) external loading + isolation; (3) arrangement UI; (4) zone helpers/wizards (v2); (5) helper-channel migration. Then the components themselves, already filed as 985s.1-.4 and aqr7.1-.12.

MEASURED BASELINE (2026-10-03): TaskbarView.axaml 563 lines; TaskbarView.axaml.cs 1256 lines; TaskbarViewModel only 128 lines exposing FIVE named properties (Model, ShowDesktopCommand, StartMenu, Tray, Stacks) that the XAML binds by name - that name-binding is the actual coupling to break. Multi-instance already exists exactly once: TaskbarStacks is a string[] feeding StacksViewModel.Stacks, proving the need but giving an instance no settings beyond a bare folder path. 27 of 46 properties on BevelSettings are taskbar keys (59% of the object), each hand-serialized in three places. TrayItemViewModel (Id/Tooltip/IconSource/IsLive, rendered by TrayIconCell) is already a state-only out-of-process component and is the pattern being generalized.

FULL SPEC: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-03-taskbar-components-design.md (sub-project 1 of 5).

LATE FINDINGS from tracing how settings are USED rather than how they are named (user prompt, 2026-10-03). These changed the design, not just its wording:

A. BAR GEOMETRY IS A GLOBAL STATIC FED BY ONE COMPONENT'S SETTING. TaskbarTheme (TaskbarWindow.cs:495) is a public static class holding MUTABLE statics (ButtonHeight, TaskIconSize), Configure()d once from App.axaml.cs:338 with TaskbarButtonSize. RowHeight => ButtonHeight+4; TaskbarHeight => RowHeight+2; HeightForRows(rows) is called in SIX places to pin MinHeight/MaxHeight and also feeds TaskbarGeometry.WorkAreaBand - the work-area strip Bevel reserves from the OS. Breaks three ways under per-instance settings: a static holds one value; a bar may have ZERO window-strip instances; and errors here are user-visible with history (bevel-kbx8, and the work-area claim in 514269e). REQUIRED: an explicit measurement pass - each instance reports its height contribution, the bar composes them, and that single composed height drives BOTH window height and the work-area claim. TaskbarTheme's statics become per-bar computed state, which bevel-tjr2 multi-monitor needs anyway. Re-measure on settings change: App.axaml.cs:375 already records the opposite failure (bevel-kclq, values frozen at Initialize). Precedent for decoupling exists at TaskbarWindow.cs:505 - the tray already escaped the static.

B. A SECOND CONSUMER WAS MISSED. OnboardingWindow.axaml.cs is the "M2 onboarding and settings window", 755 lines, consuming 25 of the 27 keys. The settings tax is paid TWICE: three serialization sites plus a hand-coded settings window. Strengthens the schema-driven-editor case and means sub-project 3 REPLACES most of that window rather than adding to it.

C. THREE MISCLASSIFICATIONS CORRECTED (by-name reading was wrong):
   - TaskbarButtonSize is NOT a plain window-strip setting - it configures the global static behind bar height and the work-area claim, so it is inseparable from the measurement pass.
   - TaskbarStartMenuFrequentCount is NOT a view setting - it feeds shellModel.FrequentCap at App.axaml.cs:309/381/382, the background data model, re-applied on settings.Changed. Making it a Start-instance setting requires the Start menu's DATA pipeline to read per-instance settings.
   - StartBadgeFullDetail is an ordinary per-instance value, not visibility.
   Final split (sums to 27): bar-level-but-computed 3 (Rows, ButtonSize, TrayIconSize); bar-level proper 5 (Locked, AlwaysOnTop, BackgroundColor, Opacity, FontSize); data-layer 1 (StartMenuFrequentCount); window-strip 8; clock 2; start 2; tray 2; visibility 3; multiplicity 1 (Stacks).

D. PRECURSOR (user idea, 2026-10-03): promote the Downloads stack to the FIRST component and deliberately via the THIRD-PARTY route (manifest, own process, component bus), not the easy local-bound path. It already exercises every hard part: multi-instance (string[] today), per-instance runtime state (StackViewModel.cs:276 one PreviewLoader per stack), a real flyout (StackFlyoutView with hover + keyboard), and decoded bitmaps as the natural first `surface`. Proving the PUBLIC path first on a genuinely hard component is what stops the contract growing a privileged shortcut only built-ins can take. If the stack cannot be expressed as a third-party component, the contract is wrong - and we learn that before migrating the clock, strip or tray.
acceptance_criteria: The bar is composed from a component registry with zone placement, multiple instances, per-instance settings and visibility; adding a new taskbar feature means adding a component, not editing the bar layout; users can add, remove, reorder and configure components from settings; unknown persisted components are ignored without breaking the bar.
notes:
RELATED EXISTING BEADS — this epic is the architecture several already-filed features should land on, rather than each editing TaskbarView.axaml again:
- bevel-9ue (edge position / auto-hide / centred alignment): "centred" becomes a zone choice, not a special case.
- bevel-tjr2 (per-Space / multi-monitor taskbars): per-display component sets are a natural extension of per-instance settings — e.g. a clock on one display only.
- bevel-c54t (big icons), bevel-m2.10.x (button display modes): sizing tiers belong to the window-strip component's settings.
- bevel-ijln (badges) and bevel-qb19 (attention state): per-button state published by apps, owned by the window-strip component; bevel-aqr7.3 (progress) is the third of that set.
- bevel-985s.1-.4 (volume / network / input / battery indicators): the four Windows shell-mode indicators are the clearest case for the model — structurally identical (glyph + state source + flyout), and building them as hardcoded blocks would bake in the problem this epic exists to remove.
- bevel-lbqg (clock calendar flyout) and bevel-aqr7.9 (additional clocks): the clock component's own surface and multi-instance proof.
- bevel-7p9r (notification surface): the notification host is a component too, and bevel-aqr7.7 decides whether indicators feed a combined panel.

SEQUENCING OPINION: the model should land before bevel-985s.1-.4, since those four are the first features that would otherwise multiply the hardcoded-block problem by four. Everything already shipped (start, strip, stacks, tray, clock) can migrate incrementally — the epic does not require a rewrite to start paying off.

DELIBERATELY NOT FILED, and why: Copilot, the Widgets board, Meet Now, search highlights and Teams/Chat are vendor-specific surfaces with no Bevel meaning. The component model should leave room for a third party to add such a thing; Bevel itself shipping them would be imitation without purpose.
Task 1: NetMQ 4.0.4.3 AOT gate — publish OK (no trim/AOT warnings emitted for NetMQ/AsyncIO/NaCl at build time), published win-x64 NativeAOT binary --selftest-bus printed 'bus-selftest: FAILED' (exit 1). Root cause (captured via temporary diagnostic logging, reverted before commit): System.NotSupportedException: 'AsyncIO.Windows.AcceptExDelegate' is missing delegate marshalling data — thrown from AsyncIO.Windows.Socket.Listener..ctor via NetMQ.Core.Transports.Tcp.TcpListener.SetAddress during RouterSocket.BindRandomPort. NetMQ's AsyncIO dependency uses runtime delegate-for-function-pointer marshalling on Windows that NativeAOT's trimmer/ILC does not flag at publish time but fails at connect/bind time. GATE FAILED. Same code path verified OK under a framework-dependent (non-AOT) Release build on the same machine, isolating the failure to NativeAOT specifically. STOPPING per task-1 brief step 9 — transport choice needs re-deciding by a human, not working around.
Task 1: NetMQ 4.0.4.3 is NOT NativeAOT-viable on win-x64 (AsyncIO delegate marshalling; publish is silent). User ruling: keep NetMQ, defer AOT. See bevel-la9j. BusSelfTest retained as the detector for when AOT work resumes.

title: bevelctl quit: shut the whole shell down without the UI
description:
A clean shutdown was reachable only by clicking Start > Turn Off. That is not just a convenience gap: the shutdown path is what restores the desktop the shell borrows — on Windows the native taskbar and its auto-hide/AppBar state (bevel-h0sr), on macOS the Dock — so any script, CI smoke test or agent that stopped Bevel by killing a process left the user's settings as Bevel had set them. It is also the missing safe alternative behind bevel-ozha, where hard-killing the launcher took the user's terminal down with it.

Shipped: bevelctl quit, routed through the one IShellAutomation seam like every other verb, implemented against a new narrow optional IShellLifecycle seam (sits beside IProgramSurface, so the command model in Bevel.Interop still does not reach into supervision plumbing; null in DI reports "not available"). The implementation fans out to the LAUNCHER via LauncherControl.Quit rather than ending the receiving process, because the launcher owns core, taskbar and the filers; unsupervised it falls back to shutting down the local Avalonia app. The verb takes no operands so a mistyped "quit filer" cannot silently tear down everything.

Verified end to end on Windows: launch, bevelctl quit prints "shutting down", all four role processes exit, and the desktop is restored exactly — work area 0..1392, AppBar state 0, native taskbar visible, claim marker gone.
acceptance_criteria: bevelctl quit tears down launcher, core, taskbar and filers, restores the borrowed desktop state, and reports success; no operands accepted.
close_reason: Shipped in c7d18fa on fix/windows-taskbar-icons (PR #2). Verified end to end on Windows: all four roles exit and the desktop restores exactly. 1269 tests pass. Filed retroactively — the work was done before the bead, contrary to the create-issue-before-code rule.

title: [bug] Luna Matte: active task button does not read as pressed (matte ramp drops the sunken cue)
description:
Under the Luna Matte gloss variant, the active window's task button does not read as pressed — it looks the same as a resting button. Reported on a live Windows shell after switching gloss to Matte.

Analysis so far (code reading only — NOT yet confirmed at runtime, the shell was holding the build):
- LunaVariantService computes targetGlossy per surface. For Matte it is false for EVERY surface (LunaVariant.cs ~line 314), so both Luna.Brush.TaskButton (resting) and Luna.Brush.TaskButtonChecked (active) are rendered through the same Matte() ramp: Lighten(base,0.20) at 0.0, Darken(base,0.03) at 0.55, Lighten(base,0.05) at 1.0.
- Matte() has no hard 50% split, unlike Bead(). The XP "sunken / pressed-in" cue that bevel-zk4a deliberately built into the checked state comes from that split plus a markedly darker base. Under Matte the only thing left distinguishing checked from resting is the base colour itself.
- The two bases, via BaseColor() picking the stop nearest offset 0.55: resting 2F6FE0, checked 2559BC. They differ on paper, but both then pass through the chromatic recolour c(hex) for the selected colourway, and both get the same lightening, so the delta may be too small to read — and it may collapse further for some colourways.
- Luna.Brush.TaskButtonCheckedBorder (0B2456) is an Inert solid and IS published regardless of gloss, so the checked BORDER is a cue that survives Matte and may be the cheapest place to carry the affordance.

Reporter also notes this is the same CLASS of bug as one already fixed for the Hybrid variant, where a static theme brush overrode the engine's published brush ("theme overrides brush"). Worth checking whether LunaTheme.axaml's static Luna.Brush.TaskButtonChecked LinearGradientBrush wins over the engine's value in the Matte path specifically, since that would produce exactly this symptom too, and the earlier Hybrid fix would be the template for it.

First step is to confirm WHICH of the two it is before changing anything: dump the actually-applied Luna.Brush.TaskButton vs ...Checked under Matte for a couple of colourways and compare, rather than tuning colours blind.
acceptance_criteria: Under Matte, the active window's task button is clearly distinguishable from resting and hover states in every Luna colourway, without reintroducing the 'reads as hovered' regression from bevel-zk4a.
close_reason: Fixed: the matte flatten discarded the surface's authored light direction, so the sunken checked ramp was redrawn raised. MatteSunken() chosen via IsSunkenRamp() reading the authored stops. Tests across 3 gloss modes and 4 colourways, verified failing without the fix (5 failures, all Matte) and passing with it. Commit d3cc8d0. Verified live on the Luna bar: the active task button reads sunken.

title: Start button: Bevel's own caption by default, auto-size to the configured label with a minimum width and padding
description:
The Start button should carry Bevel's own name rather than Microsoft's word, and should fit whatever caption the user sets.

Current state (most of the plumbing already exists):
- BevelSettings.TaskbarStartLabel exists, persists, and TaskbarView.ApplyStart pushes it live. Default is "Start".
- The caption is already editable in the taskbar Properties dialog (OnboardingWindow, "Caption" box, MaxLength 24, watermark "(logo only)"), reached from the Start button's right-click.

What is missing:
1. Default is "Start". Rename to Bevel's own word. Also aligns with the branding/legal direction that dropped vendor marks (bevel-legal-branding, bevel-8754d9e dropped Windows/Apple marks from the Start badge).
2. The button is a FIXED Width="74" in TaskbarView.axaml, so a longer caption is clipped (the button sets ClipToBounds="True") and a short one leaves dead space. It must auto-size to the configured label, with a minimum width and proper padding.
3. The divider after Start is positioned by a hardcoded Margin="76,1,0,1" that encodes the 74px button + margin. It must follow the button's real width, or it detaches as soon as the button resizes. It also stays put today when the Start button is hidden, leaving a floating divider.

Grid column 0 is Auto-sized, so the window-button strip follows the new width for free once the button and divider are right.

Min width belongs in the per-theme metric resources (Bevel.Metric.StartButtonMinWidth) next to the existing Bevel.Metric.StartButtonMargin — defined in BOTH Win2000Theme.axaml and LunaTheme.axaml, since a token missing from one skin renders wrong there (the lesson from Bevel.Brush.HighlightText in bevel-ijln).
acceptance_criteria: The Start button shows Bevel's own caption out of the box; setting a longer or shorter caption in taskbar Properties resizes the button to fit with proper padding, never below the themed minimum width; the divider and the button strip follow the new width in both themes; a logo-only (empty) caption still renders correctly.
close_reason: Shipped in 4385a80: caption defaults to Bevel, button auto-sizes to the caption with a per-theme Bevel.Metric.StartButtonMinWidth floor (74 Win2000 / 80 Luna) and 8px padding, divider tracks the button's live Bounds and hides with it, automation name follows the caption with a 'Start menu' fallback for logo-only. Already-existing editor: taskbar Properties > Caption. Verified live on the Luna bar. 1264 tests pass.

title: [bug] parked --role=filer child survives launcher death — orphan Job Object backstop misses it
description:
The parked Filer child outlived the launcher's death, which the orphan backstop is supposed to make impossible.

Observed 2026-10-01 (same incident as bevel-ozha): after the launcher (pid 23932) was terminated, core (21788) and taskbar (5076) died with it, but "Bevel.App.exe --role=filer --park" (pid 20772, parent 23932) was still running minutes later with its parent gone. WindowsProcessLifecycle.cs states the Job Object with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE means "every child assigned to it dies when the launcher's handle closes (including a launcher crash), so a wedged or missed child can never outlive the shell". This child was missed.

Likely cause: the parked pre-warm child is spawned on a different path from the supervised roles (FilerSupervisor's keep-1 park, via CreateRoleStartInfo) and never gets AssignProcessToJobObject — or it is assigned and then breaks away. Note the park child is invisible (hidden window), so an orphan is silent: the user has no way to notice it, and the next launch will add another.

Scope note: this is the same subsystem as bevel-ozha but the opposite failure — that one reaps too much, this one too little. Fix them together and the test should cover both directions: every spawned child (parked filer included) is in the job; nothing the launcher did not spawn is.
acceptance_criteria: After the launcher dies by any means (clean quit, crash, terminate), no Bevel.App process remains — parked filer included; covered by a test that enumerates survivors after each teardown mode.

title: Pre-existing: 2 Taskbar render tests fail on clean HEAD (unfocused click leaves button stuck pressed; pressed follows focus)
notes:
Root cause (investigation): NOT TaskButton.Toggle() no-op (f138c2d/bevel-zk4a).

Introduced by 81eaeca (bevel-c04q): TaskItemViewModel.ToggleAsync activate arm sets IsFocused=true optimistically (TaskItemViewModel.cs:322-323) without going through ShellModel.ApplyExclusiveFocus.

Causal chain:
1. Click runs ActivateCommand → ToggleAsync → IsFocused=true
2. OneWay binding IsChecked={Binding IsFocused} lights the button
3. Sibling focused VMs are NOT cleared → dual pressed [True,True] in Pressed_state_follows_focus_live
4. Single-unfocused test: button ends IsChecked=true against assert False

TaskButton.Toggle(){} still works; tests' premise 'stub WM never moves focus so click leaves unchecked' is false once model self-claims focus.

Causality: removing only IsFocused=true restores both tests (verified in worktree).

Fix proposal:
A) Prefer: optimistic claim must call ShellModel.ApplyExclusiveFocus (inject claimFocus Action into TaskItemViewModel at CreateItem) — preserves c04q latency + exclusivity invariant.
B) Tests must then be updated: click-on-unfocused with stub will optimistically press THAT button (exclusive); assert exclusivity not 'stays unchecked'. Or keep a pure Toggle()-noop test that does not invoke ActivateCommand.
C) Do NOT revert TaskButton — wrong suspect.
Handoff: diagnosis complete (see notes). Prefer fix A (ApplyExclusiveFocus via claimFocus inject) + update test expectations; do not revert TaskButton. Owner has not yet chosen implement vs nuclear drop. TODO.md updated to match.
close_reason: Optimistic IsFocused now goes through ShellModel.ClaimFocus/ApplyExclusiveFocus; tests expect exclusive optimistic press.

title: Debug traces are lost when the shell is launched the way users launch it
description:
## Why

BEVEL_DEBUG_TASKBAR (and the helper's [BEVEL-TRAY] lines) write to Console.Error. That works when the shell is started from a terminal, but a Finder/launchd launch sends stderr nowhere — and 'log show --predicate process == "Bevel"' returns nothing, because nothing writes to the macOS unified log.

This matters because of TCC: a terminal-launched process inherits the TERMINAL as its responsible process, so Screen Recording and Accessibility get attributed to the terminal rather than to Bevel/BevelHelper. Anything permission-related can therefore only be verified from a Finder launch — which is exactly the launch that has no logs. Today that cost real time on the tray-icon hunt: the only way to see the helper's self-test verdict was a terminal launch, whose TCC identity was wrong.

## What

When a BEVEL_DEBUG_* variable is set (or always, at low volume), also write to a rotating file under ~/.config/bevel/logs/ — or emit via os_log so 'log show' works. Cover BOTH sides: the .NET processes and the Swift helper.

## Acceptance

- A Finder-launched shell produces a readable trace without a terminal
- The helper's [BEVEL-TRAY] self-test lines are in it
- It rotates, and it is off or cheap by default

title: Tray self-test never re-verifies live capture once Screen Recording is granted mid-session
description: ensureSelfTested() runs the pipeline self-test exactly once. On a normal cold start the grant is usually absent at that moment, so runSelfTest() takes the granted=false branch and never actually calls selfTestCapture() — the verdict (liveMirroringEnabled=true) only proves discovery/AX work, not that a real capture is non-blank/healthy. If the user grants Screen Recording LATER in the same session, enumerateWithCapture()'s per-poll guard (isLiveMirroringEnabled && granted) now lets captures through, but the self-test that was supposed to gate a broken capture pipeline never gets a chance to actually check captureOk for THIS session — its conclusion was computed once during the limited-mode phase and never revisited when the real grant arrives (same family as bevel-yduf/bevel-7s9n/bevel-lej1). Reported symptom: tray icons after a mid-session grant render but look soft/low-res; a restart with the grant already active is reportedly crisp (needs on-device confirmation — not verified here). Fix: re-arm the self-test on the ungranted-to-granted rising edge so captureOk is actually exercised once real capture is possible.
notes: Fixed in commit cbbd0b7 (this worktree, branch worktree-agent-abd91dedb91eecc7f, based on refactor/macos-interop-consolidation @ ef7d303): TrayServiceImpl.ensureSelfTested() now re-arms exactly once on the ungranted->granted rising edge (selfTestShouldRun, unit tested in TrayServiceTests.swift). Also added TrayViewModelTests.Limited_to_live_transition_upgrades_the_icon_to_its_full_native_resolution, which passes unmodified and rules out the C#/Avalonia decode+display path as the source of the reported softness. NOT confirmed on-device: whether this self-test gap is actually THE cause of the reported soft/low-res icons, vs. a macOS/WindowServer backing-store staleness for a not-recently-composited status item (leading alternative hypothesis). Needs a signed on-device run with a live grant-after-launch repro to confirm either way -- explicitly deferred per this session's constraints (no dev-sign.sh / no killing the running signed Bevel instance).

title: TaskbarViewModel applied connection/settings state before subscribing to their change events
description:
Part of the stale-value audit -- exact sibling of the App.axaml.cs apply-then-subscribe bug fixed earlier the same day (settings.Changed subscribed BEFORE the startup theme read, with a comment explaining why).

src/Bevel.Taskbar/Model/TaskbarViewModel.cs ctor had the same shape TWICE:
  1. `_isDisconnected = !connection.IsConnected; connection.ConnectionChanged += OnConnectionChanged;`
  2. `ApplyConsolidation(settings.Current.TaskbarConsolidateMenuBar); settings.Changed += OnSettingsChanged;`

A connection flip or settings snapshot landing in the gap between the read and the subscribe would never invoke the handler for that transition, leaving IsDisconnected or the Strategy-C menu-bar-consolidation flag wrong until some LATER, unrelated event happened to fire again (or never, in a quiet session). The settings gap is narrower than the App.axaml.cs one (in-process construction vs. a cross-process IPC push) but real: RemoteSettingsService applies the core's live snapshot asynchronously off the UI thread, and TaskbarViewModel is constructed synchronously on the UI thread with nothing awaiting that pull first.

FIXED in this audit pass: both pairs swapped to subscribe-before-read, matching the RemoteSettingsService/App.axaml.cs discipline. Regression test added: tests/Bevel.Taskbar.Tests/TaskbarViewModelSubscriptionOrderTests.cs (asserts subscribe precedes the relevant read; verified to FAIL against the pre-fix ordering for both pairs, PASS against the fix).
close_reason: Fixed same session: src/Bevel.Taskbar/Model/TaskbarViewModel.cs constructor now subscribes to ConnectionChanged and settings.Changed BEFORE reading IsConnected/Current. Guarded by tests/Bevel.Taskbar.Tests/TaskbarViewModelSubscriptionOrderTests.cs (2 tests), verified to fail on the pre-fix ordering and pass on the fix. Full test suite (469 tests) green.

title: [bug] Filer Toolbar.ApplyIcons() rasterized once in the ctor, never re-applied on live theme switch
description:
Part of the stale-value audit (parent theme: value captured once in a provisional/prior state, nothing re-reads it when the real value arrives).

src/Bevel.FileManager/Components/Toolbar.axaml.cs:8-12: ApplyIcons() rasterizes all 15 toolbar button bitmaps (ToolbarIcons.Back()/.Forward()/etc, src/Bevel.FileManager/Components/ToolbarIcons.cs) once in the constructor. Each call resolves the ACTIVE theme's colors at that instant into a baked bitmap; nothing re-invokes ApplyIcons() when the theme later changes live.

Captured: whichever theme is active when the Explorer window (and its Toolbar) is first constructed.
Should refresh: on the same theme-change signal other chrome uses (ThemeService.Apply / settings.Changed re-theme fan-out in App.axaml.cs).
Does it: no.

Symptom: any Explorer window already open when a live theme switch happens (a genuine settings edit, or the bevel-lej1 startup race) keeps its OLD toolbar icon colors for the rest of that window's life -- only a newly opened Explorer window picks up the new theme's toolbar icons. Visually inconsistent chrome: window frame/menu re-theme live, toolbar icons don't.

Fix shape: re-invoke ApplyIcons() from wherever ItemViewModel.HideKnownExtensions / other per-window folder-options fan-out already runs on settings.Changed (App.axaml.cs:179-181 iterates FileManagerWindowRegistry -- ApplyFolderOptions could grow a toolbar re-icon step, or Toolbar could expose its own re-apply method called from there). Small and mostly mechanical, but touches the live-re-theme fan-out path shared with other FileManager chrome, so left as a bead for scoped review rather than folded into this audit's direct fixes.

title: Window-list reconnect snapshot only upserts -- possible stale taskbar buttons after core restart
description:
Part of the stale-value audit (parent theme: value captured once, nothing re-reads/reconciles it when the real value changes). Sibling of bevel-ri8c (same shape, tray side); filed separately because it needs its own verification.

src/Bevel.App/ShellCore/ShellCoreWindowManager.cs:47-51 (OnCoreEvent, case WindowSnapshot): a reconnect snapshot is replayed as WindowOpened only -- an existing code comment confirms "ShellModel upserts idempotently by id" with no removal path. A window closed while the core link was down would leave a stale taskbar button until the app is manually quit again, UNLESS ShellModel/TaskbarViewModel has its own independent close-detection poll that masks this.

Captured: the window list built at the LAST connect/snapshot.
Should refresh: a reconnect should reconcile to exactly what the fresh WindowSnapshot contains.
Does it: replay-as-WindowOpened only, confirmed; whether a separate poll masks the gap in practice is NOT yet confirmed.

Symptom (if unmasked): after a core auto-repair or restart (bevel-hprv path), a taskbar button for a window that was closed during the outage stays visible and unclickable/stale until a full shell restart.

Action needed: first confirm whether ShellModel's existing 2s reconcile backstop (mentioned in the subscribe-ordering audit) already covers window removal independently of the snapshot replay -- if so, downgrade/close this bead with that citation. If not, apply the same snapshot-reconciliation fix as bevel-ri8c.

title: Tray reconnect snapshot only upserts -- ghost icons survive a core restart
description:
Part of the stale-value audit (parent theme: value captured once, nothing re-reads/reconciles it when the real value changes).

src/Bevel.Taskbar/Model/TrayViewModel.cs (OnItemAdded/Upsert, ~line 200) plus src/Bevel.App/ShellCore/ShellCoreSystemTrayHost.cs:45-49 (OnCoreEvent, case TraySnapshot): a reconnect's TraySnapshot is replayed purely as a sequence of ItemAdded events, which TrayViewModel treats as idempotent upserts. The transport layer itself is sound -- ShellCoreServer.ClientConnected pushes a fresh snapshot on EVERY connect, not just the first -- the gap is entirely in this consumer treating a resend as pure addition instead of a reconciling replace (diff and remove what's no longer present).

Captured: the tray item list built at the LAST connect/snapshot.
Should refresh: a reconnect (e.g. LostCoreAutoRepair, bevel-hprv) should reconcile the peer's tray to exactly what the fresh TraySnapshot contains, removing items no longer present.
Does it: no -- only adds/updates.

Symptom: bevel-hprv's core auto-repair is a DESIGNED recovery path, exercised whenever the core misbehaves (exactly the kind of transient failure this shell is built to survive). If an app owning a menu-bar icon quits while the shell-core link is down, or during the few seconds a core restart takes, that icon's TrayItemRemoved event is lost -- the peer never sees it -- and the reconnect snapshot only adds/updates, never diffs out the ghost. Result: a stale tray icon for an app that's no longer running stays in the taskbar tray until the whole shell is restarted. This will recur every time the designed auto-repair path fires under the right timing.

Fix shape: on TraySnapshot, reconcile TrayViewModel's item set to exactly the snapshot's ids (remove anything not present) instead of only upserting. Needs a small design decision on how "remove" interacts with in-flight icon renders -- left as a bead.

title: Taskbar buttons need an attention state — the Dock still jumps and Bevel shows nothing
description:
## Why

User, 2026-09-29: the macOS Dock icons still JUMP when an app requests attention, while Bevel shows nothing at all. So the one signal the user actually reacts to is coming from the thing Bevel replaces, and Bevel's own bar stays silent — the worst split possible. Classic Windows flashed the taskbar button (FlashWindowEx); Bevel has no equivalent.

Note Bevel sets the Dock to auto-hide, so the bounce is often happening off-screen or behind the bar: the attention is being raised and LOST.

## Desired UX — 'designed in 2026', not a literal blink

The user's own suggestions: the button could PULSE gently, or a WHOOSH of light could sweep left-to-right across it. Both are better than the classic hard on/off flash, and both fit the north star (classic feel, modern quality — see the designed-in-2026 memory). Pick one as default and make it a setting if cheap.

Constraints that apply:
- Vector-only, bound to theme tokens; never raster, never disable antialiasing.
- It must read under BOTH skins — a light sweep over Win2000's flat grey button face is a different problem from Luna's gloss.
- Must stop on activation, and must not animate forever (classic Windows flashed a bounded number of times, then left the button tinted).
- Needs an opt-out, and should respect a reduced-motion preference if one is reachable.

## Sourcing the signal

On macOS an app asks via NSApplication.requestUserAttention, which is what makes the Dock bounce. bevel-ijln already mines the Dock's AX tree for unread badges (commit 2d01f71), so the same helper path is the obvious place to observe attention state. Confirm whether the AX tree exposes it, or whether it needs a different hook.

## Acceptance

- An app requesting attention animates its task button, under both skins
- The animation stops when the window is activated
- It is bounded, not perpetual
- There is a way to turn it off
- Render tests covering the animated state in both skins

Related: bevel-ijln (badges/counts) shares the Dock AX source. bevel-zk4a (pressed state for the focused button) shares the task-button visual states.

title: Nothing asserts popup PLACEMENT — the Start menu is only ever rendered in isolation
description:
## Why

bevel-kclq shipped a Start menu floating one RowHeight above the taskbar, and no test could have caught it. RenderLunaStartMenuTest detaches the popup's content into its own window before capturing (it has to — a popup's child measures 0x0 headlessly, the avalonia-popup-needs-visual-tree gotcha), so the menu is only ever rendered ALONE. Its position relative to the bar is never asserted by anything.

The fix for kclq is guarded by StartButtonCapTests, which checks the Start button's height cap because that is the value the anchor derives from. That is a proxy, not the property we care about.

## What

A test that asserts the popup's position against the taskbar window's — bottom edge of the menu flush with the top edge of the bar. Ideally across a row-count CHANGE (1->3->2), since a stale anchor after a resize is the same failure class.

Headless popups do not position meaningfully, so this likely needs either:
- the popup host's screen position read via PointToScreen at open (what TaskbarView.TraceMenuPlacement already logs), asserted rather than logged; or
- an on-device render harness.

## Also

Remove TaskbarView.TraceMenuPlacement() once this exists — it is debug-gated scaffolding kept only because placement was untestable.

## Acceptance

- A test fails if the Start menu's bottom edge is not flush with the taskbar's top edge
- It covers at least one row-count change
- TraceMenuPlacement is deleted

title: [bug] Tray mirrors the right items but fails to render their icons
description:
## Why

User, 2026-09-29: 'tray is not empty, it just fails to render proper icons'. So discovery and mirroring are working — the item count and positions are right — and the failure is in turning each mirrored item into a drawn icon.

Seen in a session that also had multiple shell instances running (see the single-instance bug), so FIRST re-check on a clean single instance before digging; it may be a casualty of that rather than its own defect.

## What to look at

- The tray path renders via ScreenCaptureKit capture of each status item, which needs the Screen Recording grant keyed to the HELPER's binary path. A rebuild changes the helper's cdhash, and packaging/macos/dev-sign.sh exists precisely so the grant sticks — but a grant can still be lost.
- Distinguish 'no image came back' from 'an image came back and we drew it wrong (size, format, premultiplication)'.
- Compare against the stack-grid path, which does render real content previews correctly.

## Acceptance

- Mirrored tray items show their real icons on a clean single-instance run
- A failed capture degrades to a visible placeholder rather than an empty/blank slot, and says so in the log

title: Version-skew message needs to be readable and offer actions
description:
## Why

User request, 2026-09-29. Rebuilding the bundle under a running launcher produced this dialog:

  Taskbar stamp '1|1.0.0+1f4cc8f49bf72ef73af5e83fe8984b444c39554c|639262990342066720' != launcher
  '1|1.0.0+32528975eafcc3cb3b5c1bc33eb5869b7f1409ba|639262990342066720' after 3 restarts
  The launcher has stopped restarting this process so it cannot crash-loop.

The GUARD is right and it did its job. The presentation is a raw internal stamp, two 40-char SHAs the reader must diff by eye, and no way forward.

## What

- Say what happened in a sentence: the app was updated while it was running, so the taskbar and launcher are from different builds.
- Show the two builds in human terms — short SHA and build time, or a version line — not the full stamp triple.
- Offer actions: 'Restart Bevel' (relaunch the whole shell on the new build) and 'Quit'. Right now the only route is the command line.
- Keep the full stamp available for a bug report (copy button or a details disclosure), just not as the headline.

title: Active app's taskbar button must render PRESSED
description:
## Why

User request, 2026-09-29. The task button for the currently-focused window does not render in the pressed/sunken state, so the bar gives no indication of which app is active. Classic Win2000/XP taskbars show the foreground window's button depressed; it is one of the main things the bar is FOR.

## What

- The task button bound to the focused window renders pressed (sunken bevel under Win2000, the darker inset gradient under Luna).
- It follows focus live, including focus moving to an app with no button and back.
- Exactly one button is pressed at a time; a grouped button is pressed when any window in the group is focused.
- Check against TaskItemViewModel.IsFocused, which already exists and is what bevel-hx63's handback work reads.

## Acceptance

- Render tests under both skins showing the focused button distinct from its neighbours
close_reason: Done: the active app's taskbar button renders PRESSED. Root cause of the live 'never pressed' symptom: LunaVariantService's reference TaskButtonChecked was designed LIT (brighter-than-hover + bright #2A5DB8 border) — an app-level override that outranks the LunaTheme XAML fallback, invisible to headless renders (which don't run the variant engine). Fixed to the XP-authentic pressed-in dark gradient (1B4EA8→2559BC→2E63C8, border 0B2456 — widened gap for Purple's transform). Probe chain proved every logic link already worked (IsChecked flips, :checked pseudo, brush resolution, group forwarding, exactly-one). Acceptance strengthened: AssertFaceIsDarker (pressed = darker, not merely 'distinct') under the variant engine (Blue+Purple), plus the grouped-path render test (grouping=Always + focus-after-build, the user's live config). User-confirmed live: pressed render works.

title: [bug] Shell starts unskinned (Win2000) and the theme changes under it mid-session
description:
## Why

Observed 2026-09-29 on macOS during the bevel-kclq hunt. The shell came up in the Win2000 skin when the persisted theme is Luna, and the active skin then CHANGED during the session — a trace at 19:23 showed the Start menu at Luna's natural size (360x545), and at 19:31 the same session was rendering the Classic menu (211x225) with a grey Win2000 taskbar. The user did not switch it.

## What

Two things that may be one thing:
1. First paint is unskinned because peers read settings through the core and the theme has not arrived yet. That is bevel-7s9n ('Peer-side settings snapshot cache on disk -> correct-theme first paint, zero IPC'), already filed as P1 design.
2. The theme then changes again mid-session, which 7s9n does not obviously cover. Suspect the 750ms settings poll delivering a default-valued snapshot (e.g. a read that fails or returns an unpopulated BevelSettings) and ThemeService.Apply being driven from it. A theme that flips WITHOUT a user action is the bug regardless of the first-paint question.

## Why it matters beyond the flicker

Theme switching re-templates live, and template-part setters do not revert cleanly on the way back out (see the theme-switch-live-revert-limits memory, bevel-p3va). A skin that changes by itself puts the shell through that path unprompted.

## Acceptance

- A session whose persisted theme is Luna paints Luna on its first frame
- The active theme never changes without a user action or a settings write
- Covered by a test over the peer settings path, not just a manual restart

title: [bug] Start menu and taskbar menus open with a gap above the taskbar
description:
## Why

User report on macOS, running session (signed dev build, 2026-09-29): the Start menu and taskbar menus open TOO HIGH — there is a visible gap between the bottom edge of the menu and the top edge of the taskbar. They should sit flush on the bar, as the classic shells do.

## What

Suspect the popup placement anchors to the taskbar WINDOW rather than to the visible bar, or uses a height metric that no longer matches what is drawn. TaskbarTheme has several: ButtonHeight -> RowHeight (+4) -> TaskbarHeight (+2), plus HeightForRows(rows). A placement computed from one while the window is sized from another shows up exactly as a constant offset.

## Acceptance

- Start menu's bottom edge is flush with the taskbar's top edge, no gap
- Same for taskbar context/tray menus
- Holds across the button-size tiers (Small/Normal/Large/Big) and for a 2-row bar
notes:
## Investigation 2026-09-29 — taskbar-side geometry EXCLUDED with numbers

Reported on a 2-ROW bar (screenshot). Gap between the menu's bottom edge and the taskbar's top edge is ~one button/row height. TaskbarTheme at the Normal tier: ButtonHeight=24, RowHeight=28, TaskbarHeight=30, HeightForRows(2)=58.

MEASURED in a headless repro of the real arrangement (TaskbarWindow rows:2 + real TaskbarView + real StartButton):

  windowHeight           = 58  = HeightForRows(2)     correct
  StartButton.Bounds     = 0,0,74,58                  fills the window
  StartButton top-in-win = 0,0                        top edge IS the bar's top edge
  StartButton.MaxHeight  = 86  = HeightForRows(3)     never binds at 2 rows

So Placement=Top against that target should land the menu flush on the bar. The taskbar side is right.

EXCLUDED, each for a concrete reason:
  - Row metrics / HeightForRows — measured above, correct for rows=2.
  - StartMaxRows=3 cap on StartButton.MaxHeight — 86 > 58, so it never clamps at 2 rows.
  - Bevel.Metric.StartButtonMargin — Win2000 is 1,1,0,1 and Luna is 0; both would OVERLAP by <=1px, wrong sign for a gap.
  - The popup's two layouts both measuring — ApplyThemeLayout sets IsVisible, which collapses in Avalonia rather than reserving space.
  - macOS Dock reserving the strip — Bevel sets the Dock to auto-hide (defaults read com.apple.dock autohide = 1), which reserves ~4px, not ~28.

LEADING HYPOTHESIS: the popup is being clamped to the SCREEN WORK AREA rather than placed against the target, and the work-area band Bevel reserves does not match the bar it draws. Note HeightForRows(3) - HeightForRows(2) = 28 = exactly the observed gap, so a band reserved for one row more than is drawn would produce precisely this. RecomputeWorkAreaBand uses HeightForRows(_rows), so the suspect is a stale _rows or a band recomputed at the wrong moment (e.g. before SetRows updates it), not the formula.

NOT REPRODUCIBLE HEADLESS: popup placement here is native macOS positioning. Also note the existing render test (RenderLunaStartMenuTest) DETACHES the popup content into its own window before capturing, so nothing in the suite covers placement relative to the bar at all — which is why this shipped. A regression test for this bug has to assert the popup's position against the taskbar window's, not render the menu in isolation.

NEXT: relaunch with stderr captured (TaskbarLog.Debug already traces 'SetRows req=/clamped=/MaxRows=/cur=') and read the row + band values with the menu open.
## It is STATEFUL, not static — a restart clears it (2026-09-29)

User: 'the restarts have somehow cleared the bug now'. That is the most useful fact so far and it reframes everything above: the geometry measures CORRECT at steady state, live (ApplyRowLayout rows=2 rootHeight=58 scaling=2) and headless (window 58, StartButton 0,0,74,58 filling it). Nothing static is wrong. The gap only exists in a session that has been through some transition.

ARITHMETIC POINTS AT A STALE ANCHOR ONE ROW TOO TALL. The bar drew 2 rows (58). The gap was ~one RowHeight (28). HeightForRows(3) = 86, and 86 - 58 = 28 exactly. So the menu was anchored to a bar one row TALLER than the one on screen. A stale 1-row anchor would have the opposite sign (the menu would overlap the bar), so this is specifically an anchor that did not shrink when the bar did.

LIKELY TRIGGER: the row count (or the button-size tier) changed downward during the session — resize grip, the settings slider, or a display change — and something the popup anchors to was not refreshed. SetRows and ReapplyMetrics both resize the window, re-anchor it, recompute the work-area band and raise RowsChanged; the suspect is whatever the popup path reads that is NOT on that list. Note the Start menu instance is cached (_startMenu ??= new StartMenu(...)) and parented once, so it survives every row change.

REPRO TO TRY (not yet confirmed): with the shell running, grow the taskbar to 3 rows (drag the resize grip, or the Taskbar rows slider in Bevel Settings), then SHRINK it back to 2, then open the Start menu. Expect the menu to float one row-height above the bar. If that reproduces, the fix is to refresh the popup's anchor on RowsChanged.

DIAGNOSTIC LEFT IN TREE: TaskbarView.TraceMenuPlacement() logs popup top, popup size, Start-button top, bar height, rows, HeightForRows and the work-area band at the moment the menu opens. Debug-gated (BEVEL_DEBUG_TASKBAR=1), so it costs nothing normally. Run the shell from a terminal rather than 'open' so stderr is captured. Remove it once this is fixed.

STILL TRUE AND STILL THE REAL GAP: no test covers popup placement. RenderLunaStartMenuTest detaches the popup content into its own window before capturing, so the menu is only ever rendered in isolation and its position relative to the bar is never asserted. Whatever the cause turns out to be, the regression test has to assert the popup's position against the taskbar window's — and ideally across a row-count CHANGE, since that is the transition implicated here.
## First real trace — and it is CLEAN. Two hypotheses killed (2026-09-29)

Captured live with BEVEL_DEBUG_TASKBAR after a restart that the user reported HAD reintroduced the gap:

  kclq placement popupTop=0,837 popupSize=360,545 startBtnTop=0,1382
                 barH=58 rows=2 heightForRows=58 band={X=0,Y=1382,W=2560,H=58} scaling=2

Popup bottom = 837 + 545 = 1382. Start-button top = 1382. Band top = 1382. The popup's box is EXACTLY flush with the bar. Placement is correct, and the box is correctly sized.

KILLED — 'the popup box is taller than its content because it was measured under the wrong theme'. Measured the two layouts' natural sizes headlessly (detaching the popup content into a SizeToContent window, the trick RenderLunaStartMenuTest already uses):

  win2000 (Classic) natural = 211 x 225
  luna              natural = 360 x 545

Classic is SMALLER. A box stuck at the Classic size would CLIP the Luna content, not leave space beneath it. Wrong sign, so the theme-race-sizing story does not hold.

KILLED EARLIER — stale row anchor, StartMaxRows cap, button margins, both-layouts-measuring, Dock reservation. Each with a number or a sign argument, see the previous note.

WHAT THIS LEAVES. Either (a) that particular open was fine and the gap needs a trace captured WHILE it is on screen, or (b) the popup box is right and something inside the Luna layout is not filling it in the bad state. The trace cannot distinguish those, so it needs the per-layout bounds too.

NEW AND POSSIBLY THE REAL STORY: the user reports the shell 'also started unskinned (2000s)' on that restart — it comes up Win2000 and becomes Luna once settings arrive. That is bevel-7s9n ('Peer-side settings snapshot cache on disk -> correct-theme first paint, zero IPC'), an existing P1. The restart-dependence of THIS bug and the unskinned first paint are both timing on the same settings arrival, so they are plausibly the same race even though the sizing mechanism above is not the link. Worth fixing 7s9n first and re-checking whether this survives.

NEXT: capture a trace at an open where the gap is VISIBLE, and extend TraceMenuPlacement to log LunaLayout.Bounds / ClassicLayout.Bounds / IsVisible alongside the popup box, so 'box too big' and 'content too small' are distinguishable in one line. Do NOT restart the shell while it is reproducing — a restart clears it and the current binary already carries the trace.
close_reason:
Fixed in 209a92a and verified on device 2026-09-29 (macOS, 2-row bar, Luna). The Start menu now sits flush on the taskbar.

Cause: StartButton.MaxHeight was a flat HeightForRows(StartMaxRows)=86 for the 3-row ceiling. On a 2-row (58) bar that never binds on HEIGHT — which is why it was dismissed mid-hunt — but the Start menu's popup anchors above the Start button, so a button the layout treats as 86 tall parked the anchor at the 3-row position. Now clamped to min(rows, StartMaxRows), and ApplyRowLayout re-applies it so a row change cannot leave it stale.

Measured on device at rows=2, scaling=2, captured with the menu open: popup bottom landed at logical 1355 = HeightForRows(3) off the screen bottom + the Win2000 skin's 1px button margin, where the bar's top is 1383. Error 28 logical / 56 device; an independent pixel scan measured 54.

StartButtonCapTests guards it, and was verified to FAIL on the old form (rows=1 and rows=2) before being accepted.

RESIDUAL: nothing asserts popup PLACEMENT. RenderLunaStartMenuTest detaches the popup's content into its own window before capturing, so the menu is only ever rendered in isolation — that is why this shipped, and the cap test is a proxy. Filed as the real follow-up.

Also left in tree: TaskbarView.TraceMenuPlacement(), debug-gated behind BEVEL_DEBUG_TASKBAR. Remove it once placement has a real test.

title: Landing-page shots are all 1x — harvest them at 2x for HiDPI
description:
hero-luna.png is DONE (a07e80d) — generated by Render_site_hero at 2x, and the harvest's MANUAL list is now empty. Every shot the page references is produced by a test.

ONE ITEM REMAINS: theme-win2000.png is still 1x. Avalonia mis-scales OnboardingWindow above 1x — reproduced in isolation, its TabControl content forces an intermediate composition layer which is allocated at the RenderTargetBitmap's DEVICE size and then blitted into LOGICAL space, so the window chrome renders at 1x while the client content is magnified 2x and clipped to the top-left quadrant. The other nine windows have no such layer.

It is the only soft shot left, and it sits directly beside the 2x luna-4up in the themes strip, so the mismatch is visible.

Options, cheapest first:
1. Find what forces the layer — an opacity, clip or effect on the tab presenter — and see whether it can be dropped without changing the dialog's appearance.
2. Render the Appearance page's content in a host without a TabControl (losing the tab strip from the shot, which is arguably fine since the shot is about the Appearance settings).
3. Reduce to a minimal repro and file upstream.

Currently passes scale: 1 to SiteShot.Save and is the only name in MANUAL_1X in site/check-shot-sizes.py.
