title: Taskbar: Win10/11-style big icons mode
description:
## Problem
Want a taskbar \"big icons\" mode like Windows 10/11 (large app icons on the bar, typically icon-only). Live report #8.

## Current state
- Settings already have TaskbarButtonSize { Small, Normal, Large } and TaskbarButtonLabels { Auto, Always, IconOnly } — exposed in Onboarding.
- Large only grows chrome: TaskbarTheme.ButtonHeight 30 → bar ~36pt. Task button Images are hardcoded Width/Height=\"16\" in TaskbarView.axaml; icons are not reloaded at a larger pixel size.
- Tray has its own TaskbarTrayIconSize slider (12–32); task buttons do not.
- opportunity-map Aero note assumes \"taskbarButtonLabels=IconOnly + taskbarButtonSize=Large already exist\" as the Win7/10 large-icon look — but Large is incomplete without bigger glyphs.

## Desired
Win10/11-like big-icons mode:
- Larger task-button icons (≈24–32px; match or approach ButtonHeight inset)
- Sensible default pairing with IconOnly (labels off) when picking \"big icons\" — or a single preset that sets both
- Bar height / work-area reservation follow the taller buttons (existing TaskbarTheme + ResizeToRows path)
- Icons loaded at the display size (IconLoader), not upscaled 16px bitmaps

## Acceptance
- Large (or a new Big/Win11 size) renders task icons at a clearly larger size than Normal, not just taller empty chrome
- IconOnly + Large (or the preset) looks recognizably like Win10/11 icon-only taskbar
- Setting change applies live (existing settings poll) and updates work-area
- Fake PAL / headless test asserts icon slot size or load size under Large
- Does not break multi-row / Small / tray sizing (xpfl interaction: tray still uses TaskbarTrayIconSize)

## Non-goals
- Full W11 centered taskbar / Start (separate theme profile)
- Changing default theme away from Win2000 chrome — this is a sizing/labels mode on the existing bar
acceptance_criteria: Large/big mode shows larger task icons (not just taller buttons); IconOnly pairing; live apply; icons loaded at display size; tests
notes:
## Implemented (2026-09-23), merged to main

### The bead's crux claim was WRONG — recorded so nobody re-chases it
The bead said icons must be 'loaded at the display size via IconLoader, not upscaled 16px bitmaps'.
Task-button icons never touch IconLoader at all. They arrive as ForeignWindow.IconPng and are decoded by
ShellModel.LoadWindowIcon into a process-local FNV-1a-keyed bitmap cache. The Swift helper
(WindowServiceImpl.appIconPNG) already renders every app icon at a fixed 64x64 ON PURPOSE, with a comment
saying 16 looked blocky on Retina. So 24 and 32 are DOWNSCALES — there was never an upscale to fix. The
only real defect was the slot being clamped to a literal Width=16 Height=16 in TaskbarView.axaml.

Therefore IconLoader needed NO change (it already keys cache as path|size, and serves only the Start menu
and tray stacks), and MmfBgraPool is untouched: ShellModel deliberately does NOT write window icons to the
shared pool (taskbar is a reader in split mode, see ShellModel.cs:405). No cross-process key collision is
possible because no second pool entry is ever created. The bead's concern about pool/cache collision was
therefore moot.

Held up: Large really was chrome-only (ButtonHeight 30, nothing else); both task-button Images were
literal 16; tray had its own knob and task buttons had none.

### What shipped
Both an extended Large AND a new Big tier, because the acceptance criteria wanted two different things:
Large had to stop being empty chrome (now 24px glyph in a 30px button), while the Win10/11 look needs a
genuinely tall bar (Big = 40px button, row 44, bar 46, 32px glyph).

Mechanism: TaskbarTheme.TaskIconSize published beside ButtonHeight; TaskbarView republishes it as a
Bevel.Metric.TaskbarIconSize DynamicResource that both task-button templates bind Width/Height to. Live
apply rides the existing ApplyLiveSettings 750ms poll and re-measures realized buttons without rebuilding
the strip. Bar height still flows through the single HeightForRows authority -> ReapplyMetrics -> work-area
band, so nothing is forked (this is what bevel-yv2m depends on). The icon-only floor/cap/label threshold
are now derived from the glyph edge (+8/+24/+18) and reproduce the old 24/40/34 EXACTLY at 16px, so
Small/Normal are bit-identical — which is why no render baseline moved. Tray sizing untouched
(bevel-xpfl), with a test asserting that independence. The new metric token is the anchor bevel-ijln's
badge should position against instead of assuming 16.

Onboarding gains a 'Big icons' item that also selects IconOnly in one mutate, while keeping the two
settings independent and the label combo usable.

Files: TaskbarWindow.cs, SettingsService.cs (TaskbarButtonSize.Big), TaskbarView.axaml,
TaskbarView.axaml.cs (ApplyTaskIconMetric, icon-size-aware layout constants, ComputeButtonLayout iconSize
param), OnboardingWindow.axaml/.cs, plus TaskbarThemeTests/ButtonLayoutTests extended and NEW
RenderBigIconsTaskbarTest.cs.

Tests: 9 new — per-tier TaskIconSize, glyph-fits-button invariant, tray independence, Big height maths, a
3-case theory for the scaled icon-only slot, the Auto-crowded floor, and three headless (realized
Image.Width 16->24->32->16 across LIVE tier changes; MinHeight/MaxHeight pinned to HeightForRows(2) under
Big; a render capture). No render baseline changed or weakened.

Verified on main after merge: full solution suite 998 passed / 0 failed / 2 skipped. xpfl's tray caps
survived unchanged, confirming Normal-tier metrics really are bit-identical.

### Site
RenderBigIconsTaskbarTest.Render_big_icons_taskbar_to_png writes a real 1920x46 render (env override
BEVEL_BIGICONS_TASKBAR_OUT). site/index.html was deliberately NOT edited — harvest that shot into
site/shots/ once the mode passes on-device QA, per the no-faked-screenshots rule.

### Remaining before close: on-device QA
1. 32 DIP glyphs on a 3x display are a mild upscale from the helper's 64px source (fine at 1x/2x). If it
   reads soft, bump appIconPNG to 128 in the Swift helper — weigh against the gRPC 4MB ListWindows cap
   that the existing 64px comment cites.
2. The Start button logo is still 16px (StartLogoHost) on a 46px Big bar — left alone deliberately because
   the Start/divider layout uses a fixed Margin='76,1,0,1' that a wider logo would desync. File a separate
   bead if it looks undersized in practice.
3. Multi-row Big (rows 2-4) work-area reservation + the resize-grip drag step on a real screen.

### Test gap noticed during integration
No test covers the TRAY cap under the new Big tier (xpfl's tier test predates Big). The formula
(HeightForRows(rows)-6)/rows scales automatically so it should be correct, but Big x Rows=2 is unasserted.

title: Taskbar: app unread/badge counts (Slack-style)
description:
## Problem
Apps that show a Dock badge / unread count (e.g. Slack) do not surface that number on Bevel taskbar buttons. When the Dock is covered/shimmed, those badges are unreachable (spec 02 §9). Live ask: get the badge, and/or show the number next to the icon before the title.

## Desired UX (either or both)
1. Icon overlay badge (red pill / count) on the task button icon — Dock-like
2. Inline count before the title text (e.g. \"3  Slack\" or \"(3) Slack\") — Win-taskbar-friendly, readable at small sizes

Prefer shipping (2) first if badge sourcing is hard; (1) when a reliable count is available.

## Data sources (investigate; pick least-fragile)
- macOS: NSDockTile.badgeLabel is per-app private to that process — Bevel cannot read foreign apps' Dock tiles via public API. Options:
  - Heuristic: parse window Title / AppId for leading \"(N)\", \"N ·\", Slack-style prefixes (works for many Electron apps; brittle)
  - AX / Dock observation (spec Q3 territory for bounce; similar private-API policy questions for badge labels)
  - Notification Center / UNUserNotification — usually not exposed cross-app
- Grouping count (R-TB-6 window-glomming badge) is a different feature — do not conflate with unread

## Acceptance
- TaskItemViewModel (and grouped button if applicable) can carry an optional BadgeCount / BadgeText
- When count > 0: show inline before title AND/OR icon overlay (product choice; both layouts supported or setting)
- Updates when window titles / source change without blocking UI thread
- Fake PAL can inject badge counts for tests; Slack-like title fixtures in unit tests
- Document macOS source limitations honestly in bead notes / CODEMAP if AX/private path is deferred

## Non-goals
- DemandsAttention flash/bounce (R-TB-8) — related but separate
- Replacing tray notification icons
- Inventing counts when the app does not expose any signal
acceptance_criteria: Optional badge on task buttons (inline before title and/or icon overlay); testable via Fake PAL; macOS source path documented
notes:
SOURCING DETERMINATION (verified empirically on this machine, macOS 26 / Darwin 25.6):

NSDockTile.badgeLabel is NOT readable cross-app. It is a property of the owning process's own NSApp.dockTile; AppKit exposes no API to obtain a foreign application's tile. Confirmed by API surface, not assumption — there is no foreign-tile accessor to call.

WHAT IS OBTAINABLE VIA PUBLIC API: the Dock process's own accessibility tree. com.apple.dock publishes one AXApplicationDockItem per app, and each carries AXStatusLabel = the badge label the Dock is painting, plus AXURL (-> app bundle -> bundle id via CFBundle) and AXTitle (display name). Probed live with a Swift AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue walk and then again through the shipped C# reader; real output from this machine:
  System Settings / com.apple.systempreferences = '1'   (count 1)
  Beeper Desktop  / com.automattic.beeper.desktop = '10' (count 10)
  AyuGram         / one.ayugram.AyuGramDesktop    = '..89' (count NULL — see below)
Full Dock scan cost ~17 ms for 30 app items. This is public Accessibility API (AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue), NOT private API, and needs only the Accessibility TCC grant the shell already requires.

So the title heuristic was NOT needed and was deliberately NOT implemented. A leading '(7)' / '7 ·' in a window title is never turned into a badge; a Theory test pins that.

HONEST LIMITATIONS (the statement a user should be told):
1. Needs the Accessibility permission. Without it: no badges at all (empty, never a throw, never a guess).
2. It reports what the DOCK shows. An app the Dock does not list — LSUIElement agents, apps hidden from the Dock — publishes no badge here even when it notifies.
3. The label is the Dock's own rendering, so wide counts arrive ELLIPSIZED: macOS reports '..89', not '1089'. BadgeText is therefore a string shown verbatim, and BadgeCount/AppBadge.Count is null unless the label parses as a number. Dot/glyph badges are shown as-is with a null count.
4. It is a 2 s POLL, not a push — there is no public notification for a badge change — so a count can lag by up to one reconcile tick.
5. No badge source on Windows: the taskbar overlay-icon API is per-owning-process like NSDockTile, so NullAppBadgeSource is registered there.

SHIPPED: inline pill BEFORE the title (option 2) on both the single-window and grouped task buttons. Inline rather than an icon overlay on purpose — readable at 11px, and independent of icon size so the Large/big-icons work (bevel-c54t) can grow the icon with no overlay geometry to re-derive. Code-drawn rounded ContentControl (src/Bevel.Taskbar/TaskBadge.axaml), coloured from Bevel.Brush.Highlight/HighlightText so it renders in the active skin under every Win2000 scheme and Luna variant — never a hardcoded macOS red. Bevel.Brush.HighlightText was missing from LunaTokens.axaml and was added (it existed only in Win2000 Tokens/SchemeAliases). Grouped button's badge is the app's unread, explicitly NOT the '(N)' window-glomming count (R-TB-6).

FOLLOW-UP / NOT DONE: (a) on-device QA against real Slack — verified against System Settings / Beeper / AyuGram badges, not Slack itself; (b) site/index.html not updated (no Render* harvest for a badged strip yet) — left alone to avoid colliding with the parallel taskbar work; (c) an icon-overlay layout (option 1) as a setting, if wanted later.

Full suite green: 998 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped.
## Re-raised by the user 2026-09-29

Asked for again in the same breath as the missing attention/flash state: 'supporting badges like message counts'. So this is wanted, not nice-to-have.

STATUS CHECK NEEDED before doing more: commit 2d01f71 'feat(taskbar): unread badge on task buttons, sourced from the Dock' and merge 5bea58c are already in the tree, so some or all of desired-UX option (1) may be implemented. Verify on device what actually shows today against a real badge-bearing app (Slack, Messages) before starting fresh — and if it works, close this rather than rebuild it.

Shares its Dock AX source with the new attention-state bead filed alongside this note.

title: Downloads stack: macOS-like grid with content previews
description:
## Problem
The taskbar Downloads stack (bevel-12g) ships as a Win2000 list flyout: 16×16 file-type icons + name, newest-first. On macOS Dock, Downloads opens as a fan/grid of content previews (image/PDF/doc thumbnails, not just generic type icons). Live feedback: the stack should feel more macOS-like — grid layout with real previews.

## Context
- Stack: StackViewModel / StackFileViewModel (MaxItems=16, IconLoader at 16px)
- UI: TaskbarView.axaml ItemsControl → horizontal icon+name rows in a Popup
- bevel-12g close notes explicitly left open: "popup style (Win2000 list vs macOS grid)"
- opportunity-map also lists in-Explorer Quick Look / rich Details — out of scope unless this turns out to mean Explorer; prefer stack first given ~/Downloads default TaskbarStacks

## Acceptance
- Stack flyout can present as a macOS-style grid (or fan) of recent items
- Each cell shows a content preview/thumbnail when the platform can produce one (images at minimum; PDF/others best-effort via existing IIconProvider / QLThumbnail path if any), falling back to a larger type icon
- Still opens via LaunchServices; Open folder row retained; HasNew cue unchanged
- Icons/previews load off UI thread (existing IconLoader pattern)
- Fake PAL / tests cover grid path without requiring real QL

## Non-goals (unless clarified)
- Full Finder Quick Look Space preview in Explorer (separate opportunity-map item)
- Stacks settings editor UI (opportunity-map S/M)
acceptance_criteria: Grid/fan stack flyout with content previews (images+fallback); LaunchServices open; off-thread load; tests/fake PAL
notes:
## Two real bugs found + fixed post-review (2026-09-25, commit 946c65b)

nuclear-pr-review on the merged batch found the layered-cache defect the original work missed.

MacOSThumbnailProvider correctly keys its cache on path + LastWriteTimeUtc.Ticks and ships a test for
invalidation-on-rewrite. But PreviewLoader ABOVE it cached by path alone, forever — so that invalidation
was unreachable in the real call path, and the provider's test was passing over dead code.

Bug 1: a file re-downloaded under the same name kept showing the PREVIOUS download's preview
indefinitely. Trim only reacts to a path leaving the listing, which a same-name replacement never does.

Bug 2: the stack's watcher fires on create, so a download's first preview is routinely attempted against
a partially-written file. That decode fails, the cell falls back to a type icon — and the fallback was
then cached forever, so the cell never upgraded once the download completed.

One mechanism fixes both: carry the last-write stamp that RecentEntries ALREADY reads in order to sort
(new StackEntry record), and reuse a cached entry only while that stamp still matches. A changed stamp
means a different file or a finished download, so both re-decode; a genuinely undecodable file keeps its
stamp and is not re-attempted on every refresh.

Design constraint worth remembering: the stamp comes from the caller, NOT a stat inside LoadAsync,
because EnsurePreview is invoked from inside a Dispatcher.UIThread.InvokeAsync — a stat there would be
file I/O on the UI thread.

Tests: both failure modes pinned in StackTests, and verified to FAIL against the previous path-only
behaviour (temporarily reverted to confirm red, then restored). RecentEntries now also asserts the stamp
is really carried rather than defaulted to 0. Full suite 1085 passed / 0 failed / 2 skipped.

Still open for this bead: the on-device QA list above (real HEIC/RAW/large PDFs on Retina, flyout
placement, drag-out, keyboard arrowing, 16 concurrent decodes on a cold ~/Downloads).

title: Two-row taskbar: tray icons taller than available row height
description:
## Why
User report: on a two-row taskbar, tray icons sometimes take more vertical space than they have — icons overflow / clip the tray band (machine-specific).

## What
Tray icon size is settings-driven (`TaskbarTrayIconSize`, default likely 16) and may not clamp to per-row content height when `Rows=2` (`TaskbarTheme.HeightForRows` / `RowHeight`). Scale/DPI or wrap layout may also inflate preferred height beyond the tray host. Audit tray ItemsControl/WrapPanel measure vs bar height on multi-row layouts.

## Acceptance
- With 2 rows, tray icons fit within the tray strip (no vertical overflow past the bar)
- Icon size setting still works but is capped by available row height
- Reproduced on a multi-row taskbar at non-1.0 scale if that was the machine trigger
notes:
## Fixed (2026-09-23), merged to main

Root cause: TrayItemViewModel.IconW/IconH = native menu-bar item size x slider scale, with NO upper
bound, bound to the tray Image's explicit Width/Height; TrayRowsPanel.MeasureOverride then reports
maxIconHeight x rows. The helper (TrayServiceImpl.swift:381) admits status items up to 40pt, and a
notched MacBook Pro's menu-bar band is ~37pt. Available tray content at Rows=2 is HeightForRows(2)=58pt
minus 2pt TrayArea margin minus 2x2pt sunken-well border = 52pt => 26pt/row. Two 37pt rows = 74pt, spill.

Non-1.0 display scale is NOT required to reproduce — the whole path is DIP/points. The trigger is the
host's menu-bar item height (or a slider value >~18), which is why it looked machine-specific. The bug
class was never limited to 2 rows: the default slider at 24 already wanted 33pt on a 30pt single-row bar.

Fix: TrayViewModel.MaxIconHeight(rows) derives a per-row budget from the live TaskbarTheme metrics
(HeightForRows(rows) - 6pt well chrome, / rows), pushed onto items from all three entry points (SetRows,
Configure, Upsert). TrayItemViewModel.SetMaxHeight applies a uniform Fit factor to BOTH axes, so an
over-tall icon scales down with aspect preserved — no squash, no clipping. Below the cap the slider
behaves exactly as before. Tray sizing stays independent of task-button sizing (bevel-c54t).

Rejected during the work: clamping in TrayRowsPanel.MeasureOverride. An Avalonia child with an explicit
Height ignores the offered height (it centres and overflows — measured 57pt inside a 52pt strip), so the
clamp must live at the size source. That prototype was reverted rather than left as dead weight.

Files: src/Bevel.Taskbar/Model/TrayViewModel.cs, tests/Bevel.Taskbar.Tests/TrayIconHeightCapTests.cs
(new, 5 tests, all verified red before the fix), tests/Bevel.Taskbar.Tests/TrayViewModelTests.cs
(gained [Collection("TaskbarTheme")] since it now reads shared theme metrics). No changes to
TaskbarView.axaml/.cs, SettingsService.cs or TaskbarTheme.

Verified on main after merge: full solution suite 989 passed / 0 failed / 2 skipped.

### Known interaction to re-verify
The cap is derived from TaskbarTheme.HeightForRows, and bevel-c54t (big-icons mode) changes those
metrics. When c54t lands, the numeric assertions in TrayIconHeightCapTests (24pt at 1 row, 26pt at 2,
Normal tier) may legitimately move. Re-run and re-baseline deliberately, do not weaken the assertions.

### Remaining before close: on-device QA
No real notched-Mac status-item height was sampled; the 37pt figure comes from the helper's accepted
8-40pt range, not a live capture. The cap is derived from the bar rather than a guessed native height,
so it holds across that whole range — but a visual check at Rows=2 on the reporting machine is wanted.

title: Disable or remappable click-again-to-minimize on task buttons
description:
## Why
User request: turn off Win2000-style click-again-to-minimize on task buttons, or move it to a different click (e.g. middle / Option+click). Linked to bevel-hx63 — when IsFocused/focus tracking is wrong, a click meant to raise Arc instead minimizes it, which makes the focus-steal feel worse.

## What
Today TaskItemViewModel.ToggleAsync: minimized→restore+activate, focused→minimize, else→activate. Add a setting (default off or keep classic?) to disable minimize-on-reclick, and/or bind minimize to a modifier/alternate click. Keep classic behavior available for fidelity.

## Acceptance
- User can disable click-to-minimize while keeping click-to-activate
- Optional alternate chord for minimize still works if offered
- Default choice documented (fidelity vs. modern macOS expectation)
notes:
## Implemented (2026-09-23), merged to main

### Staleness question (the blocker premise) — answered with evidence
IsFocused CAN go stale, but only in one narrow, unreproduced shape. So the setting shipped and NO
freshness machinery was added.

Evidence (ShellModel.cs): IsFocused is written only via ApplyExclusiveFocus -> SetFocused from four sites
(OnWindowOpened, OnForegroundChanged, OnWindowClosed, the 2s Reconcile). Update(ForeignWindow) genuinely
does ignore per-event flags — that comment is accurate. OnForegroundChanged calls
ApplyExclusiveFocus(w.Id.Value) for ANY reported foreground window including one failing EarnsButton, so
no VM matches and every button unpresses: the normal path self-corrects and any lag is just the
Dispatcher.Post hop (sub-frame).

The real hole is the backstop: ApplyFocusFromSnapshot is DELIBERATELY sticky — when a reconcile snapshot
names no focused window it re-applies the previous focused id rather than clearing (guarding a transient
all-false enumeration). So if the foreground moves to something the helper never reports as focused
(Spotlight-ish system UI, an unreported full-screen app, a dropped event stream), IsFocused stays true
indefinitely and a click meant to raise would minimize.

Not gated, deliberately: the only correct confirmation is a new per-platform frontmost probe plus a
pid/bundle match on the VM (the VM has only BundleId; TaskbarNative.FrontmostAppPid returns a pid), or a
full EnumerateAsync round-trip per reclick. Both are machinery for a symptom not reproduced since
bevel-hx63 was fixed, and this setting is an immediate user-level escape hatch. The hole and the exact
shape of the fix if it IS reproduced are written up in docs/design/taskbar-reclick-minimize.md.

### Shipped
Setting: taskbarReclickMinimize, enum TaskbarReclickMinimize { Click, OptionClick, Never },
DEFAULT = Click (classic Win2000, on for everyone).
Default justification: fidelity here is FUNCTION — minimize-on-reclick is one of the two things a Windows
taskbar button does. The reported 'click buried my window' case was the hx63 handback, not a minimize;
changing a default to route around a bug would have left the bug in place AND lost the behaviour. Modern
expectation is served as a choice, not as a new default.

Alternate chord: OptionClick mode — plain click raises, Option (macOS) / Alt (Windows) + click minimizes.
Middle-click was already taken by taskbarMiddleClickCloses, and Option is already Bevel's 'other verb'
modifier on this control (Quit -> Force Quit). The modifier is read from LIVE platform state at click time
(TaskbarNative.OptionKeyDown; new WindowsTaskbarNative.AltKeyDown via GetAsyncKeyState), never from an
input event — the bar is non-activating, and a live read also covers keyboard Space/Enter activation.

Surfaced: Settings > Taskbar > Window buttons > 'Re-click' combo, directly under middle-click-closes. The
middle item is relabelled at load in the host platform's vocabulary. No platform gating needed (works on
both real PALs). Live-applies with no restart; StatusText follows the mode so the accessible hint never
promises a minimize the click won't perform.

Files: SettingsService.cs (additive only — one SetOrPrune, one parse, one property, one enum; no
reordering, which is why it merged cleanly with c54t), NEW Model/TaskButtonClickPolicy.cs,
Model/TaskItemViewModel.cs (ctor seam + StatusText + ToggleAsync only, nothing else — clean merge with
ijln), TaskbarView.axaml.cs (two one-line pushes into the shared policy), WindowsTaskbarNative.cs
(AltKeyDown), OnboardingWindow.axaml/.cs, NEW docs/design/taskbar-reclick-minimize.md, CODEMAP.md nav
line, NEW tests/Bevel.Taskbar.Tests/TaskButtonReclickTests.cs, tests/Bevel.Core.Tests/SettingsServiceTests.cs.

Tests: 14 taskbar (verified present and green after integration) + 5 core. Classic minimizes on reclick;
Never activates instead with no optimistic un-press; OptionClick raises bare / minimizes with the chord;
the chord is re-read live per click; restore-when-minimized and activate-when-unfocused hold in all three
modes; StatusText per mode; a policy-less VM follows Shared. Core: default is Click and pruned from the
blob, both non-default modes round-trip the SerializeBlob/ProjectBlob peer-snapshot seam (the mechanism
peers actually read settings through), a garbage value falls back to Click, save/load round-trips.

### Integration note
Merge conflicted with bevel-c54t in OnboardingWindow.axaml.cs — both added a settings row to the same
seeding block. Resolved by hand keeping BOTH (au94's two reclick lines + c54t's ButtonSizeCombo with the
Big=3 comment). Verified afterwards: full suite 1021 passed / 0 failed / 2 skipped, and the new reclick
test class runs 14/14, so nothing was dropped in the resolution.

### Remaining before close: on-device QA
1. OptionClick on a real bar — the modifier probe is native and cannot be exercised headless (tests inject
   the seam). Also confirm Option+click doesn't collide with any AppKit Option-click behaviour.
2. AltKeyDown() on Windows — written by symmetry, never executed on this machine.
3. The sticky-focus scenario: move the foreground to Spotlight / a full-screen app and check whether any
   button stays pressed. If it does, that IS the reproduction the design doc's follow-up is written for.
4. Visual pass on Settings > Taskbar — one combo row added and that panel is scroll-height sensitive.

title: macOS Zoom ignores Bevel taskbar height
description:
## Why
User report: macOS window Zoom (green button / zoom-to-fit) does not respect Bevel's taskbar size — zoomed windows cover the bar / use the full screen instead of the usable area above it.

## What
macOS Zoom uses NSScreen.visibleFrame (Dock + menu bar insets). Bevel's bar is a utility window and does not shrink visibleFrame unless we either (a) reserve space via Dock-shim / work-area strategy, or (b) intercept/resize zoomed windows (WorkAreaMitigator Nudge). Confirm which strategy is active and why Zoom still fills over the bar.

## Acceptance
- Zoomed windows end above Bevel's taskbar (no overlap)
- Works with Dock auto-hide / Dock-shim settings as documented
notes:
## Diagnosed + mitigated (2026-09-23), merged to main

### Read this first: the acceptance criterion as written is NOT achievable
'Zoomed windows end above Bevel's taskbar (no overlap)' can only be met in the 'corrected within <1s'
sense. Zoom will still momentarily cover the bar before snapping up. Reserving space is genuinely
unavailable on macOS:
 - NSScreen.visibleFrame is computed by the system from the menu bar + Dock only, never from a
   third-party utility window, and AppKit's zoom: always animates into it.
 - docs/spike/2026-07-12-dock-inset-measurement.md records the Dock inset was not measurable on the
   reference machine, and strict mode forces a visible Dock against the user's preference.
 - Spec Req 9.5 rules out the private SkyLight work-area symbols.
So Zoom can be CORRECTED, not PREVENTED. This is now stated in the engine's doc comment, made normative
in spec 02 Req 9.2, and surfaced in the work-area setting's own description so users aren't misled.
If a true no-overlap guarantee is wanted, that is a different (Dock-shim / strict reservation) bead with
the documented cost of forcing the Dock visible.

### Active strategy
WorkAreaStrategy.Nudge is the hard default (SettingsService.cs:596/710, spec 02 Req 9.1/9.2). Verified the
Nudge path is fully plumbed end to end in the split shell: App.axaml.cs:418 wires WorkAreaMitigator in the
taskbar process -> ShellCoreWindowManager (SupportsReposition: true) -> ShellCoreServer Reposition ->
MacOSWindowManager.RepositionAsync -> helper repositionWindow (AXPosition/AXSize in top-left global points,
the same space as kCGWindowBounds, so the band comparison is apples-to-apples). The helper does emit .moved
on frame changes (reconcile diff, 500ms + kAXMoved/ResizedNotification). Band geometry comes from the single
source of truth (TaskbarTheme.HeightForRows via TaskbarGeometry.WorkAreaBand) — NOT touched or duplicated,
so bevel-c54t's big-icons bar height flows through unchanged.

### Root cause of the lingering overlap — two zoom-specific defects in WorkAreaMitigator
1. Progress-blind rate limiter. _lastReposition[id] recorded OUR OWN attempt time, so any further
   correction of that window was refused for 2s. An AppKit zoom is an animation INTO visibleFrame, so its
   final frame can land AFTER our correction, and a re-zoom seconds later presents a fresh overlap — both
   were locked out by the cooldown. The window sat over the bar until the limiter expired and the 3s
   safety poll came round (~2-5s, or apparently permanently while the user kept interacting).
2. No verification after a correction. Nothing re-checked a nudged window, so an animation's final frame
   arriving with no further AX event was only caught by the 3s safety poll.

### Fix
 - Rate limiting now keys on the OFFENDING FRAME: back off only when a window returns at the exact frame
   we just corrected within 2s (the genuine reposition fight Req 9.2 targets). A different frame = real
   motion -> corrected immediately. A window observed clear of the band forgets its back-off.
 - One verify pass 400ms after each correction (chained <=3 deep, superseded by real activity), so an
   animation landing on top of our nudge is fixed in <1s.
 - FakeWindowManager.RepositionAsync was a NO-OP; it now applies the move and raises WindowChanged, making
   the whole Nudge path observable under --pal=fake and testable without a Mac. (That no-op is why this
   regression class had no coverage before.)

Files: src/Bevel.Taskbar/WorkAreaMitigator.cs, src/Bevel.Pal.Fake/FakePal.cs,
src/Bevel.Taskbar/OnboardingWindow.axaml (one description line + TextWrapping),
docs/spec/02-macos-platform.md, tests/Bevel.Taskbar.Tests/WorkAreaMitigatorTests.cs.
No Swift helper and no .proto changes.

Tests: 4 new + 1 existing clarified — zoom landing after a correction is fixed inside the cooldown;
back-off cleared by a clean observation (re-zoom corrected at once); same-frame re-assertion still backs
off; verify pass fires with no window event (real clock, Windows-skipped like its sibling); engine drives
the real Fake PAL end to end until no window crosses the band.

Verified on main after merge: full solution suite 1002 passed / 0 failed / 2 skipped.

### Remaining before close: on-device QA (this is inherently behavioural)
1. build-app.sh && dev-sign.sh, launch launcher, confirm Nudge is the selected strategy.
2. Green-button Zoom Finder/Safari/TextEdit -> fills, then snaps up off the bar in well under a second.
   Repeat rapidly (zoom/unzoom/zoom within 2s) — previously the SECOND zoom stayed over the bar.
3. Window > Zoom and option-double-click the title bar (same zoom: path).
4. Dock auto-hide ON (Bevel's default claim) and OFF (defaults write com.apple.dock autohide false;
   killall Dock) — identical behaviour; with the Dock visible the zoom target is shorter, so watch for
   double-correction jitter.
5. Multi-row / big-icons bar (taller band) and a resolution change while a window is zoomed
   (WorkAreaChanged -> RequestMitigation).
6. An app that re-asserts its own frame (terminal with fixed geometry) must not enter a reposition fight:
   at most one nudge per 2s.
7. Sanity: Bevel's own bar must never be moved (excluded via kCGWindowLayer != 0) — worth eyeballing once
   now that the engine's decisions fire more often.

title: Windows taskbar sits too high and ignores display-size changes
description:
## Why
On Windows the bar often parks above an empty strip the same height as the native taskbar, and it does not re-anchor when the resolution or work area changes.

Causes:
- Hide Shell_TrayWnd does not clear Explorer's AppBar reservation, so rcWork still insets the bottom. Windows then clamps our borderless window into that work area.
- OnOpened never re-positions after Screens is ready / after the native bar is hidden (constructor may have run with no screen list).
- PositionAtPrimaryDisplayBottom subtracts a DIP height from a pixel Bounds and assigns pixel Width to a DIP property — wrong on any scale ≠ 1.
- Screens.Changed often does not fire for work-area-only changes; IDesktopEnvironment.MonitorsChanged is unused by the window.
- SetAlwaysOnTop / tool-window styles are macOS-only, so the Win32 window is a normal overlapped window subject to work-area clamping.

## What
- After claiming the edge: hide native bars, SPI_SETWORKAREA to full rcMonitor with SPIF_SENDCHANGE, then re-anchor.
- Re-position on OnOpened, after dock claim, on Screens.Changed AND MonitorsChanged.
- Fix DIP vs device-pixel math; set WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW|TOPMOST and SetWindowPos to the true bottom.

## Acceptance
- Bar sits on the physical bottom of the primary monitor after the native taskbar is hidden.
- Changing resolution / adding a monitor / hiding the native bar re-anchors width and Y.
notes: Fix in tree: hide Shell_TrayWnd now ResetWorkAreasToFull+SPIF_SENDCHANGE; OnOpened re-anchors after claim; DIP vs pixel math (TaskbarGeometry); WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW|TOPMOST+SetWindowPos; MonitorsChanged subscription. Tests: TaskbarGeometryTests. Pending Windows-box deploy.

title: ShellCoreSystemTrayHost duplicates tray capabilities instead of forwarding the core's
description: The taskbar-role tray proxy reports Capabilities from a per-platform literal rather than from the core's actual PAL. It was hardcoded to TrayMode=Mirrored with a 'macos-tray' note while backing the taskbar on every platform, so on Windows it claimed to mirror a menu bar that does not exist and anything gating on TrayMode got the macOS answer everywhere (this defeated the settings-dialog platform gate until corrected). Now reported per-platform, which is right in practice but still duplicates truth that belongs to the core. Proper fix: carry Capabilities in the shell-core snapshot and have the proxy report them verbatim, so a single source of truth survives future PALs.

title: macOS 26: ~25 status items expose no capturable pixels in ANY window (limited-mode fallback is correct)
description:
After fixing the self-test gate (bevel-p6g4), live tray capture works: 61/86 items mirror real glyphs. The remaining 25 are NOT a missing-image failure — measured noImage=0, blank=25: LegacyWindowCapture returns a correctly-sized CGImage (e.g. 48x60, 36x60) but every pixel is transparent, so pngFromCGImage rejects it and the item keeps its limited-mode app icon.

Geometry probe (/tmp/bevel-geo.log): 92 of 109 status windows sit off-screen around x=-6785..-5775 (the hide zone). Off-screen is NOT the discriminator — most of the 61 successful captures are ALSO off-screen, confirming LegacyWindowCapture works there as designed. The split is per-app and positionally interleaved: Caffeine, Cloudflare WARP, MouseAssistant, AdGuard, AyuGram, EXO and Jump Desktop capture fine while their immediate neighbours Bitwarden, Beeper, Nessie, flameshot, Syncthing, Spotlight and Parallels Toolbox come back blank. Leading hypothesis: some apps stop repainting their status item once it is fully off every display, so the backing store is discarded; others keep a live layer.

Note docs/design/menubar-management.md claims 4/4 for this path; the real-world rate on a heavily-populated bar is 71%. Worth re-measuring that claim.

Repro: BEVEL_DEBUG_TRAY=1, read 'captured N/M items live (noImage= blank=)'.
notes:
CONCLUSION (2026-09-12): not a Bevel capture bug. SIX hypotheses tested and disproven with measurements:

1. Capture opt-out (sharingType=.none) — NO. All status windows: share=1 alpha=1.00 store=1, blanks and renders identical.
2. Reader bug in trimTransparent — NO. Peak alpha and peak RGB measured after normalising into the same sRGB premultipliedLast context: blanks are a00 rgb00, genuinely all-zero. Format (alphaInfo=2, bpp32) and geometry (2x point size) match the working ones.
3. Apps stop repainting off-screen — NO. With Ice quit, 18 of 26 blanks are ON-SCREEN in the visible bar.
4. Different owning process — NO. All 106 ControlCenter status windows share pid 1446 (77 ok + 29 blank).
5. Ice / UseIceBar interaction — NO. Quit Ice entirely and re-measured: 63/87 live, blank=24 (vs 61/86, blank=25 with Ice running). Essentially unchanged. The +1880 twin pairing seen earlier was an artifact of Ice's duplicate stash; with Ice gone each item has exactly ONE window and no blank overlaps any rendered window.
6. SCK composited fallback for on-screen blanks — NO. Implemented and measured: recovered 0 of 25. Reverted.

EXHAUSTIVE WINDOW SWEEP: ControlCenter owns ONLY layer-25 windows (113, no composite window). Widening to ALL windows in the menu-bar band (any layer, any owner, y<=40, h<=44) finds nothing but WindowServer's StatusIndicator and an unrelated ThemeWidget. There is NO window anywhere containing these items' glyphs.

So on macOS 26 (25G229) roughly a quarter of status items are composited by WindowServer without exposing per-item window content that either CGWindowListCreateImageFromArray or ScreenCaptureKit can read. Two independent capture APIs agree the window is empty because it IS empty. Name-kind correlates but is not deterministic: Control-Centre-internal names (Item-N, Clock, NowPlaying, BentoBox, ...) render 41/41 and empty names 9/9, while bundle-id-named windows split 27 render / 24 blank — the same app can land on both sides (com.bjango.istatmenus.status renders at w=24/36/54/128 but is blank at w=6).

CURRENT BEHAVIOUR IS CORRECT: those items fall back to the limited-mode app icon, which is the designed degradation (S5.5). Live rate on this machine is 61-63 of 86-88.

REMAINING AVENUE (needs a spec decision): capture the menu bar region once and crop per item. captureWindow's old doc explicitly forbade this ('not a cropped full-screen grab - Req 5.3'), so it would change the requirement, and cropping a composited bar cannot preserve per-item transparency.

ALSO FIXED IN PASSING: the geometry probe wrote a fixed /tmp/bevel-geo.log, so a second live helper silently clobbered it and the probe reported stale data mid-investigation. Now PID-suffixed. Repro: touch /tmp/bevel-geo, run --role=core, read /tmp/bevel-geo-<pid>.log; or BEVEL_DEBUG_TRAY=1 for 'captured N/M items live (noImage= blank=)'.

title: [bug] First Filer open sometimes does nothing (2nd click works) in split mode
description:
User: clicking 'My Computer' (Start menu -> OpenExplorerAt -> Program.SpawnExplorer('/')) opened nothing on the FIRST click; the 2nd click worked. On the R2R build.

Investigation (2026-08-20): could NOT reproduce a hard failure on a clean installed shell — a single 'bevelctl open /' reliably spawns ONE --role=explorer process that stays alive 6s+ with no crash and no crash report; no spawn storm. Earlier '24 processes + Helper not connected' were DEV-TEST POLLUTION: (a) two shells (dev launcher + installed) contend on the single fixed automation socket path ~/.config/bevel/bevelctl.sock — last Start() wins and deletes the other's socket (a real fragility, see below); (b) a standalone 'dotnet run --role=explorer' with no BEVEL_CORE_TOKEN env hangs 5s in ReadNonce then throws (harness artifact; real explorers inherit the env). The explorer role does NOT use the helper — StartPollAsync/WorkAreaMitigator are inside CreateTaskbarSurface (taskbar-only); the 'Helper not connected' logs were the CORE's known startup race.

Leading hypothesis for the user's symptom: FIRST-explorer cold-start delay — a spawned explorer blocks first paint on Program.cs:87 (settingsLoad GetAwaiter().GetResult(), RemoteSettingsService.LoadAsync up to 5s) + CLR/Avalonia cold init; the first-of-session window can take seconds and look like 'never', the warm retry is instant. Candidate fixes: (1) don't block a PEER's first paint up to 5s on the settings connect — seed defaults fast + re-theme via the reconnect snapshot (short pre-paint timeout for explorer/desktop); (2) startup beads k93j(done)/yg7h.

FRAGILITY also found: the automation socket is a single fixed path; two shells clobber each other's socket (last-writer-wins) — a stray/old shell can silently kill the current one's bevelctl. Consider a liveness/ownership check or per-session path.

NEEDS from user: does it still happen on the current build? Is it EVERY first-of-session open, or was it a one-off? Does the window appear DELAYED (seconds) or TRULY never?
close_reason: Symptom deleted by bevel-t48y: the first open is now a Show dial to a parked pre-warmed filer (a frame), not a cold process start. Live-validated across multiple sessions (parked #1/#2/#3 handoffs in the restart log); user-confirmed.

title: Startup: defer the helper ScreenCaptureKit/AX tray self-test off the first-paint window
description: Measured: the Swift helper's tray self-test (ScreenCaptureKit + AX grant + liveMirroring) is ~1.3s to Ping-ready then ~4.8s more to 'liveMirroring=true', a ~5s 100%-CPU burst (t+2.5s..~8s) that overlaps taskbar paint and leaves the tray empty until it completes — the visible 'shell settles slowly / tray fills in late'. Already non-blocking to core serving (ShellCoreServer._server.Start() runs before SeedWhenHelperReadyAsync), but run the self-test at lower priority / after the taskbar's first frame so the visible shell settles before the mirroring CPU spike. native/helper-macos TrayServiceImpl self-test path.

title: Startup: ReadyToRun the published apphost to erase per-process JIT (N× cost)
description: Measured (startup investigation 2026-08-20): the shipped apphost brings each role to Main in ~0.15s and all 4 processes up in ~0.56s — but Debug/no-R2R IL means every process (launcher, core, taskbar, and each explorer) JITs the framework + Avalonia graph from scratch = the biggest MULTI-PROCESS cost paid N×. Fix: <PublishReadyToRun>true</PublishReadyToRun> on Bevel.App (+ owned assemblies) in the packaging publish (build-app.sh). Highest multi-process leverage, low risk. NativeAOT is a larger follow-on; R2R is the cheap 80%. Verify bundle still signs/notarizes + boots split.
close_reason: Added -p:PublishReadyToRun=true to build-app.sh PUBLISH_ARGS — crossgen the IL to native for the RID so each role process avoids cold JIT of the framework+Avalonia graph (the N× multi-process startup cost). Bundle builds/signs/notarizes/boots clean.

title: bug Automation socket (bevelctl / bevel://) only served by on-demand Filer in split mode
description: After role=all removal (bevel-dwhy), AutomationSocketHost (CompositionRoot.cs ~195) is registered only for role=Explorer. In split mode Explorer is on-demand, so bevelctl and bevel:// URLs don't work until an Explorer window process exists — previously role=all always served it, so 'open this folder in Bevel' from outside worked cold. The Start menu / desktop still open folders (they call Program.SpawnExplorer directly, not via the socket), so daily UI use is fine; only EXTERNAL automation is degraded. Fix: serve the automation socket from a PERSISTENT process — the core (headless, already always-on) or the taskbar — and have its window verbs spawn/route to an Explorer via the launcher (SpawnExplorer / a launcher control command). Consider that IShellAutomation window verbs need the live file manager, so the persistent server may need to spawn an Explorer to fulfill window-coupled verbs.
close_reason: Socket host + bevel:// + Apple Events moved to the persistent taskbar; role-aware IShellSurface (Explorer=in-process, others=SpawningShellSurface). open/reveal spawn --role=explorer (+ new --select= arg -> SelectAfterLoad); filesystem+launch verbs work directly; select/query-in-live-window return clear ShellNotRunning (deferred). Subteam+verifier SOUND, 9 tests, 829 green.

title: Start menu: show/hide the Desktop on demand (off by default)
description: User: the desktop is useless today and they always close it, so it must NOT spawn by default (keep split launcher spawning Core+Taskbar only). But it should be reachable from the Start menu — an entry that toggles the desktop surface on demand. In split mode the desktop is its own --role=desktop process, so the Start menu (taskbar process) must ask the LAUNCHER to spawn (or terminate) a desktop child: add a LauncherControl command (see src/Bevel.App/Supervision/LauncherControl.cs — RestartAll/RestartCore/Quit today) like SpawnDesktop/CloseDesktop, wire a launcher handler (RunLauncher command loop, Program.cs ~216) that adds/removes a RoleProcess(ShellRole.Desktop) under the supervisor, and add a Start-menu item ('Show Desktop' / toggle) that sends it over the launcher control socket the taskbar already inherits (LauncherControl.SocketEnv/TokenEnv). Reflect current state (shown/hidden) if feasible. Related: bevel-dwhy (role=all removal). Depends on dwhy landing first (desktop default-off).
close_reason: Start-menu Show/Hide Desktop toggle. Launcher SpawnDesktop/CloseDesktop/QueryDesktop verbs; supervisor mutable child set (close-before-kill => no auto-respawn of a hidden desktop; same CreateRoleStartInfo env as boot desktop). Start-menu item labels Show/Hide via launcher query at open; all off UI thread; degrades if unsupervised. Subteam+verifier SOUND, 7 tests, 837 green.

title: Taskbar lags on macOS Space (desktop) switch — no activeSpaceDidChange observer
description: Switching macOS Spaces takes 'a few rounds' for the taskbar to show the right windows. Helper (WindowServiceImpl.swift) observes didLaunch/didActivate + per-window AX notifications but NOT NSWorkspace.activeSpaceDidChangeNotification, so a Space switch gives no signal and only the >=1s/2s reconcile backstop catches it. 'A few rounds' because a mid-animation enumeration reads a stale on-screen set. Fix: add an activeSpaceDidChangeNotification observer next to the didActivate/didLaunch ones (~1419-1435); on fire poke an immediate reconcile after a ~250-400ms settle (post-animation), debounced. Event-driven fix — do NOT shorten the global reconcile interval (battery). NSWorkspace observers deliver on the main thread — mind the AX-run-loop-thread note.
close_reason: Helper now observes NSWorkspace.activeSpaceDidChangeNotification and fires a single debounced reconcile() ~300ms post-animation (coalesced via cancel/replace DispatchWorkItem), reusing the poll's enumerate+diff+broadcast so the taskbar snaps to the new Space's windows instead of waiting for the 500ms backstop. Observer + work item torn down in shutdown(); [weak self]. Benign occasional overlap with the poll reconcile (self-healing). Subteam+verifier SOUND; helper builds; no .NET change. Commit bfd301a.

title: First window-minimize after granting Screen Recording hitches the UI (one-time warmup)
description:
User-observed: the FIRST time an Explorer window is minimized after Screen Recording is granted, the shell freezes briefly, then recovers and never recurs (confirmed: 2nd minimize instant; live sampling of the single-process role=all app showed the main thread idle in the event loop except for transient .NET JIT frames — genssStructReturn/fgMorphSmpOp/LinearScan::allocateRegisters — no sustained block, no deadlock).

Cause (inferred, not yet caught mid-freeze): first-run warmup on the UI thread — JIT of the minimize->taskbar-update->capture path + the first live ScreenCaptureKit init (initial SCShareableContent establishes a CGS/WindowServer connection, slow cold). Only surfaced now because Screen Recording was just granted, so live mirroring/thumbnail capture became active for the first time.

Fix: (1) audit the window-state-change / thumbnail-capture path (TaskbarView.CaptureWindowAsync @ ~675, ShellModel window-change handlers) to GUARANTEE no capture/enumeration/helper-RPC is awaited on the UI thread — it must be fully off-thread with only the cheap result marshaled back (ties to the audit's 'CaptureWindow RPC no timeout' findings). (2) Pre-warm ScreenCaptureKit off-thread right after the grant / at helper start (a throwaway SCShareableContent fetch) so the first real capture is warm. (3) Optionally warm the minimize path.

To catch the exact cold stack: fresh-restart Bevel (cold JIT) + prime a 2s-slice sampler + trigger the FIRST minimize; the blocking frame will show which call is on-thread.
close_reason: Pre-warm ScreenCaptureKit in the helper (detached, CGPreflight-gated so no prompt, retries for grant-after-start) so the first live capture isn't cold; added the missing intrinsic timeout to the window-capture RPC (MacOSWindowManager 3s, ShellCoreWindowManager 5s, Swift-side timeout) with static-icon fallback — also resolves the audit's 'CaptureWindow RPC no timeout' finding. Root cause was first-run warmup (JIT + cold SCK CGS init), not a deadlock. Subteam: investigate+implement+2 verifiers SOUND. 802 tests green, Swift helper builds, notarized bundle installed to /Applications.

title: App/Core/UI backlog: settings CAS concurrency, theme-swap atomicity, MMF reader-role split, trash-restore parity, Glyph brush cache

(2) A failed ThemeService.Apply leaves the colour engine and template engine disagreeing about the active theme — gate ThemeVariants/Font/CrispBevels on Apply success, or re-apply for Current not the requested id (adversarial P2). (5) Glyphs brush accessors are properties re-resolved+reallocated on every icon build — cache per token per theme state, invalidated on theme/scheme/variant Apply (performance P2). Test gaps: supervisor restart-vs-stop race, settings concurrent-writers, MMF cross-process corruption/stress, trash-restore cases, theme-apply-throws consistency.

title: Filer: virtualize wrap-panel + O(n^2) InsertSorted + watcher-vs-search + Open-With wire-up + reconcile re-sort
description: ce-code-review session D backlog. (1) VirtualizingWrapPanel realizes EVERY item (icon/list/thumbnail views) not just the viewport — the tracked M2 TODO; adopt a true VirtualizingPanel like Details view (performance P1). (2) Streamed InsertSorted is O(n^2) via per-item List.Insert; merge each 32-item chunk in one O(n) pass or defer to one sort at stream end (performance P2). title: Consolidate four parallel browser bundle-id tables into one registry
description: ce-code-review session A, maintainability anchor 100. MacOSTabProvider.Apps / TabFaviconStore.Apps / GeckoSessionStore.DataRoots / GeckoTabEngine.BundleIds are four independently-maintained tables (grown one-per-commit a40b→osad→l17f); adding a browser means editing 3-4 files and a browser can end up half-wired. Blast radius also touches TaskbarGrouping.cs + MacOSWindowManager.cs (out of session scope). Add a parameterized set-equality test across the tables to catch drift.

title: Tab provider: Gecko dialect (Zen, Firefox) via accessibility — enumerate + AXPress activation
description:
Extend bevel-a40b's ITabProvider to Firefox-family browsers, verified live on the Studio against Zen (app.zen-browser.zen, 86-tab session) 2026-08-17:

- AppleScript is a dead end: Zen/Firefox expose the basic suite only — 'tab' is not a class in the dictionary (script fails to compile). The existing osascript path cannot serve this family.
- AX is the lever: every tab (including Zen's vertical sidebar) is an AXRadioButton, subrole AXTabButton, roleDescription 'tab', inside an AXTabGroup, with actions AXShowMenu/AXScrollToVisible/AXPress. AXPress switches the tab. Titles match the session store exactly. Probe source: scratchpad ax_probe.swift (this session).
- Session store recovery.jsonlz4 (mozLz4: 'mozLz40\0' magic + LE u32 size + LZ4 block) in the profile gives titles+URLs+pinned+selected promptlessly (~15 s freshness), but ordering vs the AX strip is not guaranteed across pinned tabs/workspaces.

Design: enumerate AND activate from the SAME source (AX) so tab indices can never disagree — walk app windows → AXTabGroup → AXTabButton children (title, window index, tab index); ActivateAsync re-walks and AXPresses by index (title-guarded). URLs stay null like the iTerm dialect (or optionally enrich titles from the session store by title match). Implementation seat: either C# P/Invoke of the AX C API alongside the existing ObjC interop in Bevel.Pal.MacOS (all roles share the pl.ikari.bevel AX grant), or a helper RPC — decide at build time. Update SupportsApp declines-firefox/zen tests to the new expectation.
close_reason: Shipped: GeckoTabEngine (AX enumerate + AXPress activate) verified live against Zen (84 tabs, round-trip); Opus review HIGHs fixed (truncation-safe press policy, CF type guards, interop cache races); deferred items in bevel-y3cl.

title: macOS 26: resolve real names for Control-Center-owned tray items (most show as generic 'Item')
description: On macOS 26 nearly all menu-bar status items are owned by the Control Center process with no bundle id and a generic window name, so TrayServiceImpl identity resolution falls back to 'Item' for ~most of them (observed: 30+/43 items named 'Item'). Improve resolution: mine kCGWindowName variants, owner-PID executable/bundle heuristics, known Apple menuextra keys, and per-item icon signatures. Goal: human names/tooltips in the mirrored tray instead of a wall of 'Item'.

title: feature Redesign Filer left sidebars as faithful vector era presets
description: Replace the current rough InfoPane presets with beautiful, source-faithful, resolution-independent Explorer sidebars. Cover Windows 2000/Me Web View, Windows XP Common Tasks, and at least one later navigation-pane interpretation. Preserve the best composition, hierarchy, states, and interactions of each inspiration while drawing all chrome/illustration as Avalonia vector geometry and gradients—no bitmap UI assets. Generalize the Explorer Bar host so pane mode and visual era are not conflated.
design: Treat content mode (Folders/Search/History/Favorites/Details) separately from visual era. Start from authentic Win2000/Me Web View and XP Common Tasks anatomy, then derive a restrained later navigation pane. Use semantic theme tokens and reusable vector glyphs rather than hardcoded bitmap reproductions.

title: Online updates for Bevel (check, download, apply new versions)
description: Bevel should be able to check for a newer version online, download it, and apply it (Sparkle-style). Groundwork: the 'Restart Bevel' Start-menu action becomes a full quit+relaunch and relabels to 'Restart to upgrade' when a newer on-disk binary is detected (bevel-7hf4 sibling work). This bead tracks the ONLINE half: an update feed/endpoint, background version check, secure download + signature verification, and swap-in on restart. macOS: consider Sparkle or a custom notarized-DMG flow. Depends on stable code-signing (already have pl.ikari.bevel).
notes:
## Cadence half shipped (2026-09-29, commit bd06c32)

Implemented: UpdateCheckPolicy (pure: enabled/due/delay/jitter/clamp), UpdateCheckState (persisted
last-check), IUpdateSource (the seam), UpdateCheckService (the loop, CORE ROLE ONLY). 24 tests.
Settings: updateFeedUrl (default EMPTY = disabled) and updateCheckIntervalHours (default 8, clamped 1..168).

NOT implemented, deliberately: the feed format and the apply step. UPD-01 settled on Velopack for every
platform, so inventing a wire contract here would pre-empt bevel-ym0 and create a second format to
migrate off. NoUpdateSource is registered explicitly so 'no source on this build' is a stated fact in the
container rather than an unbound dependency.

### Still blocked on, in order
1. **No feed endpoint.** site/index.html is unpublished, and publishing is gated on bevel-legal-branding
   (the theme names and era framing on that page ARE the trade dress counsel must clear). Nothing to
   point updateFeedUrl at.
2. **bevel-9po** - the 6 GitHub release environment secrets are unconfigured, so release-macos.yml
   cannot produce the signed artifacts a feed would serve.
3. **bevel-ym0** - Velopack wiring: implement IUpdateSource against its feed, plus TCC-grant survival
   across update (02 Req 11.6) and helper/launchd re-registration (ENG-070). That is the genuinely hard
   part, not the timer.
4. Surfacing the result in the UI. UpdateCheckService.Latest holds it; nothing reads it yet.

Note: this bead's description still says 'consider Sparkle or a custom notarized-DMG flow' - stale, and
00-master-plan R7 already marks that text superseded by UPD-01 (Velopack; Sparkle and MSIX rejected).

title: Hide mirrored icons from the macOS menu bar when Bevel owns them (Bartender-style)
description: User: when Bevel's tray owns/mirrors a menu-bar icon, also HIDE it from the macOS menu bar (de-duplicate), like Bartender/Ice. macOS has NO public API to hide another app's NSStatusItem. Approaches: (a) our own wide NSStatusItem that expands to push the others off the visible bar (Bartender/Ice technique) — helper-side, fragile across macOS versions + the notch; (b) Accessibility-driven manipulation. Sizable helper feature; needs its own TCC + live validation. Natural extension of the existing tray live-mirror (TrayServiceImpl). Design first: which icons to hide (owned/mirrored set), a reveal affordance, and the collapse mechanism.
notes: OVERLAY-HIDE proven viable (subteam design + PoC): a click-through borderless panel at level 26 covers the status-item strip; occluded-on-display items KEEP REDRAWING (PoC: clock id=14 prints CHANGED every 1s), fixing the live-updates freeze that off-screen push caused. Also makes clicks land directly (items never move) and retires the control NSStatusItem. NEXT: implement src/Bevel.Pal.MacOS/MacMenuBarOverlay.cs (mirror MacMenuBarControl; NSPanel via ObjC; frame = the mirrored tray items' x-range so the clock/Control-Center stay visible; ignoresMouseEvents; opaque menu-bar-matching bg), add NSRect-passing objc_msgSend + window setters to AppKitInterop.cs, swap MacOSSystemTrayHost.SetNativeTrayHiddenAsync to it (keep MacMenuBarControl off-screen push behind a per-app fallback flag). Design: docs/design/menubar-overlay-hide.md.

title: Tray live-mirror icons go stale / don't rebuild
description: User: tray icons often don't rebuild. Path: TrayServiceImpl live-mirrors menu-bar icons via ScreenCaptureKit on the 2s poll + diff; captureWindow returning empty PNG is intentionally dropped (:394) so the last-good icon sticks. So symptom = capture returns empty/stale (SCK reliability: window-id churn, throttling, or the item moved) and the stale icon persists. Runtime-only diagnosis (can't repro headless). Instrument captureWindow (log empty vs ok, item id/x/width, cadence) + consider: force a recapture on a longer heartbeat, invalidate on x/width change, or fall back to the app icon after N empties. Related: bevel-tnii (redundant 2s full re-ship).
notes: REFINED from a live screenshot: it's not stale-but-real icons — EVERY tray item renders the same generic placeholder square. So IconPng is coming through as a generic fallback (capture empty -> owning-app icon -> a default), not real menu-bar bytes. TrayViewModel.IconSource = TrayIconTint.Process(item.IconPng). Root issue is the SCK capture-mirror producing placeholders for ~all items. This weakens the whole capture-mirror model; see bevel-7hf4 (Ice-style hide) as the better direction — the user pointed there.

title: Apphost links /opt/homebrew brotli — breaks portability of signed builds

Consequences: (1) deploys fail on Macs without brew brotli at that exact path; (2) under hardened runtime, library validation rejects the brew lib (Team ID mismatch) unless disable-library-validation is granted — worked around 2026-08-06 by signing nested executables with the app entitlements in sign-app.sh. Root fix: build release artifacts with the official Microsoft .NET SDK (or bundle brotli and rewrite install names with install_name_tool), then the entitlement workaround for bevelctl can be dropped.

title: Redundant 2s full-ListWindows poll re-ships every window icon on top of the delta stream
description:
Redundant 2s full-ListWindows poll re-ships every window icon on top of the delta stream.

READY-TO-IMPLEMENT PLAN (Option A, icons-optional ListWindows) — scoped 2026-07-28, needs Swift toolchain (protoc-gen-swift) + a helper rebuild + an UNLOCKED session to live-validate icon behaviour:
- The waste: ShellModel.ReconcileLoopAsync (src/Bevel.Taskbar/Model/ShellModel.cs:163-184, ReconcileInterval=2s @ :291) calls _windows.EnumerateAsync → MacOSWindowManager.EnumerateAsync (MacOSWindowManager.cs:72-86) → helper ListWindows, which ALWAYS includes appIconPng (WindowServiceImpl.swift describe() :506-508). Reconcile (ShellModel.cs:197-241) only uses Id/Title/IsFocused/IsMinimized — never icons. Decode/render is already mitigated (icon cache + FNV-1a64 dedup; update path never touches IconSource). Remaining waste = IPC serialize/transfer + per-window ToByteArray() (MacOSWindowManager.cs:278) every 2s.
- Fix: add 'bool include_icons = N;' to ListWindowsRequest in proto/bevel.helper.v1.proto (default true keeps other callers). C# regenerates via Grpc.Tools on build. Run native/helper-macos/generate-proto.sh for the Swift .pb.swift. In describe()/enumerateWindows() skip win.appIconPng when !include_icons. MacOSWindowManager.EnumerateAsync sets include_icons=false for the reconcile poll (ShellModel is its only caller). Rebuild helper (build.sh).
- Trade-off: a window first surfaced BY the poll (a genuinely missed Opened delta) is icon-less until the next real delta — rare (helper's 500ms reconcile emits Opened WITH icons). Option B (per-window icon_hash gate) survives that but is more plumbing.
- Overlaps bevel-8ck (FIXED): the core also double-snapshots the tray. Same 'delta + periodic keyed reconcile carrying only identity, never heavy blobs' pattern as bevel-6nve.
notes: Assessed this session: the 2s reconcile backstop is a deliberate safety net (prunes a stale button from a missed Close that the Changes stream can't guarantee). The 're-ships icons' cost is PAYLOAD only — the helper caches icons per bundle-id so it doesn't re-RENDER, it just re-sends ~1KB/window every 2s (masked by the 16MB gRPC limit). The proper fix (id-only liveness enumeration on the reconcile path) needs a new lightweight helper RPC (ListWindowIds) — proto + Swift helper + client + regen + live validation. Marginal value vs cross-layer cost; deferred. NOT a quick interval bump (that would weaken the stale-button backstop).

title: Settings cross-process propagation is a wasteful 750ms full-blob poll; make it push
description: Every process runs a 750ms DispatcherTimer calling ReloadIfChangedAsync; ReadRowAsync (src/Bevel.Core/SettingsService.cs:228) always SELECTs the ENTIRE json blob just to compare a version int, and the timer defeats App Nap/idle (battery). Also App.axaml.cs:278 only wires FrequentCap on Changed, so most live settings do not reach a split-mode taskbar without restart. Fix (cheap): SELECT version first, fetch json only when it advanced. Fix (right): FSEvents watch on settings.db-wal or push via the shell-core CoreEvent broadcast, and fan every setting through ApplyLiveSettings cross-process.
notes: SHIPPED (6d6d940): version-probe — the 750ms poll now SELECTs only the version int on the no-change tick instead of the whole JSON blob (the core waste). PUSH ATTEMPTED + REVERTED this session: a FileSystemWatcher on the settings DB fired reliably for DIRECT file writes but NOT for SQLite's WAL write path (verified — direct write = 6 events, SQLite UpdateAsync = 0 within 5s), so a watcher-based push would MISS and regress propagation to the fallback interval. A reliable push needs the shell-core CoreEvent broadcast (the doc's original plan): writer signals core -> core broadcasts settings-changed -> UI processes reload. That's a cross-process feature, deferred. Poll stays at 750ms (cheap now).
close_reason: Core (and all-in-one) is now the SOLE opener+writer of settings.db; Taskbar/Explorer/Desktop use RemoteSettingsService (never touch SQLite) — snapshot on connect + SettingsChanged broadcast on write, RFC-7386 merge patches forwarded to core as sole writer, version-dedup, defaults-fallback startup. 750ms poll retired + CAS collapsed. role=all provably IPC-free. Split-taskbar tray-empty regression (shared client ate the on-connect TraySnapshot) fixed via a dedicated keyed 'settings' client. Subteam + 2 verifiers; 818 tests green. Commit 264f84f.

title: Settings load blocks first paint; parallelize startup

Fix: kick LoadAsync in parallel with BuildAvaloniaApp() and await at the first consumer (theme apply); consider a tiny theme+font fast-read split from the full blob.
close_reason: SettingsService.LoadAsync now kicked off-thread right after the Core early-return, overlapping SQLite open+parse with BuildAvaloniaApp()+host.Start(); awaited before StartWith (before dispatcher pumps). Committed e351dfd; live-verified clean boot.

title: Start menu: unify shell-management actions + fix Luna 'Log Off' mislabel

title: SPIKE: represent running-but-windowless apps in the taskbar (macOS dock-dot concept)
description:
Our taskbar is window-centric (button per window). A macOS app can be RUNNING with zero windows (closed all, didn't quit; document app between documents) — dock shows a running dot, clicking reopens a window (applicationShouldHandleReopen). Today such an app has NO taskbar button -> invisible + unreachable from the bar.

SPIKE FIRST: instrument how often this happens in practice and for which apps (real daily pain vs rare) before committing to UI.

OPTIONS:
- A. Nothing (current).

title: Frequency-based app suggestions: exclude-open filter + OS usage seeding
description:
## Motivation

Make the Start menu's frequent column (and future taskbar pins) genuinely useful by (a) surfacing the
apps the user actually launches most, weighted toward ones **not currently open** (already-running apps
don't need a launch shortcut), and (b) making that column **warm on first run** by seeding from the OS's
own usage history instead of starting empty until Bevel has accumulated its own launch data.

## Current state (what already exists)

- `ProgramUsageStore` (src/Bevel.Taskbar/Model/ProgramUsageStore.cs) — Bevel's own per-app launch
  frequency/recency tracking, persisted.
- `ShellModel` (src/Bevel.Taskbar/Model/ShellModel.cs) — computes the `Frequent` list capped by
  `FrequentCap` (the `TaskbarStartMenuFrequentCount` setting), with a `NewlyAddedWindow` recency window.
- The Luna Start menu already renders a frequent/pinned left column.
- The helper already provides the live open-window list (so "currently open" is known to `ShellModel`).

So the frequency *tracking* and *rendering* exist. This bead adds two things on top: an exclude/deprioritize-open
filter, and optional OS usage seeding.

## Scope

### Part A — "frequent among not-currently-open" filter
- `ShellModel.RecomputeFrequent` should optionally exclude (or strongly deprioritize) apps that currently
  have an open window, so the frequent column suggests apps to *launch*, not ones already running.
- Behaviour toggle in settings (`TaskbarStartMenuFrequentExcludeOpen`, default on) — some users may prefer
  the raw frequency list.
- Edge: an app that's frequent AND open shouldn't leave a gap — backfill from the next-most-frequent
  not-open app so the column stays full to `FrequentCap`.

### Part B — OS usage seeding (warm start)
- A one-time (or periodic-reconcile) seed of `ProgramUsageStore` from the OS's usage history, so a fresh
  install shows sensible frequent apps immediately. Bevel's own tracking takes over from there (seed only
  fills gaps / initial weights; never overwrites a higher Bevel-observed count).
- New PAL seam: `IUsageProvider` in Bevel.Pal.Abstractions returning `(bundleId/appPath, lastUsed, count?)`
  records, implemented per platform; no-op default so it degrades gracefully where unavailable.

## Per-platform seed mechanism

- **macOS**: Spotlight metadata `kMDItemLastUsedDate` (reliable, **no special permission**) via
  `MDQuery`/`mdls` over `/Applications` + user app dirs. `kMDItemUseCount` also exists but is mostly-null
  on recent macOS — treat as best-effort only. **Rejected**: `knowledgeC.db` (real per-app usage duration,
  but needs Full Disk Access + undocumented, schema-fragile across OS versions) — not worth the fragility.
- **Windows**: `UserAssist` registry keys (HKCU\...\Explorer\UserAssist, ROT13-encoded) — launch counts +
  last-used. This is the source the XP/7 Start-menu MFU itself used.
- **Linux**: Zeitgeist activity log (`~/.local/share/zeitgeist`) or `~/.local/share/recently-used.xbel`;
  best-effort, less standardized.

## Non-goals

- No real-time OS usage streaming (macOS has no public Screen Time read API; DeviceActivity is sandboxed).
- No usage *duration* tracking — launch frequency + recency only.
- Not changing the pinned (explicitly user-pinned) list semantics; this is the *frequent/suggested* column.

## Privacy

- Seeding reads local OS usage history only; nothing leaves the machine. Gate it behind a setting
  (`TaskbarSeedUsageFromOS`, default on for macOS Spotlight since it needs no permission; consider default
  off where a permission/gated store would be involved). Document what's read in the Properties dialog blurb.
design: New IUsageProvider seam in Bevel.Pal.Abstractions (records: appId, lastUsed, count?); macOS impl uses MDQuery over kMDItemLastUsedDate (no FDA). ShellModel.RecomputeFrequent gains an exclude-open pass over the live open-window set with backfill. Seed merges into ProgramUsageStore as max(seed, observed). knowledgeC.db explicitly rejected (FDA + fragile).
acceptance_criteria: Part A: frequent column excludes/deprioritizes currently-open apps (toggle TaskbarStartMenuFrequentExcludeOpen, default on) and backfills to keep FrequentCap filled. Part B: fresh profile shows sensible frequent apps on first run seeded from OS usage (macOS Spotlight kMDItemLastUsedDate), via an IUsageProvider PAL seam with a no-op default; seed never lowers a Bevel-observed count. Both covered by tests.

title: Start-menu program launch has no automation-seam equivalent (agent-native parity)
description:
Launching a program is the primary Start-menu action, but there is no way for an automation client to enumerate installed apps or launch one: IShellAutomation/BevelVerb has no Launch verb and AutomationQuery has no Programs flag. The new curated Frequent list + Luna 'All Programs' flyout (this session) surface program launching in the UI with no agent-reachable equivalent. title: Consolidate duplicated ObjC interop into AppKitInterop
description:
Consolidate duplicated ObjC interop into AppKitInterop.

READY-TO-IMPLEMENT INVENTORY (scoped 2026-07-28) — refactor with ObjC memory-management risk; needs an UNLOCKED session to live-validate window-level/activation/icon interop:
CROSS-ASSEMBLY BLOCKER: AppKitInterop is 'internal' in Bevel.Pal.MacOS; TaskbarWindow.cs (Bevel.Taskbar) + DesktopWindow.cs (Bevel.Desktop) hand-roll their own. Verify project refs, then make AppKitInterop public or [InternalsVisibleTo].
Three duplicate sel/class caches: AppKitInterop._selectors, TaskbarWindow.SelectorCache (:509), DesktopWindow.Selector (:124).
SAFE INCREMENTAL ORDER (lowest risk first):
1. AppleEventSpecifier.cs:23 — delete local SendInt, call AppKitInterop.SendInt (same assembly, identical sig, zero memory semantics).
2. Collapse the two duplicate sel/class caches → AppKitInterop.Sel/GetClass.
3. DesktopWindow.NativeMac → move ResolveWindow + setLevel:/setCollectionBehavior: into AppKitInterop (dup of Taskbar's window subset).
4. TaskbarWindow.TaskbarNative window subset reuse (3's helpers). LEAVE the NSEvent global-monitor block (lines 417-503) local.
5. MacOSIconProvider autorelease pool → shared PushAutoreleasePool/DrainAutoreleasePool helper (test icon render off-thread).
6. LoginItemRegistrar ServiceManagement dlopen → generalized EnsureFrameworkLoaded (preserve load-BEFORE-first-GetClass ordering).
DO NOT MOVE (keep local, hard-won correctness): AppleEventInbound dynamic class-pair machinery + FourCC msgSend overloads (macos-inbound-apple-events; class_addMethod BOOL must be [MarshalAs(I1)]); NSEvent global-monitor block (pinned GCHandles); ShellActivation activation-policy timing. Preserve NSStringCreate +1-owned/release-once vs autoreleased-don't-release (bevel-fo2).
notes:
## CORRECTION to the 2026-09-23 note, and a plan (2026-09-28)

The earlier note said 'every duplicate pair has an identical signature and marshalling shape, so there is
no drift to trigger a bug.' That was wrong — it was based on sampling three symbols. Checking all 18:
SIX DISAGREE.

  CFArrayGetCount                          nint(IntPtr)  vs  long(IntPtr)
  CFArrayGetValueAtIndex                   (IntPtr,nint) vs  (IntPtr,long)
  CFGetTypeID                              nuint         vs  IntPtr
  CFArrayGetTypeID                         nuint         vs  IntPtr
  CFStringGetTypeID                        nuint         vs  IntPtr
  CFURLCreateFromFileSystemRepresentation  3rd param IntPtr/long/nint; 4th MarshalAs I1 vs U1

Still not a live bug, and this time verified rather than assumed: on arm64/x64 nint/long/IntPtr are all
8 bytes; nuint and IntPtr are both 8 bytes and the TypeIDs are only ever compared for equality, so
signedness never matters; I1 and U1 pass byte-identical 0/1 for false/true. It would diverge on a 32-bit
or non-64-bit target, where nint != long.

But it DOES change the refactor: this is no longer a pure mechanical move. Unifying by picking whichever
copy came to hand is a coin flip on each of those six rows. Canonical types from the CF headers:
  CFIndex  = signed long   -> nint
  CFTypeID = unsigned long -> nuint
  Boolean  = unsigned char -> [MarshalAs(UnmanagedType.U1)] bool
GeckoTabEngine already holds the correct integer choices; MacOSThumbnailProvider already holds U1.

Also found: AppKitInterop is 'internal static class' with 21 PUBLIC externs, so reuse was always
possible — the four silo files (GeckoTabEngine, MacOSAppBadgeSource, MacOSThumbnailProvider,
MacOSIconProvider) declare everything private. The duplication is authoring habit, not a visibility
barrier, which is why the plan's guard test matters more than the move itself.

And: CGImageSourceCreateWithURL / CGImageSourceCreateThumbnailAtIndex are ImageIO, NOT CoreGraphics,
despite the CG prefix. Grouping by symbol prefix would bind them to the wrong dylib and fail at runtime
on a path only a real Mac exercises.

Measured state: 80 distinct symbols, 101 declarations, 11 files; 18 duplicated (21 redundant).

PLAN: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-28-macos-interop-consolidation.md — 5 tasks. Amends this bead's
'into AppKitInterop' wording to a split by framework (CoreFoundationInterop / CoreGraphicsInterop /
ImageIOInterop / AccessibilityInterop / AppKitInterop) over a shared Frameworks constants class, because
one class binding five frameworks would be a 100+ declaration grab bag named after one of them.
[LibraryImport] is deliberately excluded and deferred to its own bead.
close_reason: Consolidated into per-framework interop classes (CoreFoundationInterop / CoreGraphicsInterop / ImageIOInterop / AccessibilityInterop / AppKitInterop) over a shared Frameworks constants class, enforced by InteropConventionTests. Amended this bead's 'into AppKitInterop' wording: split by framework instead, since one class binding five frameworks would be a 100+ declaration grab bag named after one of them. 101 declarations / 11 files / 18 duplicated -> 80 declarations / 7 files / 0 duplicated. Fixed the six divergent CF signatures to the header types (CFIndex->nint, CFTypeID->nuint, Boolean->U1) and, found en route, a REAL defect: AXIsProcessTrusted was a bare bool in MacOSPermissionBroker, marshalling as a 4-byte Win32 BOOL over a 1-byte native Boolean, so undefined register bytes decided an Accessibility check; same for the two CG screen-capture gates. Added AccessibilityGateTests (the broker had none) and a CF-ownership repeat test for the Gecko path.

title: Synchronous AE get/count can freeze the UI thread on huge enumeration
description: ce-code-review (adversarial MEDIUM / reliability REL-1): AppleEventBridge.Answer resolves get/count synchronously on the AE dispatch (UI) thread via blocking resolver.ResolveAsync().GetAwaiter().GetResult(). 'count every item of startup disk' enumerates the whole tree on the UI thread → indefinite freeze (DoS). Architectural: the AE reply must be synchronous, so it can't be fully offloaded without a suspend/resume (AESuspendTheCurrentEvent) async-reply design. Interim: bound the enumeration with a cap+timeout for the query path only (must not truncate the mutation-verb resolve). Track the async-reply redesign here.

title: setd mis-attributes every 'set' AE as set-selection

Fix: inspect the setd direct-object property specifier; only treat seld==sele as set-selection, else route to SetAsync or return errAEEventNotHandled. Note SetAsync is currently dead (FileManagerShellSurface.SetAsync throws for every property) and 'set' is unreachable from bevelctl/bevel:// — window-property set is unimplemented end-to-end.

title: Fix split-taskbar tray snapshot-vs-subscribe init race
description: ce-review adversarial/correctness: ShellCoreSystemTrayHost replays TraySnapshot as ItemAdded from its ctor; TrayViewModel subscribes in Start() (async void). A snapshot arriving in the gap is dropped (GetItemsAsync returns empty) → empty tray until an unrelated delta. Buffer the last snapshot and return it from GetItemsAsync, or defer replay until first subscriber. Also the all-in-one GetItemsAsync-vs-stream ordering can resurrect a removed item.

title: Bound the Taskbar<->Core<->Helper command path with timeouts/deadlines
description: ce-review reliability: no deadline anywhere in the gRPC/UDS command chain (activate/minimize/close/reposition/capture). Hover-capture now has a call-site timeout, but MinimizeAllAsync (Show Desktop) awaits sequentially with no per-window timeout — one hung window blocks the rest. Thread CallOptions deadlines + per-op CTS.
notes: Helper leg DONE in 55b121d: MacOSWindowManager interactive RPCs + tray ForwardClick now carry a 3s linked-CTS deadline. REMAINING: the Taskbar<->Core leg — ShellCoreClient.SendAsync -> UdsMessageClient.RequestAsync awaits the correlated TCS with no timer, so a live-but-stuck core still hangs the call. Add a deadline there too.
close_reason: Both legs bounded: helper RPCs + tray ForwardClick (55b121d, 3s) and the Taskbar->Core SendAsync path (5s). A wedged helper or core can no longer hang a click.
