title: P7: NativeAOT publish (the per-process memory payoff)
description: The real RSS win. Blockers (recon): (1) migrate ~25 AXAML views to compiled bindings (x:DataType/x:CompileBindings or AvaloniaUseCompiledBindingsByDefault per UI project) — biggest effort + silent-binding-failure risk; (2) one JsonSerializerContext for BevelSettings/ThemeOverrides + 2 anonymous-type sites (SettingsService.cs:99, MacOSDockController.cs:167); (3) validate gRPC/Google.Protobuf under trim/AOT + smoke-test helper handshake. Then PublishAot+InvariantGlobalization per-RID (arm64+x64), rework packaging to single Mach-O, drop JIT entitlements, revalidate Velopack + inside-out codesign. Interop is plain DllImport (AOT-fine); DI generic/explicit (AOT-fine).
notes: PROGRESS 2026-07-13: Foundation DONE + verified — compiled bindings by default (only TaskbarView was bound; AVLN3001 fixed), JSON source-gen (SettingsJsonContext + CoreJsonContext via JsonTypeInfo), DockController anon-type removed, Assembly.Location IL3000 handled, -p:BevelPublishAot opt-in plumbed. AOT analysis 43->3 warnings. VERIFIED: dotnet publish -r osx-arm64 -p:BevelPublishAot=true produces a 28MB native Mach-O that boots --role=core --pal=fake headless and shuts down cleanly. REMAINING: (1) 3 reflection bindings -> new bead; (2) macOS AOT native link needs Homebrew openssl@3 + brotli on LIBRARY_PATH (gRPC HTTP-stack deps) -> bundle/static-link for a portable build; (3) single-Mach-O packaging + drop JIT entitlements + revalidate Velopack + inside-out codesign + notarization (needs signing infra, not validatable here). Committed 0ff207c.

title: P5: SQLite shared persistent store (settings first)
description: Move SettingsService onto a shared SQLite DB (WAL, concurrent readers, one writer) so all role processes read one source + get a change signal (replaces the single Program.cs LoadAsync + per-process JSON copies that would drift). Extensible to a thumbnail/MRU cache later. Alternatively settings could ride the shell-core broadcast — decide DB-vs-broadcast per data kind (persistent/queryable -> SQLite; live -> broadcast).
close_reason: SettingsService moved onto shared SQLite (WAL, one-writer/many-reader, busy_timeout 3s, version counter + Changed event + ReloadIfChangedAsync). Public API preserved; legacy settings.json imported once then kept as passive export. All role processes read one DB. 76 Bevel.Core tests green.

title: P4: process supervision for role + shell-core processes
description: A supervisor (shell-core, or a thin launcher role) spawns + crash-restarts the role processes, extending the HelperLifecycle/HelperProcessHost monitor-loop pattern (already supports multiple children). Define startup order (shell-core+helper before UI), restart authority, and the supervision matrix avoiding the deadlock the arch spec flags. Cross-process quit/restart fan-out (replaces App.RequestExit/RequestRestart statics).
close_reason: Process supervision + update/restart orchestration. RoleProcessSupervisor (monitor-loop policy mirroring HelperLifecycle, injectable IRoleProcess + poll delay): ordered startup (shell-core owner before UI clients), per-child crash-restart with tick-based backoff, RestartAllAsync (kill+respawn all → each re-execs the CURRENT binary = latest build), RestartCoreAsync (swap core, UIs stay up = update-on-demand), StopAsync. Launcher control channel over the shell-core UDS transport (LauncherControl: taskbar->launcher Quit/RestartAll/RestartCore, since .NET can't receive SIGUSR1/2); App.RequestExit/RequestRestart now fan out to the launcher when supervised, else in-process. --role=launcher entry (RunLauncher) spawns core+taskbar, hands children the shared shell-core + control endpoints via env, parks on SIGTERM. Deadlock-avoidance: all locks launcher-local, kills one-directional. 6 RoleProcessSupervisorTests (ordered start, crash-respawn, RestartAll, RestartCore-only, Stop-halts-loop, keeps-retrying-failing-child). LIVE smoke (--pal=fake) proved: launcher spawns core+taskbar in order; killing core → supervisor respawns fresh PID; SIGTERM launcher reaps all children cleanly. Fixed a real SIGTERM bug found live — handlers now set ctx.Cancel=true so teardown runs before .NET terminates (also applied to RunShellCore, preventing an orphaned helper). Full suite: 382 tests, 0 failures.

title: P3: shell-core owner process (C# gRPC-over-UDS server + broadcast)
description: New headless C# process = single owner of live shell state. Owns MacOSAppEnvironment (one watcher set/enumeration) + ShellModel-style window/focus/app projections + the single Changes subscription to the Swift helper; re-broadcasts snapshot-then-delta to the UI role processes. Net-new: C# gRPC SERVER (Grpc.AspNetCore + Kestrel ListenUnixSocket; regen stubs GrpcServices=Both or new proto/bevel.core.v1.proto), port Swift AuthInterceptor to a C# server interceptor (client HMAC already in HelperClient). Reuse: HelperClient UDS dial, nonce-via-env handshake, snapshot-delta contract, WindowServiceImpl broadcaster design, HelperLifecycle/HelperProcessHost supervisor template. UI processes consume IWindowManager/IAppEnvironment as shell-core clients instead of instantiating PAL impls.
notes: TRANSPORT DECISION: use a lightweight length-prefixed protobuf-framed protocol over raw UnixDomainSocket (System.Net.Sockets), NOT Grpc.AspNetCore+Kestrel — pulling ASP.NET Core into a shell process that exists to SAVE memory is counterproductive. Reuse the helper's nonce-via-env + capability-HMAC handshake and snapshot-then-delta broadcaster pattern. New headless --role=core must NOT start Avalonia (Program.Main needs a core branch). In split mode taskbar's IWindowManager/IAppEnvironment become shell-core CLIENTS; --role=all keeps direct MacOS impls (no core). DI wiring becomes role-dependent for these two services.
close_reason: Shell-core owner complete: headless --role=core branch in Program.cs (RunShellCore parks on SIGTERM, no Avalonia) + ShellCoreServer/Client + ShellCoreWindowManager/AppEnvironment adapters + UDS transport (Bevel.ShellCore.Ipc). 3 end-to-end integration tests (ShellCoreIntegrationTests) prove snapshot-on-connect, PAL delta fan-out, and command round-trip over a live socket with a controllable stub PAL. Full solution builds; 68 taskbar + 20 UI tests green.

title: P2: --role split with role-scoped DI
description: Add a RoleSelector (mirror PalSelection's --pal= parse) + App.Role static; gate the three window-creation blocks in App.axaml.cs by role; each role sets desktop.MainWindow to its own window. Role-scope DI in CompositionRoot so each process registers ONLY the services it uses (taskbar: helper/IWindowManager/ShellModel/IAppEnvironment; explorer: VfsRoot/FileOps/IIconProvider; desktop: ~none) — this alone kills MacOSAppEnvironment triplication. Move StartPollAsync + WorkAreaMitigator into the taskbar branch. Ctrl+N new-window and global restart/quit now cross process (was in-proc static events). Restart already replays args so --role survives.
close_reason: RoleSelector (--role=taskbar|explorer|desktop, default All) + App.Role static; Program.Main parses & stashes it; App.OnFrameworkInitializationCompleted split into role-gated CreateDesktopSurface/CreateTaskbarSurface/CreateExplorerSurface (All runs all three, unchanged single-process behavior; a split launch runs exactly one, sets its own MainWindow). Role-scoping falls out of MS.DI lazy singletons — non-taskbar roles never resolve IWindowManager/IAppEnvironment so no helper/AX watchers spin up; the one eagerly-started piece (HelperLifecycle hosted service) is role-gated in AddMacOSPal to taskbar/all. 57 taskbar tests green (+14: role parse incl aliases/case/unknown-default/mixed-argv, and helper-hosted-only-for-taskbar/all). Live multi-process launch to be proven at the P4 integration milestone.

title: P1: ReadyToRun publish for Bevel.App
description: Add PublishReadyToRun (RID-guarded) to Bevel.App.csproj so publishes crossgen IL->native (faster cold start, more OS-shareable read-only code pages across role processes). Interim step before AOT; AOT supersedes it. Verify with a per-RID self-contained publish.
close_reason: Added RID-guarded PublishReadyToRun to Bevel.App.csproj. Verified: dotnet publish -r osx-arm64 --self-contained -c Release exits 0 with crossgen2-applied output (libcoreclr.dylib + native apphost present). Only warning is pre-existing AVLN3001 on OnboardingWindow.axaml (never-shown window, no public ctor) — benign under R2R/JIT but must be resolved for P7 compiled-bindings/AOT.

title: Multi-process shell: --role split + shell-core owner + shared caches + AOT
description: Split Bevel.App into per-role processes (taskbar / explorer / desktop) from one exe via --role, backed by a C# shell-core owner process that holds the single source of truth for live shell state and broadcasts deltas; add SQLite for persistent shared state and an MMF-backed shared BGRA icon pool; move from JIT to ReadyToRun then NativeAOT for per-process footprint. Decisions (2026-07-13): R2R now/AOT next; build shell-core+broadcast now; build MMF pool now. Recon: caches are trivial memory-wise (icons ~0.5MB/proc); real levers are role-scoped DI + AOT; shell-core/MMF are consistency/single-source + future-large-icon plays. Grounding: only taskbar consumes the Swift helper; SettingsService is the only all-role shared singleton; C# has gRPC CLIENT stubs only (server is net-new); Avalonia 11.3.18 AOT-capable but needs ~25 AXAML views on compiled bindings.

title: Remove StartMenu's dead VM-less Programs fallback path
description: StartMenu.axaml.cs carries two parallel Programs-cascade implementations: the production bound path (WireBoundPrograms/OnProgramContainerPrepared, bound to StartMenuViewModel.Programs) and the older in-code path (LoadProgramsAsync/SetIconAsync/Launch/_programsLoaded + the '_programsVm is null' branches). The in-code path is dead in production (App.axaml.cs always supplies a StartMenuViewModel) and survives only because StartMenuTests.cs / RenderStartMenuTest construct 'new StartMenu()' with no VM. Flagged by the code review (maintainability P2).
design: Give the tests a StartMenuViewModel-backed StartMenu (new StartMenuViewModel(new ShellModel(null,null,null)) → empty Programs), then delete LoadProgramsAsync/SetIconAsync/Launch/_programsLoaded and the null-VM branches in OpenAsync/BuildStaticSubmenus. Also add a headless-Skia render test for the bound Programs path (per avalonia-popup-needs-visual-tree: a VM-only assertion would pass even if WireBoundPrograms/ContainerPrepared wiring silently broke).
acceptance_criteria: Single Programs implementation; StartMenuTests pass with VM-backed construction; bound-Programs cascade covered by a real-pixel render test.
close_reason: Removed the dead VM-less Programs data-loading path (LoadProgramsAsync/SetIconAsync/Launch/_programsLoaded); null-VM construction now degrades to a '(No programs)' placeholder. Added Bound_programs_cascade_realizes_containers_from_the_view_model render test that drives real ContainerPrepared realization of the bound StartMenuViewModel.Programs and asserts headers + captures pixels. Extracted shared StubAppEnvironment. 37/37 taskbar tests green.

title: Fold Windows taskbar path onto shared ObservableReconciler
description: The taskbar Windows collection (ShellModel._byId upsert/prune with exit-animation grace period) is a bespoke hand-rolled version of the same keyed in-place diff now generalized in ObservableReconciler (used by Programs). Fold Windows onto the shared primitive to remove duplication.
design: Reconciler must grow an optional 'defer-remove' hook so the XP-style exit animation (mark IsClosing, animate Width/Opacity to 0, remove after 160ms) is preserved. Windows key = ForeignWindow.Id.Value (already stable). Risk: animation timing is only observable in the live UI, so verify with the app running, not just headless render tests. Keep the Revive() grace-period semantics (a reappearing native id cancels a pending exit).
acceptance_criteria: Windows path uses ObservableReconciler; grow-in/shrink-out animations still play live; ShellModelTests (revive-in-place, prune, focus) still green.
close_reason: Folded the taskbar Windows path onto the shared ObservableReconciler; deleted the bespoke _byId upsert/prune bookkeeping. Grew the reconciler with an optional onRemove(TItem, Action) deferred-remove hook (default = immediate remove, unchanged for Programs; taskbar defers to play the XP exit animation + identity-keyed commit continuation). ShellModel.Reconcile builds a stable-slot-ordered desired list (survivors ranked by current slot so CG z-order reshuffles don't reorder buttons; new windows appended) and delegates via keyOf/sourceKeyOf=Id.Value, update=Revive+Update, onRemove=BeginExit. Preserved: stable button order, EarnsButton title/app-id gate incl. transient-empty-title survivor retention, CloseGeneration epoch guard, ApplyExclusiveFocus/sticky _focusedWindowId, 2s backstop. Common close path (OnWindowClosed event) still removes IN PLACE via BeginExit — no reconciler reorder — so interactive exit animation is pixel-identical. 41/41 taskbar tests green (2 new deferred-remove reconciler tests), independently re-run; no _byId references remain. Rare backstop-catch cosmetic edge tracked as bevel-e26. Grow/shrink smoothness warrants a routine live eyeball.

description: For hasAX apps whose miniaturized window reports a non-standard subrole (e.g. Jump Desktop -> AXDialog), the helper's subrole filter dropped it -> taskbar button vanished on minimize. title: Taskbar-button click raises the window but doesn't activate its app
description: helper activateWindow only did AXRaise (reorders within the app). Exposed once the taskbar became a real always-on-top window (level 23) holding key focus on click: the target window came forward but its app never became active, so it 'didn't always come up'. Fix: after AXRaise, set kAXFrontmostAttribute=true on the owning app element (AX-native, not the deprecated NSRunningApplication.activate(options:)). Verified live.

title: Taskbar not always-on-top: window level never applied (NSView vs NSWindow handle)
description: TaskbarWindow.TryGetNativeHandle cast the Avalonia platform handle to INativePlatformHandleSurface, which the macOS window handle doesn't implement -> returned Zero -> ApplyTaskbarBehaviors bailed, so setLevel:/setCollectionBehavior: never ran. CGWindowList showed 'Bevel Taskbar' at layer 0 (same as ordinary windows), so windows and their drop shadows rendered over it. Fix: TaskbarNative.ResolveWindow resolves the content NSView to its NSWindow via [nsView window] (respondsToSelector-guarded). Verified: layer 0 -> 23.
close_reason: Fixed: NSView->NSWindow resolution in TaskbarNative.ResolveWindow; taskbar now at window level 23 (verified via CGWindowList).

title: Implement MacOSIconProvider (in-process app/file icon render) + Start-menu Programs icons
description: MacOSIconProvider.GetIconAsync is a NotImplementedException stub, so installed-app icons (InstalledApp.IconPath = .app path) can't be shown in-process. Implement it: NSWorkspace iconForFile: -> render to BGRA at requested size (CoreGraphics CGBitmapContext) -> PalImage. Add a PalImage->Avalonia bitmap helper (first consumer of the IIconProvider pixel path). Wire IIconProvider into TaskbarView->StartMenu and set MenuItem.Icon on Programs entries (theme reserves the 19px icon column). Also unblocks desktop/file-manager icons later. The taskbar's live WINDOW icons already work via the Swift helper; this is the installed-app equivalent in-process.

Wired into Start > Programs via IIconProvider; verified live by user. Tests: MacOSIconProviderTests (Calculator/Finder/Safari non-blank BGRA, missing-path safe, cache identity) green.

title: Start menu is not Win2000-faithful — rebuild against the reference corpus
description: Current StartMenu.axaml is a hand-rolled set of Borders that misses most Win2000 fidelity (per docs/reference/win2000/taskbar-start-menu.md): (1) NO per-item icon column — real Win2000 shows a large icon left of every item (Programs/Documents/Settings/Search/Help/Run/Log Off/Shut Down); blocked on the icon set (bevel-assets). title: M1: per-capability RPC auth scoping for helper services (ScriptingService/InputService)
description: M0's helper exposes only SupervisionService (Ping), gated by the per-session nonce — one token grants everything. M1 adds ScriptingService (Apple Events) and InputService (synthetic input), which are strictly more dangerous; a single all-or-nothing token means any code that can read the token (or any future in-proc plugin) gets input synthesis for free. Implement the capability-scoped design from bevel-vgg (see design field) before those services ship.
design:
Design (bevel-vgg item 3, 2026-07-10):
1. TOKEN FORMAT: keep one 16-byte session nonce as the MAC key, but per-RPC auth becomes 'x-bevel-token: <capability>:<HMAC-SHA256(nonce, capability)>' where capability ∈ {supervision, scripting, input}. The helper derives the expected MAC per capability at startup from --token; constant-time compare as today (SupervisionServiceImpl pattern).
2. SCOPING: HelperClient.Connect gains a capability set; Bevel.Ipc exposes typed sub-clients (SupervisionClient, ScriptingClient, InputClient) each attaching only its own capability header. App composition decides which sub-clients a component receives — e.g. the AE dispatcher gets scripting but never input.
3. HELPER SIDE: each Swift service impl validates ONLY its own capability's MAC, so a leaked scripting MAC cannot call InputService. Unknown/missing capability → RPCError(.unauthenticated), same as today.
4. NO NEW SECRETS: everything derives from the existing nonce; no extra key exchange, rotation still per-session via helper relaunch.
5. TESTS: contract tests assert cross-capability rejection (scripting MAC on input RPC fails), and Bevel.Ipc unit tests assert each sub-client sends exactly its own header. Extend Bevel.Pal.ContractTests.
Deliberately NOT chosen: separate nonces per capability via env (env size/leak surface grows), and TLS/mTLS on the UDS (overkill under 0700 dir + same-user threat model).

title: ComputerProvider: volume names with '/' break VfsPath round-trip on macOS (resolve/navigate fails)
description: GetVolumeDisplayName embeds the native mount path in parentheses, Windows-style ('Local Disk (C:)'). On macOS mount paths contain '/' — e.g. 'Macintosh HD (/)' or '/System/Volumes/Data/home (/System/Volumes/Data/home)' — and for the root drive Name.TrimEnd('/') even yields an empty string. Since VfsPath segments split on '/', node.Path.FileName is mangled, so ResolveAsync(node.Path) throws DirectoryNotFoundException ('Volume not found: ()') and ResolveEffectivePath never matches — clicking a volume under My Computer cannot resolve it by path. Repro: enumerate computer:// root, then ResolveAsync(first.Path). Fix at the right altitude: make the path segment volume-identity-safe (e.g. use a slash-free stable key such as the mount path with an escaped separator, or label-only with disambiguation) and keep the Win2000 'Label (mount)' presentation in DisplayName only; add the enumerate→resolve round-trip test that bevel-972 scoped out.
close_reason: Path segment is now the escaped mount path (identity), display name is presentation-only; ResolveAsync/ResolveEffectivePath match by exact mount; list activation of volumes navigates via shared ToNavigablePath seam. Core 66/66, FM 144/144. Follow-up bevel-1cc for real macOS labels via PAL.

title: Real macOS trash + trash-restore undo
description: Follow-up from the /code-review fix to ExecuteDeleteAsync. Today LocalFsMutator.DeleteAsync permanently deletes even when toTrash=true (macOS trash is meant to live in the helper), and IVfsMutator.DeleteAsync returns no trash path, so trashing is (a) not actually reversible and (b) silently permanent data loss for a user who expects Recycle-Bin semantics. The dead TrashUndoEntry scaffolding in ExecuteDeleteAsync was removed. Real fix: implement move-to-trash via the helper (NSFileManager trashItem), have DeleteAsync return the trash location, populate trashPairs, and push a TrashUndoEntry so UndoTrashAsync can restore.
acceptance_criteria: Delete-to-Trash moves items to the macOS Trash and Undo restores them to their original location.
close_reason: Real trash + trash-undo implemented + tested. IVfsMutator.DeleteAsync now returns the trash location (VfsPath?); LocalFsMutator moves to an injectable trash dir (default ~/.Trash) with collision-free naming, returns null for permanent delete. FileOperationService.ExecuteDeleteAsync records (original,trash) pairs and pushes a TrashUndoEntry; UndoTrashAsync restores. 3 new tests: trash+undo round-trip, permanent-delete-not-undoable, same-name collisions both survive. Helper-based NSFileManager.trashItem (records Finder 'Put Back' metadata) is a future refinement over the ~/.Trash move.

title: BevelHelper answers RPCs without peer-credential/nonce check (IPC-04)
description: The deleted main.swift documented that the helper 'verifies the peer credential + nonce (IPC-04)' before answering RPCs. The replacement (native/helper-macos/Sources/BevelHelper/*.swift) parses/requires --token but never passes it to the service, and Ping is answered unconditionally with no SO_PEERCRED/getpeereid peer-uid check. The UDS lives in a world-accessible temp dir (Path.GetTempPath()/bevel-helper, HelperLifecycle.cs:44), so any local process can call the helper. Fix: enforce the --token/nonce and check the peer uid before serving RPCs, restrict socket dir perms.
acceptance_criteria: Helper rejects RPCs from clients without the correct nonce and from other uids.
close_reason: Nonce auth implemented + tested both sides. Swift: SupervisionServiceImpl requires the x-bevel-token metadata header on every RPC, constant-time compared to the --token nonce; unauthenticated RPCError otherwise (5 XCTest cases). C#: HelperClient sends the nonce as gRPC metadata (BuildAuthMetadata), HelperLifecycle passes NonceToken through Connect(). Socket dir hardened to 0700 (HardenSocketDirectory, tested). Peer-UID transport check deferred to bevel-kyf (blocked on grpc-swift-2 handler API; redundant with 0700 dir + nonce for the cross-user threat).

title: FileOperationService._cts shared field: dispose/cross-cancel race
description: FileOperationService.cs:63-64 assigns the per-call 'using' linked CTS to the shared field _cts; Cancel() (:81) and in-job _cts?.Cancel() (:223,:376) read it with no synchronization. After ExecuteAsync returns the linked CTS is disposed but _cts still points to it -> a later UI Cancel() throws ObjectDisposedException. Two overlapping ExecuteAsync calls clobber _cts so operation A's internal cancel actually cancels operation B. Fix: pass the CTS through the call graph instead of a shared field, or track per-operation state and null/guard _cts on completion.
acceptance_criteria: Cancel after completion is a no-op; overlapping operations cancel independently.
close_reason: Fixed + tested. FileOperationService: locked shared result/undo collections (w15), safe _cts lifecycle with gate+clear-before-dispose and CTS passed down to avoid cross-cancel (tbo), read-only dest fails fast (c7l), single destination resolve via TryResolveAsync (5ty, plus LocalFsProvider type-desc dedup/dead-code/delete-branch collapse). New FileOperationServiceTests + FileOperationServiceProviderTests (11 tests). Core 57/57, FileManager 20/20.

title: LocalDirectoryWatcher.Notify races Dispose -> ObjectDisposedException on threadpool
description: LocalFsProvider.cs:326-342: FileSystemWatcher Created/Deleted/Changed/Renamed handlers call Notify() on threadpool threads, which does _subject.OnNext with no coordination against Dispose() (sets EnableRaisingEvents=false then disposes the Subject). A queued FSW event delivered after disposal calls OnNext on a disposed Subject -> ObjectDisposedException on a background thread (no catch) during rapid folder navigation (FileManagerWindow.LoadDirectory disposes the old watcher on each navigate). Fix: guard OnNext against disposal (dispose flag + lock, or check _subject.IsDisposed) and swallow post-dispose notifications.
acceptance_criteria: Rapid navigation between folders never throws from the watcher on a background thread.
close_reason: Fixed with unit tests: VfsPath canonical parse/combine (VfsPathTests), enumerate TOCTOU guard + watcher dispose race + type-desc dedup (LocalFsProviderResilienceTests). Core 57/57 green.

title: HelperClient gRPC 'unix://' channel has no ConnectCallback -> never connects
description: src/Bevel.Ipc/HelperClient.cs:25-31 builds GrpcChannel.ForAddress('unix://<path>') with only Insecure credentials and no SocketsHttpHandler.ConnectCallback opening a UnixDomainSocketEndPoint. Grpc.Net.Client cannot dial a UDS without that callback, so PingAsync never connects and HelperLifecycle.WaitForReadyAsync (:109) times out after 5s. Currently masked because the host is never started (see bevel-c0y), but this blocks the helper the moment that is fixed. Fix: set GrpcChannelOptions.HttpHandler = new SocketsHttpHandler { ConnectCallback = ... UnixDomainSocketEndPoint(socketPath) } and use http://localhost as the address.
acceptance_criteria: HelperClient.PingAsync connects to the helper over the Unix domain socket.
close_reason: Fixed + tested. HelperLifecycle: single self-healing monitor loop started once in StartAsync (never spawns duplicates on restart), non-blocking graceful start (missing/broken helper no longer aborts boot — enables host start), backoff on repeated failures (mox). title: SearchPaneViewModel.StopSearch disposes CTS still in use by the walk
description: SearchPaneViewModel.cs:104-110: WalkAsync is fire-and-forget (:100) and keeps enumerating with _searchCts.Token, but StopSearch calls Cancel() then Dispose() then null. Disposing a CTS whose token is still registered inside 'await foreach' throws ObjectDisposedException (not OperationCanceledException), escaping the catch(OperationCanceledException) filters and becoming an unobserved task exception. Triggered on every Stop / new-search-while-running. Fix: don't Dispose the CTS until the walk task has completed (await it, or dispose in a continuation), or swap-then-dispose the old CTS after the task ends.
acceptance_criteria: Cancelling or restarting a search never throws ObjectDisposedException.
close_reason: Fixed + tested. SearchPaneViewModel: walk owns CTS lifetime (disposed only after the walk, never mid-use) + guarded Stop/Dispose (u0z); content search reads via provider OpenReadAsync for all schemes (5ya). ItemView.SortAsync: shared ApplyOrder detaches ItemsSource and never drops streamed late arrivals (rn9). New SearchPaneViewModelTests (4) + ItemViewSortTests (4). FileManager 28/28.

title: LocalFsProvider enumerate: uncaught GetAttributes TOCTOU aborts whole listing
description: LocalFsProvider.cs:45 calls File.GetAttributes(entry) inside the EnumerateFileSystemEntries loop with no try/catch. If another process deletes/moves the entry between enumeration and GetAttributes, it throws FileNotFoundException/IOException and the whole IAsyncEnumerable terminates -> pane shows partial/zero items instead of skipping the vanished entry. Reproducible in busy folders (Downloads, build/temp). Fix: wrap the per-entry stat in try/catch and 'continue' on transient IO/not-found.
acceptance_criteria: Enumerating a folder while entries vanish yields the surviving entries without aborting.
close_reason: Fixed with unit tests: VfsPath canonical parse/combine (VfsPathTests), enumerate TOCTOU guard + watcher dispose race + type-desc dedup (LocalFsProviderResilienceTests). Core 57/57 green.

title: HelperLifecycle restart spawns duplicate monitor loops
description: HelperLifecycle.cs: on exit detection MonitorLoopAsync (:167) calls LaunchAndConnectAsync, which unconditionally assigns a NEW _monitorCts and a NEW _monitorTask=MonitorLoopAsync(...) (:101-102). The current loop keeps running under its old, now-unreferenced token (never cancelled). After N crashes there are N+1 concurrent monitor loops; the next crash makes all of them KillHelper()+relaunch simultaneously -> duplicate helper processes, orphaned CTSs, NRE races on _helperProcess. StopAsync only cancels the latest CTS. Fix: restart in-place within the existing loop (don't recurse into LaunchAndConnectAsync's monitor-spawn), or cancel/await the prior loop before starting a new one.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated helper crashes leave exactly one monitor loop and one helper process.
close_reason: Fixed + tested. HelperLifecycle: single self-healing monitor loop started once in StartAsync (never spawns duplicates on restart), non-blocking graceful start (missing/broken helper no longer aborts boot — enables host start), backoff on repeated failures (mox). HelperClient: SocketsHttpHandler.ConnectCallback dials the Unix domain socket via UnixDomainSocketEndPoint (cwv). New Bevel.Pal.MacOS.Tests: HelperLifecycleTests (3) + HelperClientTests (4), 7/7 green.

title: ItemView.SortAsync drops items streamed during sort + virtualization crash
description: ItemView.axaml.cs:242-266: for lists >=500, SortAsync snapshots _viewModels, awaits an off-thread sort, then _viewModels.Clear() + re-adds ONLY the stale snapshot. Rows appended by streaming AddItems during the await are silently lost (large dirs are exactly the ones still streaming). Also, unlike SortItems (:280 nulls ItemsPresenter.ItemsSource first 'to avoid virtualization teardown crash'), SortAsync mutates the still-bound collection, risking that crash. Fix: detach ItemsSource before mutating; re-apply the sort to the live collection (or merge post-sort additions) instead of replacing with a stale snapshot.
acceptance_criteria: Sorting a large directory mid-stream keeps all items and does not crash.
close_reason: Fixed + tested. SearchPaneViewModel: walk owns CTS lifetime (disposed only after the walk, never mid-use) + guarded Stop/Dispose (u0z); content search reads via provider OpenReadAsync for all schemes (5ya). ItemView.SortAsync: shared ApplyOrder detaches ItemsSource and never drops streamed late arrivals (rn9). New SearchPaneViewModelTests (4) + ItemViewSortTests (4). FileManager 28/28.
