title: M3 — Systray mirroring (Ice technique)
ToolTip was unthemeable and inherited hover foreground from its owner's style scope
description:
Filed retroactively: fixed in eaa91c1, no bead existed first (process miss).

Two defects, one shipped fix.

1. STYLE LEAK. A ToolTip is a LOGICAL DESCENDANT of the control it is attached to, so a descendant selector in the owner's style scope reaches it. StackFlyoutView had 'Border.stackcell:pointerover TextBlock { Foreground: White }' (and the :focus-visible twin) for its selection state — and because a tooltip is shown precisely WHILE its owner is hovered or focused, those rules fired on the tooltip's own text every single time: white on the pale-yellow info surface, i.e. invisible. Reported by the user on the Downloads stack.

2. NOT THEMEABLE. The vendored Classic.Avalonia theme maps ToolTip onto SystemColors.Info*, which is the right Win2000 look but sits OUTSIDE the Bevel token set, so no skin, colourway or Theme Studio could change it.

FIX. Both themes now carry an implicit {x:Type ToolTip} ControlTheme over Bevel.Brush.InfoWindow / InfoText / WindowFrame — implicit on purpose, because tooltips are attached with ToolTip.Tip all over the shell and are never given a Theme=, so only the implicit key reaches them. Luna gained the two tokens, deliberately NON-chromatic (#FFFFE1 / #000000): the info surface is a system affordance, not chrome, so it must not re-hue with the colourway. Guard styles ('ToolTip TextBlock' re-asserting Bevel.Brush.InfoText) added LAST in document order in both affected scopes, since Avalonia breaks equal-specificity ties by declaration order.
acceptance_criteria: ToolTip background/foreground/border resolve from Bevel tokens in both themes and change with a theme switch; hovering a stack cell or task button leaves tooltip text legible; Luna's info surface stays pale yellow across all colourways.
notes:
GENERALIZABLE HAZARD, worth a lint: any ':pointerover <Element>' or ':focus-visible <Element>' descendant selector in a scope that also attaches ToolTip.Tip will repaint the tooltip. It is not an edge case — the tooltip is visible exactly when the selector matches, so the collision is guaranteed rather than occasional. Two scopes were affected (StackFlyoutView, TaskbarView); a repo-wide grep for ':pointerover' + descendant TextBlock/Path selectors would find any others, and the implicit ControlTheme now limits the damage to Foreground-on-descendant rules specifically.

Also fixed in the same commit (separate symptom, no separate bead): the Start button's caption clipped its trailing glyph even at correct padding, because Avalonia clipped at content bounds and Luna's italic caption ink leans past them. ClipToBounds=False on the button.
close_reason: Shipped in eaa91c1 on fix/windows-taskbar-icons (PR #2). Filed retroactively for the record; build clean, 1267 tests pass.

title: Per-item tray visibility (always show / hide in overflow / suppress)
description:
Windows lets the user decide PER TRAY ITEM whether it is always visible, hidden in the overflow, or suppressed — Win11's "Other system tray icons" list, XP's "Customize notifications". Bevel has a global overflow cap (TaskbarTrayOverflowCap) which decides by COUNT, not by the user's preference, so which icons hide is effectively arbitrary.

As a component concern (parent bevel-aqr7) this is the tray component's own settings: a persisted per-item visibility map keyed by the stable tray item identity, plus a settings surface listing known items (including ones not currently present, so a user can pre-decide for an app that is not running).

Note the identity question is real: the tray mirror keys items by the source's own handle, which is NOT stable across restarts of the owning app. A per-item preference needs a durable key — owner executable plus the item's tooltip/guid — decided when this is built, or preferences will silently stop applying.
acceptance_criteria: Each tray item's visibility is user-configurable and persists across restarts of both Bevel and the owning app, using a durable identity rather than a per-session handle.

title: Pinned apps on the taskbar (launch-or-activate, reorder, Win+number)
description:
Win11 pins apps to the taskbar: launch when not running, activate when running, drag to reorder, pin/unpin from the context menu, and Win+1..9 to activate by position. Bevel has none of this — its strip shows only OPEN windows, so there is nothing to click when the app is closed.

As a component (parent bevel-aqr7): a pinned-apps component holding an ordered list of app ids, merged with the live window strip so a pinned app that IS running shows as one button rather than two. That merge is the subtle part and the reason this is not just "a launcher": Explorer and the Dock both collapse pinned+running into a single button, and getting it wrong produces the duplicate-button bug every lesser taskbar has.

Needs: persistence of the pin list (per component instance), drag-to-reorder within the strip, pin/unpin verbs on the existing task-button context menu, and Win+number activation. App identity is already resolved per platform (BundleId on both; AUMID for packaged Windows apps), so the pin list keys off that.

macOS parity note: this is the Dock's persistent-app behaviour, so the component is useful on both platforms rather than being a Windows import.
acceptance_criteria: Apps can be pinned and persist across restarts; a pinned app that is running shows as ONE button, not two; pins reorder by drag; Win+1..9 activates by position.

title: Jump lists on task buttons (recent/frequent documents + app tasks)
description:
Right-clicking a Windows taskbar button gives a jump list: recent and frequent documents, app-declared tasks, and pin-to-list. Bevel's task-button context menu currently offers only window verbs (minimize/restore/quit).

Platform surface: jump lists come from ICustomDestinationList / IApplicationDocumentLists (recent and frequent are maintained by the shell per AppUserModelID; app-declared tasks live in the app's own custom destination list). Reading them is a documented COM surface, so this does NOT need the undocumented territory the tray mirror ran into.

As a component concern (parent bevel-aqr7) this belongs to the window-strip component's context menu rather than being its own bar element.

macOS counterpart: the Dock menu's recent documents. The abstraction is "what extra verbs does this app offer", which both platforms can answer — a PAL seam like the existing ITabProvider, rather than a Windows-only bolt-on.
acceptance_criteria: Right-clicking a task button offers the app's recent/frequent documents and declared tasks, opening them in that app; absent gracefully where the platform provides none.

title: Windows shell mode: render legacy balloon tips (NIM_INFO) — mandatory with the tray claim
description:
MANDATORY as soon as Bevel owns Shell_TrayWnd (parent bevel-7p9r). An app calling Shell_NotifyIcon with NIF_INFO expects the shell to draw a balloon; with Explorer gone and nobody drawing it, the notification is simply lost — a regression against Explorer AND against classic shell replacements, which all rendered these.

Protocol: NIM_INFO arrives on the SAME WM_COPYDATA/SHELLTRAYDATA channel the bevel-2t7u spike already receives, so there is no new transport to build — the handler just has to notice NIF_INFO in uFlags and read szInfo / szInfoTitle / dwInfoFlags (icon: none/info/warning/error, or a custom hIcon on newer struct versions) and uTimeout. Same NOTIFYICONDATA-versioning caution as the icon path: read by cbSize, never guess the layout.

Behaviour to match: balloon anchors to the owning tray icon, auto-dismisses (Windows clamps the app-requested timeout), click raises the owner (send its callback message with NIN_BALLOONUSERCLICK), close button sends NIN_BALLOONTIMEOUT. An app that never gets its callback cannot tell the user ignored it, so the callbacks are part of correctness, not polish.

Design: Bevel draws it in the active skin — a Win2000-era balloon in Win2000, Luna-styled under Luna — rather than imitating the Win11 toast. Accessibility: it must be announced, and dismissible from the keyboard; a notification only reachable by mouse is not reachable.
acceptance_criteria: An app calling Shell_NotifyIcon with NIF_INFO shows a skinned balloon anchored to its icon, auto-dismisses, and sends NIN_BALLOONUSERCLICK / NIN_BALLOONTIMEOUT back to the owner; keyboard-dismissible and announced to screen readers.

title: [spike] Do modern toasts survive without Explorer? (ShellExperienceHost is a separate process)
description:
Answer before any notification design work (parent bevel-7p9r): do Windows.UI.Notifications toasts still appear when Explorer is not the shell?

They are rendered by ShellExperienceHost.exe, a SEPARATE process from explorer.exe, so they plausibly survive a shell swap untouched. If they do, Bevel coexists with the platform toast surface and only owes the legacy balloons. If they do not, the notification epic grows by a whole modern-toast surface. The difference is large enough that guessing is not acceptable.

Cheap to measure, and the harness already exists: docs/spike/ shellspike exits Explorer cleanly via WM_USER+436 without a logout and restarts it afterwards. Extend it to raise a toast (a plain WinRT ToastNotificationManager local toast, or `New-BurntToastNotification` equivalent) while Explorer is down and observe whether it renders, whether it lands in the notification centre, and whether ShellExperienceHost is even still running.

Record the answer on bevel-7p9r either way — a negative result is as useful as a positive one, and the measurement is only valid per Windows build, so note the build number.

CAUTION from the first run of that spike: it restarted Explorer with Process.Start in a finally without waiting for the old shell to exit, which produced a WEDGED taskbar that needed all explorer processes killed and one started fresh. Fix that before reusing it.
acceptance_criteria: A measured, recorded answer on the parent epic for a named Windows build: whether toasts render and reach the notification centre with Explorer not running.

title: [epic] Windows shell mode: Bevel owns the notification surface (balloon tips, toasts, history)
description:
Once Bevel replaces Explorer on Windows, nothing else renders notifications. This is an epic rather than a task because it spans a mandatory protocol obligation, an open question about what survives without Explorer, and a genuine design quest.

WHY IT LANDS ON US. Owning Shell_TrayWnd is a contract, not just a privilege. Apps deliver balloon tips through the SAME WM_COPYDATA channel the bevel-2t7u spike proved we receive: NIM_INFO arrives alongside the NIM_ADD/NIM_MODIFY/NIM_DELETE we already measured. The shell is expected to draw them. Accept the tray and you have accepted the balloons.

THE THREE PIECES.
1. Legacy balloon tips (NIM_INFO) — MANDATORY the moment we own the tray. Not optional, not deferrable: an app calling Shell_NotifyIcon with NIF_INFO gets silence otherwise, which is a regression against both Explorer and every classic shell replacement.
2. Modern toasts (Windows.UI.Notifications / WinRT) — OPEN QUESTION. These are rendered by ShellExperienceHost.exe, which is a SEPARATE process from explorer.exe, so they may well survive a shell swap untouched. Cheap to answer and must be answered before any design work, because the answer decides whether we build a toast surface or merely coexist with one.
3. Notification centre / history — DESIGN QUEST. Win10 Action Center and Win11 notification centre keep history, group by app, and host quick actions. Bevel does not have to copy either; but it does have to decide what "a notification arrived while you were away" means in a Win2000-reimagined shell, which is a design question with no 1999 precedent (balloons were ephemeral and historyless).

ERA NOTE worth keeping: Win2000/XP balloon tips were pure Shell_NotifyIcon, ephemeral, no history, no centre. The notification CENTRE is a Win10-era invention. A shell whose north star is "Win2000 as if designed in 2026" has a real choice here rather than an obligation to clone Action Center.
acceptance_criteria: With Explorer replaced: apps sending NIM_INFO get a visible, dismissible balloon; the project has a measured answer on modern toasts; and notification history is designed and implemented in each theme's own voice.

title: Windows shell mode: Bevel-drawn input/language indicator (per-thread layout, follows foreground)
description:
Explorer draws the input/language indicator ("ENG / PLP" in the spike capture) itself; it is not a Shell_NotifyIcon client, so in shell-replacement mode it vanishes and Bevel must provide it (parent bevel-985s).

This one is not optional polish for this user: the machine in the spike runs English (United Kingdom) AND Polish (Programmers), and Explorer's own tooltip advertises Win+Space to switch. Losing the indicator on a multi-layout machine means losing the only visible answer to "which layout am I typing in", which is a daily-use regression, not a missing nicety.

Needs: a compact two/three-letter layout badge, a click list to switch layout, and live updates when the layout changes by any route (Win+Space, per-window layout, an app switching it).

Platform surface: GetKeyboardLayout for the foreground thread's layout — note layout is PER-THREAD on Windows, so the indicator must follow the FOREGROUND window rather than our own thread, which pairs with the WinEvent foreground hook the window manager already runs (bevel-ncfp.3). GetKeyboardLayoutList/LoadKeyboardLayout for the available set, and ActivateKeyboardLayout or a synthesized Win+Space to switch. Language names come from the LCID.

Accessibility: the badge must carry the full language name, not just the three-letter abbreviation a screen reader would spell out.
acceptance_criteria: With Explorer not running, the taskbar shows the active keyboard layout for the FOREGROUND window, updates on Win+Space and per-window layout changes, allows switching from a click, and exposes the full language name to screen readers.

title: Windows shell mode: Bevel-drawn volume indicator + flyout (Core Audio endpoint)
description:
Explorer draws the volume indicator itself; it is not a Shell_NotifyIcon client, so in shell-replacement mode it vanishes and Bevel must provide it (parent bevel-985s, measured in the bevel-2t7u spike).

Needs: a speaker glyph whose state reflects the default render endpoint (level, muted, no-device), a click flyout with a level slider and mute, and scroll-to-adjust on the glyph — the behaviours people actually use without opening Settings.

Platform surface: Core Audio — IMMDeviceEnumerator for the default eRender/eConsole endpoint, IAudioEndpointVolume for level/mute plus IAudioEndpointVolumeCallback for external changes (hardware keys, other apps) so the glyph tracks reality instead of only what we set. IMMNotificationClient for default-device changes, which is the case that makes a naive implementation go stale when headphones are plugged in. Bevel already has a working pattern for COM-on-a-dedicated-thread in WindowsShellStaThread.

Note the PAL already has WindowsAudio.cs for IAudioPlayback (sounds), which is a different concern — endpoint volume control is new surface, not an extension of it.

Accessibility: the glyph needs a name reporting the current level and mute state, and the slider must be keyboard-operable — the tray is reachable by keyboard (bevel-vk4n) and this must not be a mouse-only control.
acceptance_criteria: With Explorer not running, the taskbar shows a volume glyph tracking the default render endpoint including external changes and device switches; click opens a working level/mute flyout; scroll adjusts; keyboard and screen reader can operate it.

title: Windows shell mode: Bevel-drawn network indicator (NLM connectivity + WLAN signal)
description:
Explorer draws the network indicator itself; it is not a Shell_NotifyIcon client, so in shell-replacement mode it vanishes and Bevel must provide it (parent bevel-985s, measured in the bevel-2t7u spike).

Needs: a glyph distinguishing the states people actually act on — ethernet vs wi-fi, signal strength, connected-but-no-internet, disconnected — plus a tooltip naming the active connection (the spike captured Explorer's own as "Network ikari's net / Internet access", which is the shape to match) and a click action that opens the system network UI rather than reimplementing connection management.

Platform surface: INetworkListManager for connectivity level (this is what distinguishes "connected" from "has internet", the distinction a naive IsNetworkAvailable check misses), plus the WLAN API (WlanOpenHandle / WlanQueryInterface) for wi-fi signal strength and SSID. NLM fires connectivity-change events via INetworkEvents, so this should be event-driven rather than polled.

Deliberately NOT in scope: a full connect/disconnect/credentials UI. Opening the shell's own network flyout or Settings page is the honest first version; reimplementing wi-fi connection management is a separate decision and a much larger surface.

Accessibility: the glyph needs a name reporting connection type and state, like the tooltip.
acceptance_criteria: With Explorer not running, the taskbar shows a network glyph that distinguishes ethernet/wi-fi, signal strength, no-internet and disconnected, updates from NLM events, names the active connection, and opens the system network UI on click.

title: [epic] Windows shell mode: Bevel must draw the system tray indicators Explorer owns (network, volume, input, battery)
description:
Under shell-replacement mode Bevel owns the notification area, and the spike for bevel-2t7u measured exactly what that costs: of ~9 visible tray items, only 4 re-registered via Shell_NotifyIcon when we claimed Shell_TrayWnd and broadcast TaskbarCreated. The rest — Network, Volume, the input/language indicator, battery on laptops, and the action-centre affordance — are NOT Shell_NotifyIcon clients at all. They are Explorer's OWN taskbar UI, drawn by the shell process.

The consequence is structural, not cosmetic: the moment Bevel is the shell, those controls simply do not exist. There is no API to mirror them and nothing to forward a click to, because there is no foreign status item behind them. Bevel has to implement each one itself, the same way it already draws its own clock.

This is an epic because each item is its own platform surface with its own API family, its own flyout UI, and its own accessibility story — they share almost nothing except where they sit on the bar. Each child should be independently shippable so the tray fills in incrementally rather than landing as one slab.

Scope note: these are needed ONLY in shell-replacement mode. While Explorer's taskbar is running, its own indicators are still present on its bar, so this work is gated behind the same epic as bevel-2t7u and should not be started before shell replacement is a real target.
acceptance_criteria: In shell-replacement mode the taskbar presents working network, volume, input-language and battery indicators drawn by Bevel, each with its flyout and keyboard/screen-reader access, with no dependency on Explorer running.
notes:
SCOPE WIDENED: this is the superset of what the SHELL owns in the tray/clock area, not just four indicators — and it is a burden that is NEW to the Win10/11 era.

Era matters, and it is the reason this looks harder than the old shell-replacement lore suggests:
- Windows 2000 / XP: volume, network and battery were REAL Shell_NotifyIcon clients (systray.exe, sndvol32). A shell replacement that owned Shell_TrayWnd got them for free, which is why LiteStep-era shells never had to build them. The only genuinely shell-owned pieces were the clock, the XP "hide inactive icons" overflow, and the language bar (MSUTB).
- Windows 10 / 11: those same controls became shell-drawn XAML with no Shell_NotifyIcon registration. The spike for this bead measured it directly — 4 of ~9 visible items re-registered with us; the rest never arrive because they are not clients at all.

So the Win10/11 superset Bevel must own once it replaces Explorer:
  ALREADY HAVE: clock, tray overflow / hidden-icons chevron, show-desktop affordance.
  FILED AS CHILDREN: volume (.1), network (.2), input/language (.3), battery (.4).
  NOT YET FILED, and bigger than the indicators: the NOTIFICATION SYSTEM — see the separate epic.
  DESIGN DECISIONS, not yet beads: a clock CALENDAR flyout (Win10/11 expose one on click; Bevel's clock has only a tooltip); whether to follow Win11 in merging volume/network/brightness into one Quick Settings flyout or keep XP-style separate indicators; Focus Assist / do-not-disturb; touch-keyboard and pen affordances (tablet only, probably out of scope).

The decisive new fact is that owning Shell_TrayWnd is not only a RIGHT, it is a CONTRACT: apps send balloon tips through the very same WM_COPYDATA channel this bead's spike proved we receive. Accepting NIM_ADD means accepting NIM_INFO, and nothing else will draw those balloons once Explorer is gone. That is what turns "draw four indicators" into "own the notification surface".

title: [bug] SettingsServiceSqliteTests concurrency test fails only under full-suite parallel load
description:
Bevel.Core.Tests.SettingsServiceSqliteTests.Concurrent_readers_and_writers_never_hit_database_is_locked fails intermittently when the whole solution's test run is in flight, and passes every time the project is run on its own.

Observed on Windows 11 / .NET 10.0.401, 2026-10-01, across several full-suite runs in one session: dotnet test Bevel.sln reported it failed 3 times; dotnet test on just Bevel.Core.Tests passed it twice back to back immediately afterwards. The difference is CPU/IO contention from the other seven test assemblies running concurrently.

Why it matters beyond flake noise: the assertion is that concurrent readers and writers NEVER see "database is locked". If the only thing standing between that invariant and a failure is a quiet machine, then the busy/retry budget in SettingsService is tuned to an idle box and the same contention could hit a real shell on a loaded desktop — settings writes come from the core while peers read. So the first question is not "stabilise the test" but "is the busy timeout / retry policy actually sufficient", with the test tightened or the timeout raised accordingly.

Repro: dotnet test Bevel.sln (full parallel run) on a machine with other load; compare against dotnet test tests/Bevel.Core.Tests/Bevel.Core.Tests.csproj alone.

Not caused by the Windows taskbar work in this session — that touches no settings concurrency path (the only SettingsService change was the TaskbarStartLabel default).
acceptance_criteria: The concurrency test passes reliably in a full parallel solution run, and the fix is justified by the SQLite busy/retry policy being adequate under contention rather than by relaxing the assertion.

title: Luna theme is named after one of its own colourways (Bevel 2001 Blue)
description:
The Luna theme was listed as "Bevel 2001 Blue" in the theme picker, but blue is only its DEFAULT colourway — the Luna colour axis (Blue/Silver/Black/Purple, LunaVariant.Colors) is user-switchable, so the name contradicts the feature as soon as anyone switches. Renamed to "Bevel 2001" in ThemeService.Themes.

The id "luna" is the PERSISTED value and is untouched; only the display string changed, so no settings migration is needed.

Reported alongside: the Start button lacks a few pixels of right padding under this theme. That is handled in bevel-6x9z (the Start button now auto-sizes to its caption with a themed min-width and 8px horizontal padding) — but verify the Luna pill specifically once that lands, since its ControlTheme draws its own rounded face and may not honour the button Padding.
acceptance_criteria: The theme picker names the theme independently of its selected colourway; the persisted id is unchanged.
close_reason: Renamed to 'Bevel 2001' in ThemeService.Themes (4385a80); persisted id 'luna' untouched so no migration. The Start right-padding reported alongside is addressed by the bevel-6x9z padding/auto-size work and looks correct on the live Luna pill; reopen if it still reads tight in a specific colourway.

title: SiteShot 2x silently mis-renders animated content (task-button strip) — name the affected surfaces or auto-fall-back
description:
SiteShot.Save renders at 2x through RenderTargetBitmap, and content that forces an intermediate composition layer comes out wrong: the chrome renders at 1x while the content is magnified and clipped. SiteShot's own doc comment already records this for one landing-page shot ("the one that isn't passes scale: 1"), but does not say WHICH content triggers it, so the next person rediscovers it the hard way.

The taskbar strip is in the affected set, found while harvesting a Windows task-button shot for bevel-epsz: at the default 2x the strip rendered as one giant clipped glyph in the first button and five completely empty buttons, while the logical tree reported correct 32x32 Images with bound sources throughout. It reads exactly like an icon bug. scale: 1 renders it correctly.

Trigger is animated properties: TaskItemViewModel.Width and .Opacity are bound through template transitions, which forces the composition layer.

Wanted: either make SiteShot detect-and-warn (or fall back to scale 1) when a window subtree has active transitions/composition layers, or at minimum name the known-affected surfaces in its doc comment — task buttons included — so a 2x harvest of the taskbar is not silently wrong. Worth noting any site screenshot of the taskbar harvested at 2x today would be broken.
acceptance_criteria: Harvesting a taskbar shot at the default scale either renders correctly or fails loudly; SiteShot's guidance names the surfaces that force a composition layer.

title: Windows: packaged (UWP/AUMID) windows get a flat exe icon — resolve via AppsFolder IShellItemImageFactory instead
description:
Packaged (UWP/MSIX) windows get a flat, low-quality taskbar icon because their real artwork is not in the exe. Measured on a live desktop while fixing bevel-epsz:

- The Settings window (AUMID windows.immersivecontrolpanel_cw5n1h2txyewy!microsoft.windows.immersivecontrolpanel) publishes NO WM_GETICON icon and NO class icon, so WindowsWindowManager falls through to its exe backstop.
- PrivateExtractIcons on the hosted exe C:\Windows\ImmersiveControlPanel\SystemSettings.exe yields a 32px and 64px icon that is 0% transparent, corner alpha 255 — a flat square. That is genuinely all the exe carries.
- A packaged app keeps its visual identity in the package manifest (Application/VisualElements Square44x44Logo etc.) as scaled/targetsize PNG assets, not as an .ico resource in the exe.

Fix shape: resolve packaged apps through the shell instead of the exe. SHCreateItemInKnownFolder(FOLDERID_AppsFolder, ...) with the AUMID gives an IShellItem whose IShellItemImageFactory.GetImage(size, SIIGBF_*) returns the icon the native taskbar and Start menu show — correct for packaged AND classic apps, and it is the same mechanism the Start-menu icon path would want. Needs the shared STA COM thread (WindowsShellStaThread), so it belongs behind the existing off-thread icon path, not on the WinEvent pump.

Scope note: only the packaged-app source is wrong. Classic Win32 windows are fine (WM_GETICON, or PrivateExtractIcons at 64px) and must keep using the current path — do not route everything through the shell item without measuring, the AppsFolder parse is per-app COM work.
acceptance_criteria: A packaged app's taskbar button (e.g. Settings) shows the same icon the native Windows taskbar shows for it, at 64px source quality, verified on a real Windows box; classic Win32 windows keep their current icon source and no regression in enumeration latency.

title: [bug] Windows Start-menu icons ignore the .lnk icon index, so indexed-resource shortcuts show the wrong glyph
description:
WindowsAppEnvironment.ResolveShortcuts reads a Start-menu .lnk icon location with IShellLinkW.GetIconLocation(iconSb, cap, out _) and DISCARDS the icon index (src/Bevel.Pal.Windows/WindowsAppEnvironment.cs:283). The path alone then goes into InstalledApp.IconPath, and WindowsIconProvider resolves it with SHGetFileInfo, which hands back the FIRST icon in the file.

So any shortcut whose icon is an indexed resource — imageres.dll,15, shell32.dll,3, app.exe,2 — shows the wrong glyph in the Start menu rather than no glyph. Shortcuts pointing straight at an exe are unaffected, which is why most entries look right.

Fix shape: keep the index alongside the path (InstalledApp.IconPath cannot express it today) and resolve indexed icons with PrivateExtractIcons(path, index, edge, edge, ...) — WindowsWindowManager already does exactly that for its exe-icon backstop, and WindowsIconBits already converts the resulting HICON — instead of SHGetFileInfo.

Found while fixing bevel-epsz (missing Windows task-button icons); separate surface, separate defect.
acceptance_criteria: A Start-menu shortcut whose icon location is an indexed resource (e.g. imageres.dll,15) renders that exact icon, verified against the native Start menu on a real Windows box.

title: EPIC: per-Space / multi-monitor taskbars
description: User intent: listing other-Space windows may eventually want a taskbar per Space (or per display Space). Not the #5 toggle — architecture follow-on.

title: IPermissionBroker.PermissionChanged is declared but never raised anywhere -- dead live-update contract
description:
Part of the stale-value audit (design-gap finding, not yet a live bug -- but an attractive nuisance for the exact bug class this audit is hunting).

src/Bevel.Pal.Abstractions/Interfaces.cs:237 declares:
  event EventHandler<ShellPermission>? PermissionChanged;
Implemented (declared, NEVER invoked) in:
  src/Bevel.Pal.MacOS/MacOSPermissionBroker.cs:15
  src/Bevel.Pal.Fake/FakePal.cs:258
  src/Bevel.Pal.Windows/WindowsPal.cs:32
Grepped the whole repo: no `.Invoke(` call on this event exists anywhere.

Captured: n/a -- this is a promised push-notification contract with no producer.
Should: fire when Accessibility or Screen Recording grant state changes (the broker already re-checks both live and correctly, per this audit's TCC-permission pass -- MacOSPermissionBroker.GetStateAsync calls AXIsProcessTrusted()/CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess() fresh every call, so the DATA needed to raise this event is already computed on every poll, just never diffed+raised).
Does it: no.

Why this matters even though nothing is broken TODAY: the interface promises a live-update contract the platform never fulfills. The next feature built against "subscribe to PermissionChanged and react live" will ship with the EXACT "works after restart only" bug this whole audit is about, because the interface looks wired but isn't. OnboardingWindow currently self-heals correctly ONLY via its own poll (StartPermissionPoll, OnboardingWindow.axaml.cs:110) while its window stays open -- it does NOT use this event. Any future surface outside onboarding (e.g. the taskbar reacting to a grant given via the menu-bar pulsing-indicator flow rather than the onboarding dialog) has no live re-check today and would inherit this gap if it naively subscribed to PermissionChanged expecting it to fire.

Fix shape: either (a) wire GetStateAsync's existing poll to diff against last-known state and raise PermissionChanged on a real transition, giving the contract real teeth, or (b) remove the dead event from the interface until there's a producer. (a) is more useful long-term since it turns "poll while a dialog is open" into a reusable push signal other surfaces can build on. Needs a design decision on polling cadence/ownership -- left as a bead.

title: StacksViewModel reads TaskbarStacks once at construction, never subscribes to settings.Changed
description:
Part of the stale-value audit (parent theme: value captured once at startup, no live refresh path at all).

src/Bevel.Taskbar/Model/TaskbarViewModel.cs:40-41:
  Stacks = new StacksViewModel(settings?.Current.TaskbarStacks ?? Enumerable.Empty<string>(), appEnv, icons, thumbnails);

src/Bevel.Taskbar/Model/StackViewModel.cs:250-260 (StacksViewModel ctor): builds its Stacks collection ONCE from the folders passed in and never touches settings again. Grepped the whole src/ tree: TaskbarStacks (BevelSettings, persisted, has a merge-patch diff in SettingsService.cs) has exactly ONE C# read site in the entire app -- this constructor.

Captured: whatever settings.Current.TaskbarStacks was at TaskbarViewModel construction time.
Should refresh: on settings.Changed, the way TaskbarViewModel's own consolidation flag does (see the fix in this same audit pass, TaskbarViewModel.cs ApplyConsolidation/OnSettingsChanged).
Does it: no -- no subscription exists for this value anywhere.

Symptom: currently dormant because bevel-12g shipped without a UI to edit TaskbarStacks yet (folder scope was an open design point: "Downloads-only vs user-pinnable arbitrary folders/multiple stacks"). But TaskbarStacks IS a real persisted setting with a real default and diff path, reachable via the settings JSON / automation surface today. The moment any UI or automation verb writes a new TaskbarStacks value while the taskbar is running, the visible folder-stack list will not update until a full shell restart -- exactly the audited bug class, just currently unreachable from the UI.

Fix shape: subscribe to settings.Changed in TaskbarViewModel (or StacksViewModel itself, given a settings reference) and reconcile the Stacks collection to the new folder list, add/remove StackViewModel instances for folders that changed. Needs a small design decision on how a live remove interacts with an open flyout -- left as a bead.

title: AddressBar's folder icon uses hardcoded hex, not theme tokens
description:
src/Bevel.FileManager/Components/AddressBar.axaml draws its folder icon with Fill=#F0B84A / #FFD064 and Stroke=#9C6B15 literals. Every other folder glyph goes through Glyphs' FolderBack/FolderFront/FolderEdge brushes, which resolve ColorIconFolderBackTop/BackBottom/FrontTop/FrontBottom/Edge and pick up the Luna variant and Win2000 colour-scheme recolour engines. So the address bar's folder stays the same gold under every skin while the ones beside it recolour.

Noticed while fixing the back-panel geometry in c98431d, which replaced that file's transcribed path data with a binding to Glyphs.FolderBackGeometry/FolderFrontGeometry. The geometry is shared now; the brushes are not. Left alone deliberately: binding them changes the icon's appearance under themes, which is beyond the shape fix that commit was doing.

Fix: expose the brushes the same way the geometries are, or lift the whole icon into a small shared control so the address bar and the list glyph cannot drift again. Note Glyphs' brushes are static readonly and resolved once, so check they re-resolve on theme switch before reusing them from XAML — see [[luna-brushes-regenerated-by-variant]].

title: Centralise dlopen's path argument structurally, not by convention
description:
Frameworks holds every native library path and InteropConventionTests asserts every DllImport names one - but paths passed as ARGUMENTS to dlopen are invisible to that guard, and are centralised only by a comment asking future authors to be careful.

AppKitInterop.dlopen was made public specifically so LoginItemRegistrar could call it, and the duplication has already started: RTLD_LAZY is now a private const in BOTH AppKitInterop.cs and LoginItemRegistrar.cs - the exact per-file silo pattern bevel-uat set out to remove, reintroduced in the one place the guard is blind.

Fix: make dlopen private again and add Frameworks.Load(string frameworkPath, bool onlyIfAlreadyLoaded = false) as its sole caller, with the RTLD_* constants living there once. LoginItemRegistrar then calls Frameworks.Load(Frameworks.ServiceManagement). The convention becomes a type boundary - you cannot reach dlopen to hand it a literal - and a reflection-based guard could additionally assert dlopen's declaring type. Three call sites.
close_reason: dlopen is now private in Frameworks, its sole caller, with Load/IsLoaded as the API. RTLD_LAZY went from two file-local copies to one. The convention is a type boundary now: you cannot reach dlopen to hand it a literal.

title: Guard the P/Invoke convention by reflection instead of a regex over source
description:
tests/Bevel.Pal.MacOS.Tests/InteropConventionTests.cs asserts one-declaration-per-symbol and names-a-Frameworks-constant by regexing source text. That regex has already been wrong once: it required an explicit accessibility modifier, so it covered 80 of 98 declarations (C# defaults to private; the AppleEvent* files write a bare 'static extern') and hid two real cross-file duplicates - SendInt and SendNInt - behind a green test. Fixed by dropping the modifier requirement, but a text scan stays approximate: #if blocks, unusual formatting, a nested class, or a new subdirectory (EnumerateFiles is non-recursive) can all evade it.

Reflection over the built assembly is exact: Assembly.GetTypes() + MethodInfo.GetCustomAttribute<DllImportAttribute>() yields the resolved library string and entry point with no parsing.

Tradeoff to accept: reflection sees declaring TYPES, not files, so a duplicate inside the AppleEventInbound partial (spread across three files) collapses to one type. C# forbids identical signatures within one type, so only a same-name/different-signature pair could hide - a weaker harm than what is being guarded.

The real prize: it unlocks a rule the regex cannot express - every bool in a DllImport signature must carry an explicit [MarshalAs]. That is exactly the defect class fixed BY HAND in three places on this branch (AXIsProcessTrusted plus the two CG screen-capture gates each read a 4-byte Win32 BOOL over a 1-byte native Boolean), and nothing currently stops the next one. The tree has zero bare bools today, so the rule passes on landing.

Shape it as a [Theory] over targets so Bevel.Pal.Windows becomes one row rather than a copied class.

Verify first that DllImportAttribute and MarshalAsAttribute are reconstructed by GetCustomAttribute - they are pseudo-attributes stored in metadata (ImplMap), not ordinary custom attributes.
close_reason: Guard is now reflection over the built assembly: complete by construction (all 96 P/Invokes, verified DllImportAttribute/MarshalAsAttribute are reconstructed despite being metadata pseudo-attributes), keyed on (library, entry point, signature) so objc_msgSend's ~22 legitimate shapes pass while same-shape duplicates fail. Added the bare-bool marshalling rule the regex could not express. Shaped as a Theory over targets. It immediately found real duplicates the name-based regex missed: AppleEventInbound/Query had their own msgSend family shadowing AppKitInterop's (Send_nint and Send_ptr being the same signature under two names, since nint IS IntPtr) - 4 shapes deleted, 15 call sites repointed.

title: Bevel.Taskbar and Bevel.Desktop hold their own libobjc P/Invoke silos
description:
bevel-uat centralised macOS interop inside Bevel.Pal.MacOS, but 17 declarations remain outside it with hardcoded path literals: src/Bevel.Taskbar/TaskbarWindow.cs (13 - objc_getClass, sel_registerName, dlsym, nine objc_msgSend shapes) and src/Bevel.Desktop/DesktopWindow.cs (4). Four are name-for-name identical across the two files: sel_registerName, objc_msgSend_void_intptr_intptr, objc_msgSend_ret, objc_msgSend_bool_sel.

AppKitInterop already exposes the whole Send* family plus Sel(), GetClass() and EnsureAppKitLoaded(), and Frameworks now holds the two paths these spell as literals.

BLOCKER - decide the layering first: neither Bevel.Taskbar.csproj nor Bevel.Desktop.csproj references Bevel.Pal.MacOS (both reference only Bevel.UI, Bevel.Core, Bevel.Pal.Abstractions). Reuse needs either a new project reference or moving the ObjC primitives down into Bevel.Pal.Abstractions.

InteropConventionTests scans only Bevel.Pal.MacOS, so these will not be caught if they drift. Related: the Windows-side silo bead (bevel-p5bx).
close_reason: Layering resolved: both windows derive from BevelWindow in Bevel.UI, which already does macOS window work, so Bevel.UI hosts the shared primitives with no new project reference and no PAL inversion. Bevel.Desktop went 4 externs -> 0; Bevel.Taskbar 13 path literals -> 0; the 4 name-identical duplicates -> 1 each; two local selector caches -> one concurrent cache. The bounded two-layer overlap with AppKitInterop is documented in the file, with the leaf-project escalation named if it grows.

title: Share one repo-root locator across test and tool projects
description:
Four independent walk-ups from AppContext.BaseDirectory now look for a marker directory, with three different markers and three different failure modes:
  tests/Bevel.Taskbar.Tests/ProofModelTests.cs RepoRoot() - marker proofs/ - throws
  tests/Bevel.Pal.MacOS.Tests/InteropConventionTests.cs SourceDir() - marker src/Bevel.Pal.MacOS - Assert.NotNull
  tools/ThemeStudio/StudioWindow.cs FindRepoRoot() - marker Bevel.sln - returns null
  tools/ThemeGen/Program.cs FindRepoRoot() - marker Bevel.sln

Each behaves differently if the bin layout moves or a test binary runs outside the tree, and the newest one is the only one keyed to a PROJECT directory, so it breaks if Bevel.Pal.MacOS is renamed while the others keep working.

The fix is not a fifth helper: add an AssemblyMetadata item to the existing root Directory.Build.props whose value is MSBuildThisFileDirectory, and read it back via Assembly.GetEntryAssembly + GetCustomAttributes<AssemblyMetadataAttribute>. That deletes all four walkers rather than unifying them.

Found by /simplify on the interop-consolidation branch; not applied there because it touches three call sites outside that diff.
close_reason: One injected repo root (AssemblyMetadata from the root Directory.Build.props, gated on BevelNeedsRepoPaths) replaces four divergent walk-ups. No fallback by design. HelperProcessHost keeps its walker deliberately: it is shipped code locating a dev-build helper at runtime and must not depend on a build-time path, which is precisely why the metadata is gated to dev-time projects.

title: Windows P/Invoke has the same silo duplication macOS had
description: Bevel.Pal.Windows holds ~108 extern declarations across 7 files (WindowsWindowManager 41, WindowsDesktop 20, WindowsFileStack 19, WindowsAppEnvironment 17, WindowsShellSession 7, WindowsSystemTrayHost 3, WindowsAudio 1) with no shared interop class. Out of bevel-uat's scope but the same fix applies: one declaration per symbol in a class per module (user32/shell32/dwmapi/...), paths in one constants class, and extend InteropConventionTests to scan Bevel.Pal.Windows too. Measure the duplicate count first -- macOS was 18 symbols / 21 redundant declarations. Watch specifically for bare 'bool' returns: on macOS that turned out to be a real defect (4-byte Win32 BOOL over a 1-byte native Boolean) -- on Win32 a bare bool is CORRECT for BOOL, so the audit differs.

title: CFNumberCreate declares CFNumberType as int, but it is CFIndex (pointer-sized)
description: CoreFoundationInterop.CFNumberCreate declares 'int type' where CFNumberType is 'typedef CFIndex CFNumberType' -- pointer-sized. Passing 4 bytes where the callee reads 8 leaves the upper half undefined. It demonstrably works today (the thumbnail options dictionary builds and MacOSThumbnailProviderTests decode real images), which is why it was left alone during bevel-uat: unlike the nint/long and nuint/IntPtr swaps there (identical widths, provably no-ops), widening 4 to 8 is a real ABI change and there was no observed defect to justify bundling it into a consolidation commit. Fix: change to nint, verify the pixel-content tests still decode. Flagged in a comment in the file.

title: Migrate macOS P/Invoke to source-generated [LibraryImport]
description: Now that each symbol is declared once (bevel-uat), move Bevel.Pal.MacOS to [LibraryImport] for AOT/trim friendliness (AOT is a stated goal, bevel-gww). Held back from the consolidation deliberately: LibraryImport needs partial members and source-generated stubs and rejects non-blittable parameters without explicit config -- CFURLCreateFromFileSystemRepresentation's bool and the CF/AX Boolean returns are exactly that case -- so bundling it would have made a marshalling regression indistinguishable from a transcription error. Do it per interop class, with the thumbnail pixel-content tests and AccessibilityGateTests green after each. Current: 80 DllImport, 0 LibraryImport.

title: StartMenu.axaml.cs grew 38% absorbing the search UI — extract the search strip
description:
## Why

nuclear-pr-review finding (P2) on the 2026-09-23 bead batch. bevel-cezo's type-to-search correctly
extracted its pure logic to Model/StartMenuFilter.cs, but put all the view wiring inline: StartMenu.axaml.cs
went 543 -> 752 lines (+38%) and StartMenu.axaml gained 70 lines, in a file that was already one of the
busiest in the project.

The same diff contains the proof that a better shape was available: bevel-9elh moved the stack flyout into
its own StackFlyoutView.axaml(.cs) and referenced it with a one-liner, which SHRANK TaskbarView.axaml.cs
from 1141 to 1120 lines even though three other agents were adding to it concurrently.

## What

Extract the search strip (the classic sunken field + the Luna rounded field, their bindings, and the
key/text-input handler attachment) into its own view, leaving StartMenu.axaml.cs to host it. Keep
StartMenuFilter as-is; it is already correctly placed.

Note the constraint that shaped the current code: handlers must attach to the popup's OWN root panel and to
the inner Menu, because the menu lives in a Popup with its own TopLevel. Any extraction must preserve both
attachment points and their per-event de-duplication, or typing silently stops reaching the filter.

## Acceptance

- StartMenu.axaml.cs materially smaller; search markup in its own file
- Both attachment points preserved; StartMenuSearchTests still green including the handler-attachment test
- No behaviour change

title: Windows: mirror third-party notification-area icons into the tray
description:
User feedback 2026-09-12 after the first real Windows run: the tray shows no icons at all. This is BY DESIGN in v1, not a regression — WindowsSystemTrayHost.GetItemsAsync returns empty and the class documents the deferral (bevel-ncfp.4 spike, KTD-5): Bevel surfaces only its own status items and reports TrayCapability.Authoritative honestly, with no mirror source wired.

Two approaches are already analysed in that file:
1. Own Shell_TrayWnd — register a window with class name Shell_TrayWnd after TaskbarCreated so apps send their Shell_NotifyIcon (NIM_ADD/MODIFY/DELETE) traffic to us directly. Clean and event-driven; requires explorer's taskbar not running, i.e. real shell-replacement mode. PREFERRED: Bevel is a shell replacement, so this is the honest fit and needs no undocumented structures.
2. Cross-process TB_* enumeration — walk Shell_TrayWnd/ToolbarWindow32 (plus Win11's NotifyIconOverflowWindow, poll-only) reading the undocumented TBBUTTON/dwData layout via ReadProcessMemory in explorer's address space. Version- and bitness-sensitive; explicitly rejected for v1.

Note the tray settings page is now hidden on Windows (bevel-platsettings) because it is about consolidating a MIRRORED macOS menu bar; if approach 1 lands, Windows will need its own tray settings surface rather than reusing that one.
notes:
SPIKED AND NOT SHIPPED — all three approaches are now ruled out on Windows 11 except shell replacement. Measured on Win11 Pro 26300, 2026-10-01. Working mirror preserved at docs/spike/WindowsTrayMirror.cs.spike (UIA enumeration + PrintWindow glyph crop, ~330 lines, built and run against the live tray).

1. UIA over the notification area (the approach I built): the tray IS enumerable while Explorer's bar is normal — 9 items with names, tooltips, exact bounds and stable runtime ids. It is NOT enumerable once the bar is out of the way. SW_HIDE collapses the tree to a childless "Taskbar" root; AUTO-HIDE collapses it too, once the bar has actually slid away. A reading taken ~1s after setting auto-hide showed all 9 items and led me to believe auto-hide was safe — that was a transient, and with Bevel actually running the mirror returns 0 items, with the pointer at the bottom edge included. Explorer unloads the tray XAML when the bar is hidden.

2. Cross-process TB_* enumeration (the spike's approach 2): IMPOSSIBLE on Win11, not merely fragile. There is no toolbar left to read. Enumerating every child class under Shell_TrayWnd on this machine gives: MSTaskListWClass, MSTaskSwWClass, ReBarWindow32, Start, TrayDummySearchControl, TrayNotifyWnd, Windows.UI.Composition.DesktopWindowContentBridge, Windows.UI.Core.CoreWindow, Windows.UI.Input.InputSite.WindowClass. No SysPager, no ToolbarWindow32, no NotifyIconOverflowWindow. The TBBUTTON/dwData technique targets a Win10-and-earlier structure that no longer exists.

3. Own Shell_TrayWnd (the spike's approach 1): still the only viable path, and the earlier analysis holds — Shell_NotifyIcon resolves its target with FindWindow("Shell_TrayWnd", NULL), which Explorer's window wins while it merely sits hidden. So it needs Bevel to genuinely be the shell.

Conclusion: tray mirroring on Win11 is blocked on shell-replacement mode. It is not a standalone P2 feature; it should become a child of whatever epic covers being set as the shell, OR be scoped to Win10 (where approach 2's toolbar still exists) if that is ever a target.

Useful by-products worth keeping if this resumes:
- PrintWindow DOES render the Win11 XAML tray (verified: a 322x48 grab of TrayNotifyWnd showing every glyph), so a capture-based glyph source works and survives occlusion by Bevel's own topmost bar, where a screen read would not.
- Per-item glyphs crop cleanly from one grab using UIA bounds, with a soft colour key against the corner pixel for transparency — verified against both Win2000 grey and Luna blue.
- Do NOT source a mirrored glyph from the owning process's exe: UIA reports the HOST process, so on Win11 every status item claims explorer.exe and they all come out wearing Explorer's icon (measured: six items, six identical 5245-byte glyphs).
SPIKE RESULT 2026-10-01: approach 1 is PROVEN on Windows 11, and it can be tested without logging out.

Method (docs/spike/ shellspike, run on Win11 Pro 26300): ask Explorer to exit cleanly with WM_USER+436 (0x5B4) — the message behind the Ctrl+Shift+right-click "Exit Explorer" item; unlike a kill, Windows does NOT auto-restart it, and the session keeps running. Shell_TrayWnd then disappears, a plain window can RegisterClassEx("Shell_TrayWnd") (atom returned, window created), and broadcasting the registered TaskbarCreated message makes live apps re-add their icons to whoever owns the class now.

Measured in a 20s window: WM_COPYDATA=10, of which NIM_ADD=4, NIM_MODIFY=1, NIM_DELETE=3, with readable tooltips ("Not signed in" = OneDrive, "1 user connected"). So the full Shell_NotifyIcon lifecycle arrives, not just a first snapshot. Explorer restarted cleanly afterwards; work area and taskbar verified back to normal.

What this changes: bevel-2t7u is no longer blocked on an unknown. The tray is implementable the documented way — no UIA, no ReadProcessMemory, no undocumented TBBUTTON layout — PROVIDED Bevel runs as the shell (Explorer's taskbar not running). It should become a child of the shell-replacement epic rather than a standalone feature.

Two scoping facts for whoever picks it up:
1. Only ~4 of the ~9 visible tray items re-registered, and that is correct: Network, Volume, Clock and the input indicator are Explorer's OWN UI, not Shell_NotifyIcon clients. Under shell replacement Bevel mirrors third-party icons and must draw its own equivalents for the system ones — same as it already does for the clock.
2. Receiving the data is only half of it. The handler must parse SHELLTRAYDATA (dword unknown, dword message, NOTIFYICONDATA) properly — the spike's tooltip reader is a crude byte-scan and produced one garbled string ("Ҩ٨1 user connected"), which is a reminder that NOTIFYICONDATA layout varies by cbSize and must be read by version, not guessed. The hIcon in that struct is a cross-process handle, so the glyph needs CopyIcon/DrawIconEx in our process — the WindowsIconBits path from bevel-epsz already converts an HICON.

Superseded from the earlier note: the conclusion "blocked on shell-replacement mode" stands, but "unknown whether approach 1 works at all on Win11" is now answered — it does.
CORRECTION to the earlier note "PrintWindow DOES render the Win11 XAML tray, so a capture-based glyph source works and survives occlusion".

That is only true while Explorer's bar is still RENDERED. Re-tested 2026-10-01 with Bevel actually running (edge claimed, Explorer auto-hidden for a while): PrintWindow on TrayNotifyWnd returns an all-black 322x48 bitmap. Same root cause as the UIA tree going empty — Explorer unloads the tray's XAML content once the bar is hidden, so there is nothing left to render OR to enumerate.

So both non-shell approaches fail for the same reason, and the earlier successful capture was taken with Bevel NOT running. There is no mirror-from-the-outside path on Win11: the content only exists while Explorer is presenting its own bar, which is precisely when Bevel is not the shell. Shell replacement (approach 1, proven to work) is the only route.

Keep from the capture work: the crop-from-one-grab and soft colour-key technique is still the right shape for turning a raw glyph into a transparent tray bitmap IF a future source produces pixels. It just cannot source those pixels from a hidden Explorer.
SHIPS WITH bevel-7p9r.1, in the same release, not merely before it. The dependency edge runs claim -> balloons because you cannot receive NIM_INFO without owning Shell_TrayWnd first; but the claim must not reach users without balloon rendering, or every app calling Shell_NotifyIcon with NIF_INFO gets silence. That is a release-gating constraint, recorded here because a dep edge cannot express "neither ships alone". bevel-yli7's acceptance criteria cover both.

REPARENTED under bevel-yli7 (Windows shell replacement) on 2026-10-03: this bead had become the de-facto gate for two epics and seven children while still being titled as a tray-mirroring task. The root epic now carries the shell-replacement mechanics; this bead is scoped to the Shell_TrayWnd claim and WM_COPYDATA ingest specifically.

title: CI: Windows runtime smoke test (not just build)

High-risk (a bad shell key can lock the user out of a working desktop) — must be reversible + documented. Est: 2-3 days.

title: ISystemTrayHost (Windows notification area) — HIGH RISK spike
description: Mirroring third-party tray icons on Windows is genuinely hard: the notification area is owned by explorer's Shell_TrayWnd/ToolbarWindow32; consuming icons means either replacing the shell (become Progman/registered shell) or cross-process TB_ enumeration + icon extraction. Time-boxed spike to pick an approach BEFORE committing. May degrade to 'own-app tray only' for v1. Est: spike 2-3 days, then TBD.
close_reason: Implemented on feat/windows-pal-port (parallel subagents, integrated green: ~938 solution tests pass, Release clean under CI flags). Guarded P/Invoke; on-Windows runtime validation pending a box.

title: [design] Launcher self-update on RestartAll (version-stamped handshake, re-exec)
description: Fable: RestartAll respawns CHILDREN on the new inode but the supervising LAUNCHER stays on the old image until a full quit — old launcher + new children works until a launcher-control/supervisor-contract change breaks it silently. Fix: version-stamp the build into the control handshake; on RestartAll, if the on-disk binary version != running launcher version, the launcher re-execs ITSELF first (spawn new launcher, hand over the lock + children env, exit) — or simpler: RestartAll always escalates to 'spawn new launcher, old exits'. Also: RestartAll kills serially w/ 3s grace each (~6-9s blackout) -> kill parallel + bring taskbar back before core; coreReadyProbe is File.Exists (a stale socket satisfies it) -> probe connectability or drop it.

title: Automation channel: harden composite WindowRef bit-budget + pid-reuse edge
description: From bevel-uldj (v1-acceptable edges): (1) composite WindowRef packs (regId<<16)|localId — localId masked to 16 bits, regId<<16 overflows the sign bit at regId>=32768, so >65535 windows in one Explorer or >32767 distinct Explorer pids over the taskbar lifetime corrupt ids. Widen to long or recycle regIds. (2) pid-reuse before prune: if the OS reuses a crashed Explorer's exact pid before a dial prunes the stale _pidToReg mapping, an old composite ref could land on the new process's same-local-id window. Add a registration epoch/nonce per Explorer so a reused pid is distinguished. Both improbable; harden when convenient.

title: Startup: stagger the taskbar post-paint installed-app enumeration + icon rendering
description: Measured: after first paint the taskbar shows a 99-108% CPU sawtooth from t+2.5s to ~t+13s — ShellModel installed-app enumeration + icon-pool rendering + tray mirroring populating. The bar paints early but looks unpopulated and takes seconds to reach a steady state. Throttle/stagger this post-paint work so it settles faster and without the CPU sawtooth; confirm the taskbar icon path is pure read-only pool mmap and never blocks on a miss during startup.

title: feature Automation: taskbar->Filer channel for select/query-in-live-window verbs
description: Deferred from bevel-e7a7: with the automation socket on the taskbar, verbs that need a LIVE Explorer's per-process FileManagerWindowRegistry — bevelctl 'select' (in the frontmost existing window), 'query windows', 'query selection' — return ShellNotRunning/empty (the taskbar has no FM window registry; the core's ForeignWindowId projection is a different id space that can't map to the scripting WindowRef). Build a taskbar->Explorer control channel so the taskbar can forward these to a running Explorer process. Also: SpawningShellSurface.RevealAsync currently selects only items[0] on a multi-item reveal (FileManagerShellSurface selected all) — extend --select to multiple paths.
close_reason: Each Explorer hosts an ExplorerControlServer (nonce-auth UDS rendezvous); taskbar's SpawningShellSurface dials them via TaskbarExplorerControlClient — query aggregates (frontmost-first), select forwards via composite WindowRef ((regId<<16)|localId). Bounded 2s, off-UI-thread, dead-Explorer pruning, no-Explorer degrades cleanly. Router/WindowRef/security unchanged. Subteam+verifier SOUND, 7 tests, 844 green.

title: install-local.sh relaunch races the quit (_LSOpenURLsWithCompletionHandler error -600)
description: After the was-running relaunch, 'open' sometimes fails with LaunchServices error -600 (procNotFound) because the quit hasn't fully torn down the old instance / LS is mid-transition, leaving the shell DOWN. Add a short retry loop around the final 'open $DEST' (poll until a Bevel process appears, retry open a couple times with a small delay), or wait for the old PIDs to actually exit before opening.
close_reason: Relaunch now waits for the old instance to exit, then retries 'open' up to 5x until a process appears (warns if not) — no more -600 leaving the shell dead. Script-only, bash -n clean.

title: SettingsService: shared SQLite _connection used by ReloadIfChangedAsync without _writeLock
description: Surfaced (not introduced) during bevel-ha3x review: the single shared _connection is used by the write path under _writeLock and by the 750ms ReloadIfChangedAsync poll WITHOUT the lock. Microsoft.Data.Sqlite doesn't support concurrent commands on one connection; if the poll fires during a write's async window a collision is possible. Pre-existing (the old SaveAsync+file-write await had the same exposure); the CAS retry loop slightly lengthens the window. Fix: gate ReloadIfChangedAsync's read under _writeLock too, or give the poller its own read connection.
close_reason: Dissolved by bevel-6nve: peers no longer open settings.db at all (RemoteSettingsService is push-based over IPC), so the poller-vs-writer shared-connection race no longer exists. The core's single SettingsService still uses _writeLock, and with core the sole writer there is no concurrent-command contention.

title: SettingsService: optimistic-concurrency (CAS) write to stop concurrent edits clobbering
description: ce-code-review session E, adversarial P2 (advisory) — SPLIT OUT of bevel-lha4 (whose other four items are done). SettingsService is last-writer-wins over one JSON blob: SerializeRaw writes ALL of _settings, so if two surfaces (e.g. the Settings window + an Explorer window) save DIFFERENT keys between one process's Load and Save, one side's change is silently clobbered. Fix: make WriteRowAsync a compare-and-swap — UPDATE settings SET json=$json, version=version+1 WHERE id=1 AND version=$expected (pass the last-loaded _version); on 0 rows affected, reload the peer's blob, RE-APPLY this process's pending delta on top, and retry (bounded, then last-writer-wins fallback). Requires UpdateAsync to own the retry loop (it holds the Action<BevelSettings> delta to re-apply). CAUTION: load-bearing persistence path with migration/pruning subtleties (SerializeRaw/MigrateRaw/ApplyRaw) — needs careful testing incl. a two-instance concurrent-different-keys test. Deliberately deferred from the audit's mechanical pass as higher-risk for only advisory severity.
close_reason: Delta write paths (UpdateAsync/UpdateThemeOverridesAsync) now CAS-merge: bounded retry over 'UPDATE ... version=version+1 WHERE version=$expected RETURNING version'; on miss, reload+migrate+re-apply delta so different-key edits merge; LWW fallback on exhaustion; whole-blob SaveAsync (tests-only) stays LWW. Existing version column reused, no DDL. Subteam, both verifiers SOUND (confirmed new tests fail under LWW, pass under CAS). 796 green.

title: Taskbar: tray seed/stream ordering + StartMenu O(n^2) startup + All-Programs flyout rebuild
description: ce-code-review session C backlog (P2/P3, not applied). (1) TrayViewModel seed snapshot can resurrect a concurrently-removed item — buffer stream events behind a _seeding flag, apply snapshot, replay (adversarial P2, anchor 50). (2) ShellModel.RecomputeFrequent is O(n) per Programs.CollectionChanged and initial population inserts one-at-a-time → O(n^2 log n) on the UI thread at first Start-menu open (performance residual). (3) StartMenu 'All Programs' flyout Clear()+rebuilds every row on any Programs change, dropping scroll/hover — diff-in-place like ObservableReconciler (performance P3). (4) Testing gaps: consolidation reflow, WorkAreaMitigator strategy/capability gate, task-menu race guard, grouped TaskGroupViewModel menu branch (testing P2/P3).

title: Gecko tab engine: stable window identity, pid carry, URL enrichment
description:
Deferred MEDIUM/LOW findings from the bevel-osad Opus review (2026-08-17), all needing an AppTab shape change or session-store work:
1. WindowRef is a positional AXWindows index and AXWindows reorders on focus between menu-open and click; SelectTarget's title guard contains the blast radius but duplicate titles across windows are routine. Prefer a stable token (_AXUIElementGetWindow CGWindowID) or carry+match the window AXTitle.
2. PidFor re-resolves at activation; with multiple running instances (two Firefox profiles) enumeration and activation can hit different processes. Carry the pid captured at enumeration (AppTab has no field for it today).
3. Gecko rows have Url=null — Zen's AXTabButton exposes no URL anywhere (probed: AXHelp empty, no AXURL). Enrichment would come from the profile's sessionstore recovery.jsonlz4 (mozLz4) by title match; decoder proven in-session (scratchpad mozlz4_probe.py).

title: MacOSTabProvider: seam + tests for the osascript runner (timeout, kill, non-zero exit)
description: Review follow-up on bevel-a40b (Opus review 2026-08-17): RunOsaScriptAsync is a private static, so the three behaviors that protect the shell — the 4 s child timeout, Kill(entireProcessTree), and non-zero-exit → empty string — have no test that can fail. Extract the runner behind an internal seam (e.g. internal Func<string,CancellationToken,Task<string>> or internal virtual) defaulting to the current implementation, then add tests pointing it at /bin/sleep 10 (asserts timeout + child reaped) and at a script exiting non-zero (asserts empty). This also de-vacuouses Activate_refuses_invalid_refs off-macOS: with a recording seam the test can assert directly that no script was generated instead of inferring it from elapsed time.

title: Remove dead trayGlyphLayout sizing code + its test (native-size rendering replaced it)
description: bevel-7hf4 switched the mirrored tray to NATIVE per-item sizing (render at bounds points, no rescale). TrayServiceImpl.trayGlyphLayout + the TrayGlyphLayout struct + TrayServiceTests.testTrayGlyphSizing are now unused/dead. Remove them and the pngFromCGImage no longer references them.

title: Explore: tab-level previews (CDP opt-in / extension) + window hover thumbnails beside tab list
description: Background tabs have no pixels — no macOS API renders a non-active tab (SCK captures screen only; background tabs often have no process). Realistic paths: (a) ship window-level hover previews next to the tab list using the existing IWindowManager.CaptureWindowAsync (bevel-cust) — cheap, do first; (b) optional CDP integration for Chromium browsers launched with --remote-debugging-port (Page.captureScreenshot per tab) — power-user opt-in, needs browser relaunch; (c) WebExtension + native messaging bridge — also unlocks Firefox/Zen enumeration (see bevel-9w0h tail). Spike (a), spec (b)/(c) before committing.

title: Folders browsed INSIDE the Trash switch to file:// and regain normal caps
description: Navigating into a FOLDER within the Trash resolves via ResolveEffectivePath (non-null for leaves) → ToNavigablePath converts it to file://~/.Trash/folder, so its children show normal Rename/Trash caps instead of trash caps. Top-level trash items are correct (the common case: delete/empty). Low harm, but deleting a sub-item 'to trash' would nest-retrash it. Consider keeping sub-navigation in the trash:// namespace.

title: net:// Network tree node is a dead stub (silent no-op)
description: FileManagerWindow builds a 'Network' tree node tagged VfsPath.Root('net') but no 'net' provider is registered, so selecting it throws KeyNotFoundException (swallowed → nothing happens). Same crash-class as the Trash bug (bevel-sw3k) which is now fixed. Either register a stub NetworkProvider or hide the node until network browsing exists.

title: Luna render tests intermittently flake on shared headless Application state
description: Even serialized, RenderFileMenuBarTest.Render_luna_start_menu_under_purple_variant (and siblings) fail ~1/12 full-suite runs: the whole Bevel.Taskbar.Tests assembly shares ONE headless Avalonia Application + Skia surface (TestAppBuilder), and theme tests do not fully reset Application.Current between runs, so a render occasionally captures a null/incomplete frame. 55b121d reduced it (assembly serialization + settle/capture-retry) but did not eliminate it. Proper fix: reset Application.Current theme/variant/scheme state deterministically between theme tests, or give render tests an isolated app. Related: bevel-hd05 (closed), bevel-7qdi.

title: Settings store has no schema version / migration hook
description: SettingsService.cs:182 relies on one json blob, no migration, and prunes values equal to the code default (:256) so an improved default silently changes a users live behaviour on upgrade. Fix: add a schemaVersion key + migration hook and a default-drift escape hatch.

title: Luna ControlThemes have hardcoded hex that ignores the colour variant
description: Under Black/Purple/Silver these stay beige/grey: ProgressBar Background #F4F2E9 / Border #8A887A (LunaTheme.axaml:450), GroupBox frame #D0CDBF (:546), TabItem #D7D1BC and selected-tab gradient (:578,:599). Inactive-caption text stays light #E8EEF7 so Silver renders near-white on pale (LunaVariant.cs:215). And the static TaskButtonChecked (LunaTheme.axaml:99) is the visual opposite of the runtime override (LunaVariant.cs:108). title: Address bar is a plain textbox — no breadcrumbs/autocomplete/history

title: Flaky: parallel theme-mutating render tests collide on Application.Current.Resources
description: Bevel.Taskbar.Tests intermittently fails 1 test in a full 'dotnet test Bevel.sln' run but passes 202/202 when the project runs in isolation. Cause: several tests mutate global theme state (ThemeService.Apply / LunaVariantService.Apply/Clear / ColorSchemeService) against the shared Application.Current.Resources; xUnit runs test classes in parallel by default, so two theme-mutating tests can interleave. Fix options: put the theme-mutating render/guard tests in a single xUnit [Collection] (serialized), or snapshot+restore resources per test. Not blocking; purely a test-harness isolation issue.
close_reason: All 12 theme/resource-mutating test classes now share [Collection("TaskbarTheme")] so they serialize on Application.Current; Taskbar suite green 3x consecutively. Committed.

title: Intermittent: tray icons render too small (not reproduced)
description: User reported tray icons became 'too small' at least once; possibly correlated with screen-geometry changes, but NOT reproducible on demand (survived deliberate geometry changes in testing). Investigation found the code path intact end-to-end: live captures are 32px cells, CellHeight=min(30, IconSize*1.7)=27.2 at default IconSize 16, TrayRowsPanel preserves the explicit Height, settings resolve to 16. No code cause found; current runtime measures correct (27px). ARMED diagnostics (commit 4a6a323, gated on BEVEL_DEBUG_TASKBAR): timestamped logs of tray-icon decoded size + CellHeight, ApplyRowLayout rows/height/scaling, SetRows clamp/MaxRows, ScalingChanged/PositionChanged. NEXT RECURRENCE: run the shell with BEVEL_DEBUG_TASKBAR=1, capture stderr, and read the timeline at the moment icons shrink.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce or catch it via the armed diagnostics; identify the trigger (geometry/scaling/rows) and fix; or confirm non-issue.

title: Taskbar menu: true live Quit⇄Force-Quit swap via in-tree Popup
description: The app-centric taskbar menu (bevel-ww71) currently decides Quit vs Force Quit AT OPEN (Option held while right-clicking), because a live relabel while the MenuFlyout is open is impossible: the popup does not repaint after it settles (verified via content/TextBlock.Text/IsVisible probes) and the non-activating taskbar window gets no keyboard events + no modifier flags on pointer events. To get a TRUE live relabel (hold Option after opening → item swaps), re-host the menu as an in-tree Popup like the Start menu (StartMenu.axaml MenuPopup), which repaints live on property changes. Larger rewrite (lose MenuFlyout submenu/keyboard-nav conveniences). Native OptionKeyDown() poll already exists in TaskbarNative.
acceptance_criteria: Holding Option while the taskbar button menu is already open relabels Quit→Force Quit live and back on release.

title: Theme Studio: fold caption colour/height into Save
description:
The Theme Studio's 'Save to theme.json' persists Bevel.Metric.* and Bevel.Color.* but SKIPS the caption keys that live OUTSIDE the Bevel.* namespace — the vendored SystemColors caption colour/gradient/text and the WindowCaptionHeight (SystemParameters) key. It lists them as 'skipped' in the status. Persist them too.

SITE: tools/ThemeStudio/StudioWindow.cs Save() (the skipped branch for non-string keys) + PatchXaml to target the LunaTokens.axaml <Color x:Key="{x:Static common:SystemColors.ActiveCaptionColorKey}">... entries and the WindowCaptionHeightKey <x:Double>.
acceptance_criteria: Tuning caption colour/gradient/text or caption height in the Studio and hitting Save writes them into LunaTokens.axaml (no 'skipped' for those); reload shows them.

title: Luna menus: render mac ⌘-glyph accelerators (not "Cmd+X")
description:
The Luna MenuItem shows macOS shortcuts as text ("Cmd+X", "Return") via the shared KeyGestureConverter, but the design plate (docs/design/luna/preview.png) uses the ⌘ glyph and "Enter". Map menu accelerators to the mac glyphs (⌘ ⌥ ⌃ ⇧, Return, ⌫, etc.) under Luna.

SITE: LunaTheme.axaml Bevel.Theme.MenuItem -> PART_InputGestureText (KeyGesture converter). Likely a Luna-specific converter or a post-format on the existing one.
acceptance_criteria: Luna dropdown/context-menu accelerators read ⌘X / ⌘C / Enter etc., matching the plate; Win2000 keeps its text form.

title: Migrate drag-drop to Avalonia DataTransfer API (retire IDataObject)
description:
Avalonia 11.3 deprecated the IDataObject drag-drop model (CS0618). Migrate the file/taskbar DnD to the new DataTransfer API. Deprecation only — old API still works — so no urgency, but it should not rot.

SITES (from a warnings-un-suppressed Release build):
- src/Bevel.FileManager/Components/ItemView.axaml.cs: StartDragAsync (new DataObject + DragDrop.DoDragDrop), OnDragOver/OnDrop (e.Data.Contains(DataFormats.Files), e.Data.GetFiles(), e.Data.Get(FileDropPayload.DataFormat)).
- src/Bevel.Taskbar/TaskbarView.axaml.cs (~L320): new DataObject + DataFormats.Files + DragDrop.DoDragDrop.

API MAPPING:
- DataObject           -> DataTransfer / DataTransferItem
- DragDrop.DoDragDrop  -> DragDrop.DoDragDropAsync (now async)
- DataFormats.Files    -> DataFormat.File
- DragEventArgs.Data   -> DataTransfer (new read API)
- custom FileDropPayload.DataFormat -> DataFormat<T> equivalent (keep the internal cross-window payload working)
acceptance_criteria: Zero CS0618 drag-drop warnings in a Release build; file drag-drop verified LIVE in the file manager (item drag + folder/empty drop) and the taskbar stack drag (headless can't exercise real drag gestures).

title: Taskbar grouped-button jump-list: per-app custom actions (New window, etc.)
description: Follow-up to the grouped-app context menu (bevel-cust.ctxmenu). Grouped buttons now show an app-identified menu with Minimize/Restore/Close All. TRUE app-specific jump-list items — e.g. 'New Finder window' for the Bevel file manager, keyed on TaskGroupViewModel.AppId — need a launch/new-window surface (IShellSurface / FileManagerWindowFactory) threaded down to the group VM, which the taskbar VM doesn't currently hold. Add a small per-app action provider (AppId -> extra MenuItems) and wire the file-manager 'New window' first.

title: bevel:// implements only 2 of 8 automation verbs; 'set' unreachable from CLI/URL
description: ce-code-review (agent-native #1 & #3): BevelUrlParser.Parse handles only reveal/open; select/mkdir/delete/duplicate/move/query fall through to 'unknown bevel:// verb' though BevelVerb + AutomationCommandRouter support them all (bevelctl exposes them). And neither bevelctl nor bevel:// has a 'set' verb, so view-mode/sidebar/toolbar/bounds (AutomationProperty enumerates them) are unreachable from CLI/URL. Close the parity gap or document the intentional scope.

title: Cross-volume MoveDirectory orphans a partial copy if CopyDirectory fails midway
description: ce-code-review (reliability REL-5): LocalTrash.MoveDirectory's EXDEV fallback does CopyDirectory then Directory.Delete(source). If CopyDirectory throws partway (permissions, disk full), a partial tree is left at the destination and the source is NOT deleted — inconsistent state, no cleanup. Wrap the copy in try/catch that removes the partial destination before rethrowing.
close_reason: Cross-volume fallback now deletes the partial destination and keeps source intact on copy failure; tested via forced mid-copy collision. Committed.

title: Tray click-forwarding: custom status items unresponsive on macOS 26 (bevel-m3.3)
description: AX-press-first click-forwarding (533f189) opens the real menu for standard NSMenu status items on macOS 26. CGEvent synthesis is also ignored (Control Center hosts all items on macOS 26, FB18327911). Diagnostics: Control Center's AXExtrasMenuBar has ~51 children incl. off-screen/hidden ones, but on-screen positions don't align with CGWindowList bounds, so position-matching the real child failed. Investigate: (a) matching the AX child by identity/order rather than position, (b) whether these items respond to a real HID mouse sequence with the menu bar activated, (c) per-app quirks.
