title: Route taskbar window-icon PNG path (ShellModel.LoadWindowIcon) through the shared BGRA pool
description: gww.6 landed the pool behind IIconProvider (installed-app/Start-menu icons). ShellModel.LoadWindowIcon still decodes each ForeignWindow.IconPng (raw PNG over the wire) into an Avalonia Bitmap per-window, uncached — so N windows of the same app re-decode the same PNG. To route it through MmfBgraPool: derive a stable key (content hash of the PNG, since window icons have no path key), decode PNG->BGRA once, TryGet/TryAdd against the pool, and wrap the PalImage via PalImageBitmap.ToBitmap for the VM. Lower value than the IIconProvider path (window icons are per-window + transient) and touches the hot taskbar path, so split out of gww.6.
close_reason: ShellModel.LoadWindowIcon now dedupes window-icon PNG decode via an FNV-1a64 content-hash ConcurrentDictionary<long,Bitmap>: N windows of an app decode once and share one immutable bitmap. Deliberately an in-process cache, NOT the shared MMF pool — window icons are process-local + transient and the pool is single-writer (the split taskbar is a reader; writing there would be a second writer). Full MMF sharing would need the core to decode ForeignWindow.IconPng into the pool (split-mode-only benefit); deferred. Build green; 74 taskbar tests pass.

title: P6: MMF-backed shared BGRA icon pool behind IIconProvider
description: Replace MacOSIconProvider._cache with a memory-mapped (CreateFromFile, macOS has no /dev/shm -> runtime dir) store of (w,h,BGRA) slots keyed path|size; each process's PalImageBitmap.ToBitmap wraps a view into the MMF instead of a private byte[]. Route the currently-uncached taskbar PNG path (ShellModel.LoadWindowIcon) through the same pool. Note: ~0.5MB/proc at 16px today (memory win is small); real payoff is decode-cost/consistency now + readiness for large/Retina icons. Named MMF is Windows-only; cross-process notify via shell-core, not named sync primitives (process-local on Unix).
close_reason: MMF-backed shared BGRA icon pool wired behind IIconProvider via PooledIconProvider decorator (Bevel.UI): writer (All/Core role) renders each icon once + publishes to a memory-mapped file; reader roles (split taskbar/explorer/desktop) map the same file and serve without re-decoding; reader miss falls back to a private render without touching the shared file. Per-process writes serialized (pool is single-writer). Wired in CompositionRoot with 512-slot × 96×96 geometry co-located with the shell-core runtime dir. 3 PooledIconProviderTests (render-once, cross-instance reader-serve, reader-miss-fallback) + the pre-existing 9 MmfBgraPool tests green; full solution builds; 68 taskbar + 23 UI tests pass. Taskbar window-PNG dedup split into a follow-up (distinct hot-path optimization, lower value).

title: Backstop-caught window close reorders the exiting button to the strip end
description: Cosmetic edge from the bevel-wak reconciler fold. The COMMON close path (OnWindowClosed event -> Remove -> BeginExit on the single VM) animates the button out IN PLACE, unchanged. But when a Close event is MISSED and the 2s backstop Reconcile() catches it, the shared ObservableReconciler's onRemove defers the leaving item while phase-2 compaction moves survivors to slots 0..n-1, pushing the closing button to the end of the strip — so it shrinks at the end instead of in place, ~2s after the window is already gone. Rare (only on dropped Close events) and low-impact. Proper fix would need the reconciler to PIN deferred-leaving items at their slot so survivors flow around them; deferred as not worth the complexity/live-tuning now. Verify/adjust live.
close_reason: Fixed in ObservableReconciler. Rewrote Reconcile to build an explicit finalOrder list and diff the collection to it, instead of pruning then compacting survivors to slots 0..n-1. Deferred-leaving (pinned) items — those the onRemove hook kept in the collection — are spliced back into finalOrder at their original index (ascending inserts, clamped), so they HOLD their slot while animating out. The apply loop moves only genuinely out-of-position items, so an undisturbed strip with one button mid-exit raises ZERO moves — the closing button now shrinks in place on the backstop-caught path too, matching the event path and the old bespoke behavior. Immediate-remove (Programs, onRemove null) path unchanged: pinned is null → finalOrder == desired items → identical behavior. 2 new tests (middle item holds slot; deferred middle removal moves nothing); 43/43 taskbar tests green.

title: Redo Start-button Windows + Tux badges from PNG to SVG/vector
description: The Start-button OS badges for Windows and Tux currently ship as 512x512 PNG bitmaps (src/Bevel.Taskbar/Assets/StartBadge/windows.png, tux.png) loaded via avares in StartLogo.Raster(). The Apple mark is already self-drawn vector. Redo Windows + Tux as vector (SVG path data or hand-authored geometry like the Apple mark / Bevel.FileManager Glyphs) so all three badges are resolution-independent and asset-free, and the taskbar has no raster dependency.
design: Options: (a) hand-author path geometry in StartLogo (matches Apple + Glyphs idiom, no new package); (b) add an SVG rendering package (Avalonia.Svg / Svg.Skia — none referenced today) and ship .svg assets. Prefer (a) for the flag (simple, already had a good drawn version in git history); Tux is detailed, so either trace the PNG to path data or accept a stylized vector. Also resolve licensing: the current PNGs are downloaded third-party icons and likely need attribution — vectorizing our own removes that concern.
acceptance_criteria: Windows + Tux badges render as vector at any DPI; PNG assets removed from Assets/StartBadge; StartLogo.Raster()/bitmap cache gone; RenderStartLogoTest still renders all three; no third-party icon license obligation remains.
close_reason: Windows + Tux now ship as SVG assets parsed to Avalonia vector paths by StartLogo (resolution-independent, no raster). PNGs removed; Raster()/bitmap cache replaced by Svg()/SvgCache; RenderStartLogoTest renders all three; Flaticon PNG attribution obligation gone. Apple stays self-drawn per user. Dependency-free: a small <style>-class + path/polygon SVG-subset reader, no SVG package added.

title: App ignores SIGTERM: graceful-shutdown handler registered but process doesn't exit
description: Program.cs registers PosixSignalRegistration for SIGTERM/SIGINT -> App.RequestExit() -> Dispatcher.UIThread.Post(lifetime.Shutdown()). Observed during bevel-m2.13 work: kill (SIGTERM) leaves the app running; only kill -9 stops it. Pre-existing (not caused by the mitigator's Exit handler, which only cancels a CTS). Likely the classic desktop lifetime Shutdown() doesn't terminate the process while background loop tasks (window poll, mitigator) are alive, or RequestExit isn't reaching Shutdown. Repro: pgrep the app, kill <pid>, observe it survives. Fix: ensure Shutdown fully exits (or Environment.Exit fallback) so 'launchctl'/system logout can stop Bevel cleanly.
close_reason: Root cause: sync-over-async deadlock. After StartWithClassicDesktopLifetime returns, Avalonia's SynchronizationContext is still installed on the main thread; host.StopAsync().GetResult() blocked it, and StopAsync's await-continuation was posted back to that blocked thread -> hang (only kill -9 worked). Fix: run host.StopAsync via Task.Run (detached from the UI context) in Program.cs; root PosixSignalRegistrations with 'using'; ConfigureAwait(false) in HelperLifecycle.StopAsync. Verified: SIGTERM exits in ~1s with graceful cleanup (helper killed, no orphan).

title: AppKitInterop.NSStringCreate returns an autoreleased string but doc says 'caller must release' — callers over-free it
description: NSStringCreate uses +stringWithUTF8String:, which returns an AUTORELEASED NSString the caller does NOT own. The XML doc says 'Caller must release when done', and URLForApplicationWithBundleIdentifier follows that by calling release on it — an over-release / use-after-free that's a no-op for short/tagged strings but corrupts/crashes for real heap strings. Found while implementing MacOSIconProvider (bevel-m2.15), which hit an intermittent segfault from exactly this until it stopped releasing the string. Fix: either make NSStringCreate retain (so the contract holds) or drop the release in callers and rely on an autorelease pool. Audit all NSStringCreate callers.
notes: NOT STARTED (queued after bevel-d2z start-menu). Audit AppKitInterop.NSStringCreate over-release: it returns an AUTORELEASED string (+stringWithUTF8String:) but doc/callers may over-free. NOTE: MacOSIconProvider already documents this correctly (does NOT release nsPath); check URLForApplicationWithBundleIdentifier + other callers.
close_reason: Fixed in d941581

title: Reconcile spec metric/color discrepancies found by the Win2000 reference corpus
description: docs/reference/win2000/README.md 'Discrepancies vs specs' section (bevel-t97) flags several values where corpus evidence disagrees with 05-theming.md and win2000-explorer-chrome.md — most notably: (1) toolbar row height: win2000-explorer-chrome.md says ~26 DIP, 05-theming.md §8.4 says 22px — the two SPECS disagree with each other, and 2 independent corpus measurements both land near 22px, sided with 05-theming.md; (2) GradientInactiveTitle end color #C0C0C0 (05-theming.md) vs #B5B5B5 (win2000-explorer-chrome.md + corpus, 2 sources agree); (3) several quppa.net 'documented default' colors conflict with our pixel-measurement-backed values but the corpus itself sides with our specs in each case (selection highlight #0A246A vs #000080, menu face #D4D0C8 vs #C0C0C0, 3DDkShadow #404040 vs #000000) — worth a footnote/citation upgrade in 05-theming.md rather than a value change. Read the full section before editing; decide per-item whether to update theme.json/schemes.json (bevel-51t/bevel-c75 machinery) or just leave a citation.

title: Dispose per-tab FileOperationService on tab/window close (make Dispose mid-op safe)
description: CloseTab and window teardown never dispose the closed tab's FileOperationService (documented gap in FileManagerWindow.CloseTab; window factory has the same gap for the main controller). bevel-c8g now cancels the tab's in-flight ops via IFileOpHandle on close, but the service itself (progress Subject, VolumeQueueExecutor, undo stack) leaks. Naively disposing mid-op is unsafe today: a draining operation still calls EmitProgress, and OnNext on a disposed Subject throws, faulting the Completion task. Make FileOperationService.Dispose (or a DisposeAsync) safe while operations drain — e.g. complete/guard the subject, await in-flight completions after cancel — then dispose the service in CloseTab and OnClosed.
close_reason: Dispose now cancel-only for CTS ownership, OnCompleted for the subject, VolumeQueueExecutor no longer disposable; controller IDisposable wired into CloseTab/OnClosed, replacing InFlightOps tracking. 141/141 tests green.

title: Verify helper code signature / team-id before launch (defense-in-depth)
description: Follow-up to bevel-tyv, which closed the PATH-fallback and env-substitution vectors (SEC1) by requiring an absolute existing path. Needs the signing team-id (only BundleId=pl.ikari.bevel exists today) and a Release-only check (dev builds are unsigned), e.g. via 'codesign --verify' or SecStaticCode APIs. Gate off in DEBUG so unsigned dev builds still launch.

Wire each FileManagerWindow's file-op invocation to keep its IFileOpHandle so a window's Cancel button (and window-close mid-op) cancels only that window's operation. Removes reliance on the ambient externalCt path for multi-window scenarios.
close_reason: OperationRunner now hands the view the started op's IFileOpHandle; ProgressDialog cancels via the handle and filters progress by OperationId; tab/window close cancels only that tab's/window's in-flight ops. 137/137 tests green. Follow-up: bevel-70g (service disposal).

title: FileOp/VFS cleanup: double-resolve, duplicated type-desc, dead code
description: Cleanup batch from /code-review. (1) HandleConflictIfNeeded resolves the destination twice — DestinationExistsAsync ResolveAsync then again at FileOperationService.cs:~916 for Size/Modified; collapse to one ResolveAsync returning null-or-node. (2) LocalFsProvider.GetFileTypeDescription (~:212) is a byte-for-byte duplicate of GetTypeDesc (~:128); extract one shared helper. New FileOperationServiceTests + FileOperationServiceProviderTests (11 tests). Core 57/57, FileManager 20/20.

title: SearchPane content-search bypasses provider OpenReadAsync (file-scheme only)
description: Altitude finding. SearchPaneViewModel.cs:246 ContentMatchesAsync early-returns unless node.Path.Scheme=='file' and reads bytes via raw File.Exists/FileStream on node.Path.Value, bypassing the provider's OpenReadAsync that already abstracts reading any node's bytes. Content search is permanently blind to non-file providers (zip/net/trash) and assumes Path.Value is an OS path. Fix: read via the provider's OpenReadAsync so content search works for every scheme.
acceptance_criteria: Content search works for any provider implementing OpenReadAsync, not just file.
close_reason: Fixed + tested. SearchPaneViewModel: walk owns CTS lifetime (disposed only after the walk, never mid-use) + guarded Stop/Dispose (u0z); content search reads via provider OpenReadAsync for all schemes (5ya). ItemView.SortAsync: shared ApplyOrder detaches ItemsSource and never drops streamed late arrivals (rn9). New SearchPaneViewModelTests (4) + ItemViewSortTests (4). FileManager 28/28.

title: FileManagerWindow reimplements the tree + VfsRootLocator static global
description: Altitude finding. FileManagerWindow.axaml.cs:176 hand-rolls a second tree directly on TreeViewItem (placeholder sentinels, inline VFS enumeration, kind filtering) that duplicates TreePaneViewModel — but with no cancellation/off-thread handling, so slow-volume expansion blocks the UI thread. It relies on a process-global mutable static VfsRootLocator.Current (VfsRootLocator.cs) because the static expand handler can't capture instance state, which breaks with a second window/test. Fix: drive the tree through TreePaneViewModel (route VfsRoot via instance state) and delete VfsRootLocator.
acceptance_criteria: Tree uses TreePaneViewModel with cancellation/off-thread; no static VfsRoot global.
close_reason: Fixed core defect + tested. Tree expand/create handlers are now INSTANCE methods binding to the window's own _vfsRoot with a per-window _treeCts (cancellable); deleted the global mutable VfsRootLocator (broke with >1 window). Added OnClosed disposing _treeCts/_enumerateCts/watcher (also fixes the on-close CTS/watcher leak). Test: FileManagerWindowTreeTests proves two windows expand against their own roots. Full solution builds; FileManager 29/29.

title: VfsPath hardcodes '/' separator; duplicated vfs:// parsers
description: Altitude finding. VfsPath.Combine/ParentValue/FileName hardcode '/' while LocalFsProvider stores native OS paths in Value (breaks on Windows: Combine('C:\foo','bar')='C:\foo/bar'). There is no VfsPath.Parse, so call sites hand-roll vfs:// parsing two different ways (FileManagerWindow NavigateTo ~:244 via new Uri, SearchPaneViewModel.ParseLookInPath ~:274 via manual slicing) and will diverge. Fix: make VfsPath own canonical parsing/combination and normalize separators; route all vfs:// parsing through it.
acceptance_criteria: One canonical VfsPath parse/combine used everywhere; correct on mixed separators.
close_reason: Fixed with unit tests: VfsPath canonical parse/combine (VfsPathTests), enumerate TOCTOU guard + watcher dispose race + type-desc dedup (LocalFsProviderResilienceTests). Core 57/57 green.

title: Copy read-only-dest fallback writes to a read stream (NotSupportedException)
description: FileOperationService.cs:491-493 (CopyFileContentsAsync else branch): when GetMutatorAsync returns null (read-only destination) it opens destProvider.OpenReadAsync(destination) as the write target and calls readStream.CopyToAsync(writeStream) -> writing to a read-only stream throws NotSupportedException instead of a clean 'destination is read-only' error. Currently unreachable (only LocalFsProvider exists and always returns a mutator) but latent once a read-only provider lands. Fix: fail fast with a clear 'destination is read-only' error when the mutator is null.
acceptance_criteria: Copy to a read-only destination fails with a clear, correct error.
close_reason: Fixed + tested. FileOperationService: locked shared result/undo collections (w15), safe _cts lifecycle with gate+clear-before-dispose and CTS passed down to avoid cross-cancel (tbo), read-only dest fails fast (c7l), single destination resolve via TryResolveAsync (5ty, plus LocalFsProvider type-desc dedup/dead-code/delete-branch collapse). New FileOperationServiceTests + FileOperationServiceProviderTests (11 tests). Core 57/57, FileManager 20/20.

This is the foundation of the multi-theme system per 05-theming.md §11. Not an M0 bootstrap concern — sequence with theming work.

Follow-ups: bevel-51t (MET-01 codegen), bevel-sp5 (ENG-01 Classic template audit). Child bevel-38y.1 (smooth bevels) stays open. FM 148/148, UI 1/1.

title: SPIKE: bundle-id shadowing of com.apple.finder (documents failure mode; never ships)
SPIKE: tier-3 headless-Finder mirroring (measure window-escape rate)
Tablet/compact posture and touch-only components (deliberately deferred)
description:
Win11 collapses the taskbar in tablet posture (thin when not touched, expanded on swipe); Win10 had Tablet Mode; Win2000 had nothing. Also in this family: the touch keyboard button, pen menu and virtual touchpad toggles Windows shows only on touch/pen hardware.

Filed for completeness of the Win11 surface, at low priority and with a deliberate recommendation: Bevel should NOT chase tablet posture until there is a touch target to test on. The component model (bevel-aqr7) is what makes this cheap later — a compact presentation is a property of components and zones, not a second taskbar.

The one piece worth doing earlier is hardware-conditional VISIBILITY: components that only make sense with touch or pen hardware should be absent rather than dead, which is the same Capabilities feature-detect rule the PAL already uses.
acceptance_criteria: Components can declare hardware requirements and are absent where unmet; a compact posture is implemented only once touch hardware is available to test against.

title: Show-desktop corner component (+ the Aero Peek question)
description:
Hovering Win7–Win10's "show desktop" corner made every window transparent so the desktop showed through (Aero Peek), returning on mouse-out; Win11 kept the click-to-show-desktop corner but dropped the peek. Bevel has a Show Desktop verb (bevel-gdie) but no peek.

Parent bevel-aqr7: belongs to a show-desktop component, which also owns the Win11-style far-corner click target — currently Bevel exposes Show Desktop only from menus, so the corner affordance itself is missing too.

Feasibility differs sharply by platform and should be checked before promising it: Windows peek used DWM; doing it by setting every foreign window transparent is heavy-handed and risks leaving windows altered if the shell dies mid-peek — a failure mode this project has already been bitten by with the taskbar claim. macOS has no equivalent and should simply not offer it.
acceptance_criteria: A show-desktop component provides the far-corner click target; peek is implemented only if a check shows it can be done without leaving foreign windows altered when the shell exits unexpectedly.

title: Additional clocks / time zones (as a second clock instance)
description:
Win11/Win10 support additional clocks for other time zones (shown in the clock flyout and hover tooltip); Win2000 had the single clock plus the Date/Time control panel. Bevel's clock has format options already (24h, seconds, date) but one zone only.

As a component (parent bevel-aqr7) this is also the cleanest demonstration of multi-instance: a second clock for another time zone is literally a second instance with a different zone setting — no special "additional clocks" feature needed, which is the component model paying for itself.

Pairs with bevel-lbqg (clock calendar flyout), where additional zones are conventionally displayed.
acceptance_criteria: A user can place more than one clock with independent time-zone and format settings, demonstrating per-instance component settings.

title: Drag-and-drop onto task buttons (open-with, and hover-to-raise)
description:
Dropping a file on a Windows taskbar button opens it in that app (hover a button to raise its window, then drop into the window). Bevel's task buttons accept no drops, and its stack flyout already implements drag OUT (bevel-9elh) so the drag plumbing partly exists.

Two behaviours, both expected: drop ON a button to open the file with that app, and hover-to-raise so a user can drag into a buried window — the second is the one people rely on without noticing.

Parent bevel-aqr7: belongs to the window-strip and pinned-apps components, which should share one drop handler rather than each growing their own.
acceptance_criteria: Dropping a file on a task button opens it in that app; hovering a button during a drag raises its window so the user can drop into it.

title: [design] Per-indicator flyouts vs a combined Quick Settings panel
description:
Win11 collapses volume, network, bluetooth, brightness, battery saver, night light, accessibility, cast and nearby-share into one "Quick Settings" flyout opened from the tray corner; Win10 split them between Action Center quick actions and per-icon flyouts; Win2000/XP had neither — each indicator owned its own small menu.

This is a DESIGN DECISION that gates how bevel-985s.1/.2/.4 present themselves, so it should be decided before those are built rather than discovered afterwards: does Bevel give each indicator its own flyout (XP-ish, matches the era voice, simpler per component), or one combined panel (Win11-ish, fewer clicks for related settings, but a big bespoke surface that fights the component model)?

Component-model angle (parent bevel-aqr7): a combined panel is awkward precisely BECAUSE components are independent — it would need a shared host that reaches into several components' state. That is an argument for per-indicator flyouts plus, if wanted later, a panel that simply AGGREGATES component-provided tiles rather than reimplementing them.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded decision, taken before the indicator components are built, on whether indicators own individual flyouts or feed a combined panel — with the component-model implications stated.

title: Folder toolbars on the bar (the Win11 regression worth keeping)
description:
Win2000/XP/Win10 supported taskbar TOOLBARS: Address, Links, Desktop, and any folder the user dragged on — a strip of that folder's contents living on the bar. Win11 removed them entirely, which is one of its most-complained-about regressions, and is exactly the kind of thing a Win2000-reimagined shell should keep.

Bevel already has folder STACKS (bevel-12g/bevel-9elh) — a folder as a bar button with a flyout grid. A toolbar is the same data with a different presentation: items inline on the bar rather than behind a flyout, with an overflow chevron when they do not fit.

As a component (parent bevel-aqr7) this is the clearest case for multi-instance support: users had several toolbars at once, and the component model should make that natural instead of special-cased.

Related: the existing Quick Launch-ish behaviour and the stacks implementation should be reviewed for what can be shared rather than duplicated — same folder watcher, same icon pipeline, different layout.
acceptance_criteria: A folder can be added to the bar as an inline toolbar with overflow, multiple toolbars can coexist, and it shares the stacks implementation's folder watching and icon path rather than duplicating it.

title: Taskbar search component (box / icon / hidden)
description:
Win11 puts search on the taskbar (box, icon, or hidden — a user setting). Bevel has type-to-search INSIDE the Start menu (bevel-cezo) but nothing on the bar itself.

As a component (parent bevel-aqr7), with the display modes Win11 offers — full box / icon only / hidden — which falls out naturally once components have per-instance settings rather than a global bool.

Scope decision to make rather than assume: what it searches. Bevel's Start menu already searches installed programs; a bar search could be the same thing with a different entry point (cheap, coherent), or could reach files via the VFS (much larger, and overlaps the Filer's own search). Pick deliberately — the Win11 search box also pulls web results, which Bevel should not copy.
acceptance_criteria: A search component can be placed on the bar in box, icon or hidden mode per instance, opening a search surface whose scope is a recorded decision rather than an accident.

title: Task View component: window overview, and the virtual-desktop question
description:
Win11 has a Task View button (virtual desktops + window overview); Win10 the same; Win2000 had nothing comparable. As a bar component (parent bevel-aqr7) this is a button that opens a desktop/window switcher.

Two separable halves, and only the first is cheap:
1. A switcher UI Bevel draws itself over its own window model — it already enumerates every window with titles, icons and live previews (bevel-c04q's capture path), so an overview grid is mostly composition of parts that exist.
2. VIRTUAL DESKTOPS, which are a platform concept Bevel does not model at all. Windows exposes IVirtualDesktopManager (public, limited: query/move a window) while switching and enumerating desktops is undocumented COM that changes between builds — the same trap class as the tray TBBUTTON layout. macOS Spaces are already partly handled by the helper (SpaceContext, switchToSpace).
Do not promise desktop switching on Windows without first checking what is actually supported on the target build.

Honest first version: a window-overview switcher with no virtual-desktop awareness, which is useful on its own and platform-neutral.
acceptance_criteria: A bar component opens a window overview built from the existing window model and previews; any virtual-desktop capability is gated on a recorded check of what the platform actually supports.

title: Task-button progress indication (apps publishing progress to the shell)
description:
Windows apps report progress on their taskbar button (ITaskbarList3::SetProgressValue/SetProgressState) — a file copy, a download, a build — and the button fills with a progress tint. macOS apps do the equivalent on the Dock tile. Bevel shows nothing, so a long operation is invisible once its window is behind others.

Note this is the INBOUND direction and is distinct from Bevel's own progress dialogs: the shell must RECEIVE progress other apps publish. On Windows the values arrive per-window via the taskbar COM interface; reading other processes' progress requires owning the taskbar (shell-replacement mode) or hooking the same channel the tray claim uses — scope that before promising it.

Related and already filed: bevel-qb19 (attention/flash state) is the same family — an app asking the shell to represent something about itself on its button. Worth implementing the two together as "button state published by the app".
acceptance_criteria: An app reporting taskbar progress shows it on its Bevel task button in both skins, including indeterminate and error states, with the acquisition path documented per platform.

title: Clock calendar flyout (the clock currently has only a tooltip)
description:
Win10/11 open a calendar (and in Win11 the notification centre) when the clock is clicked; Bevel's clock has only a hover tooltip with the long date. Once Bevel is the shell, nothing else provides that surface either (related: bevel-985s superset, bevel-7p9r).

Smallest honest version: click the clock, get a month calendar in the active skin. Win2000 had no such flyout, but it had the Date/Time control panel — so a calendar reachable from the clock is a reasonable reimagining rather than a Win10 import, and it is the natural host if notification history (bevel-7p9r.3) ever lands.

Keep out of scope unless separately decided: agenda/appointments (needs a calendar data source), multiple time zones, and the Win11 habit of merging notifications into the same flyout.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking the taskbar clock opens a skin-native month calendar in both themes, keyboard-navigable and dismissible.

title: Notification history: design its Win2000/Luna interpretation (it gets built, not skipped)
description:
DESIGN QUEST, not a straightforward port (parent bevel-7p9r). Decide what "a notification arrived while you were away" means in a shell whose north star is Win2000 reimagined — then build it, or deliberately decide not to.

The honest starting point is that there is no 1999 precedent to reimagine. Win2000/XP balloon tips were ephemeral and historyless: miss one and it was gone. The notification CENTRE is a Win10-era invention (Action Center), carried into Win11 merged with the calendar flyout. So unlike the taskbar, the Start menu or the tray — where Bevel is reinterpreting something that existed — here Bevel is deciding whether a modern affordance belongs in the design language at all.

Three defensible outcomes, and the point of this bead is to pick one on purpose rather than by drift:
1. No history. Balloons stay ephemeral, exactly as 2000/XP. Most faithful; loses a genuinely useful modern capability, and users WILL miss notifications.
2. Quiet history. A small, skin-native log reachable from the clock or tray — closer to a Win2000 "event log" idiom than to Action Center's card stack. Keeps the era voice while fixing the miss-it-and-lose-it problem.
3. Full centre. Grouped-by-app cards with quick actions, i.e. reimplementing Action Center in the skin. Most capable, least era-faithful, by far the most work.

Blocked on bevel-7p9r.2 (the toast spike): if modern toasts keep rendering and keep landing in the platform notification centre without Explorer, option 1 becomes much more defensible because the platform already covers the history case — and option 3 becomes duplicated effort.

Design inputs when it is picked up: where it is summoned from (the clock is the Win10/11 convention and Bevel's clock currently has only a tooltip, so a calendar/notification flyout there is a natural home), whether quick actions belong in it at all, and how it reads in BOTH skins rather than being designed for one.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded, reasoned decision among no-history / quiet-history / full-centre, taken after the toast spike, with the chosen option either implemented in both skins or explicitly logged as deliberately omitted.
notes:
CORRECTION (user, 2026-10-01) — the earlier framing of this bead was wrong and is withdrawn.

It offered "no history, exactly as 2000/XP" as a defensible outcome and leaned on era-faithfulness to justify possibly shipping nothing. That is not the project's rule. "There is no 1999 precedent to reimagine" means only that there is no existing design to COPY; it never means there is less to build. The feature gets built, and we invent its interpretation in every theme.

So the question is NOT whether to have notification history. It is what history LOOKS like:
- in Win2000's voice — what would a 1999 designer have built for this, given the era's idioms (sunken panels, list views, the event-log lineage)?
- in Luna's voice — XP's softer chrome, which never had a notification centre either, so this is equally an invention.
- in Flat/Whistler's voice when that renderer exists.

Still blocked on bevel-7p9r.2 (the toast spike), but for a narrower reason than before: if the platform's own centre keeps working without Explorer, that changes what Bevel's history must CONTAIN (its own balloons only, versus everything), not whether it exists.

The real design work: where it is summoned from (the clock flyout, bevel-lbqg, is the natural host), how a missed notification is represented, grouping and dismissal, and how all of that reads in each skin rather than being designed once for one.
SHARPENED (user, 2026-10-01): the design bar is "the best a Windows 2000/Me designer would do" — and that era had real design chops, so this is a HIGH bar, not a licence to draw something flat and call it period-accurate.

Vocabulary that is genuinely of the era and available here: layered windows with true alpha (UpdateLayeredWindow shipped IN Windows 2000), fade and slide transitions for menus and tooltips, gradient title bars, menu shadows, hot-tracking, alpha-blended selection, smooth-scrolling lists — the Display Properties > Effects tab is effectively a list of the toolkit.

The decisive fact for THIS bead: balloon tips were themselves a Windows 2000 invention — Shell_NotifyIcon's NIF_INFO arrived in 2000, drawn as layered windows with alpha. So a notification surface is not an alien modern import being retrofitted; it is squarely inside the era's own vocabulary, and only the HISTORY/centre is the extension. That makes the Win2000 interpretation a question of "how would that team have presented a list of balloons you missed", with their own idioms to hand, rather than an invention from nothing.

title: Windows shell mode: Bevel-drawn battery indicator (hidden on desktops)
description:
Explorer draws the battery indicator itself; it is not a Shell_NotifyIcon client, so in shell-replacement mode it vanishes and Bevel must provide it (parent bevel-985s).

Lower priority than its siblings ONLY because the current dev machine is a desktop and the spike therefore never saw this item — on any laptop it is as load-bearing as the clock, and shipping a shell that cannot show remaining charge is not viable.

Needs: a charge glyph with charging/discharging state, remaining percentage, and the estimated-time tooltip; a low-battery state that is visually distinct rather than just a smaller fill.

Platform surface: GetSystemPowerStatus is enough for level/charging/estimated seconds. Power-state changes arrive via WM_POWERBROADCAST / PBT_APMPOWERSTATUSCHANGE, so the indicator should be event-driven with a slow poll as backstop (the broadcast is not always delivered promptly).

Hide-when-absent: desktops report BATTERY_FLAG_NO_SYSTEM_BATTERY and the indicator must then take no space at all, rather than rendering an empty or 100% glyph.
acceptance_criteria: On a battery-powered machine with Explorer not running, the taskbar shows charge level and charging state with an estimated-time tooltip and a distinct low state; on a machine with no battery the indicator occupies no space.

title: IPermissionBroker + IAudioPlayback on Windows
description: Windows has no TCC — IPermissionBroker reports granted (UAC elevation only where an action needs it). IAudioPlayback via winmm PlaySound/MessageBeep for system sounds. Small. Est: 1 day.
close_reason: U9 complete: IPermissionBroker=NotApplicable (no TCC on Windows), IAudioPlayback=real winmm PlaySound (guarded, muted/missing-path safe). Tests green.

title: Startup: replace ShellCoreEndpoint.ReadNonce 5s Thread.Sleep poll with async wait (latent hang)
description: Startup investigation exposed: ShellCoreEndpoint.ReadNonce() polls 50×100ms = 5s SYNCHRONOUS Thread.Sleep for the core.token file when BEVEL_CORE_TOKEN env is absent, then throws. Real explorers inherit the env token from the taskbar (fast path, instant), so this only bites a mis-launched process — but it's a latent 5s hang and it also gates a peer's first paint on a synchronous connect. Replace the Thread.Sleep loop with a bounded async wait; keep the env-token fast path. Also tightens the taskbar's brief defaults->re-theme flash. Related: the RemoteSettingsService first-connect race (already mitigated by early _server.Start() + reconnect-on-failed-first-connect).
notes: Re-examined: ReadNonce's env fast-path (BEVEL_CORE_TOKEN, inherited by every supervised peer) returns INSTANTLY — real boots never hit the 5s Thread.Sleep loop, which is a fallback only for a mis-launched standalone process. So this is NOT a startup-speed win; it's minor latent-hang robustness. A true async fix would need to thread async through the sync ShellCoreClient ctor / CreateClient — not worth the churn for a fallback path. Downgraded to P4; do only if the sync ctor is refactored for other reasons.

title: Second-source the WinDaisy-derived named color schemes (Brick, Desert, Eggplant, etc.) in schemes.json
description: schemes.json's 14 non-Standard schemes were extracted from the already-vendored Classic.Avalonia Colors/*.axaml files (bevel-c75), which per the new reference corpus (docs/reference/win2000/color-schemes-accessibility.md) trace to a modern hobbyist GitHub reconstruction (WinDaisy) rather than a period screenshot or registry export — single-sourced, not independently verified. Low priority: find a second source (registry .reg exports, period screenshots of each scheme in Display Properties) to confirm or correct before these ship as the W2K-01 scheme picker.

title: RTL: set FlowDirection from OS locale at startup + verify bevel light source vs RTL Win2000 references
description: bevel-3cd made the FM chrome honour the ambient FlowDirection (arrow keys, mirrored header, LTR-pinned path field), but nothing sets it: Avalonia does not derive FlowDirection from culture. Wire app startup to set the main windows' FlowDirection RightToLeft for RTL locales (he/ar), presumably behind a settings override. Open fidelity question needing public RTL Win2000 reference screenshots: whether the 3-D bevel light source mirrors under RTL (Win32 WS_EX_LAYOUTRTL mirrored DrawEdge output) or stays physical — decide, then make BevelBorder/ClassicBorderDecorator match.

title: Audit vendored SystemParameters tail vs spec metrics (MenuBarHeight 18 vs 19, caption metrics)
description: The shared scheme-file tail (now generated by ThemeGen from one template, bevel-c75) carries upstream's SystemParameters: MenuBarHeightKey=18 and WindowCaptionHeightKey=18, while spec 05-theming.md §3 says Win2000 MenuBarHeight=19 (CaptionHeight=18 matches). Bevel.Metric.* already carries the spec values; the vendored keys drive the Classic templates' menu bar/caption sizing. Verify against reference screenshots which is right for Win2000, reconcile the tail template in tools/ThemeGen (single line), and ideally derive the tail from theme.json metrics so the two systems can't disagree.
close_reason: Tail metrics now interpolated from theme.json (single source with Bevel.Metric.*); MenuBarHeight corrected 18→19 per spec §3 + SM_CYMENU; invariant test locks vendored SystemParameters == Bevel metrics. UI 10/10, FM 148/148.

title: Properties polish: real size-on-disk + recurse folders in multi-select size
description: Size on disk is a flat 4 KiB-cluster approximation (no per-volume cluster probe); multi-selection sums only top-level item sizes (folders in the selection are not recursed). Improve both if it matters.
close_reason: Properties actionable (rename+attr commit via IVfsMutator) + per-file cluster size-on-disk & multi-select folder recursion. Core 57/57, FM 125/125, rendered.

title: FM: remove dead SearchPaneViewModel + its tests
description: The rewritten SearchPane (bevel-aev) no longer uses SearchPaneViewModel; it and SearchPaneViewModelTests are now dead (still compile+pass). Verify nothing else references it, then delete both. Its content-search/look-in logic could be salvaged into SearchService first if wanted.
close_reason: Closed
